synopsis: In a future where science has cured aging and death, population-control law requires a volunteer to die for every birth; a father awaiting triplets confronts the bureaucracy of the euthanasia service.

title: 84, Charing Cross Road
author: Helene Hanff
synopsis: A twenty-year correspondence between a witty, book-hungry New York writer and the staff of a London antiquarian bookshop, sparked by her orders for out-of-print English classics and warmed over the years by parcels of rationed food sent in return.

title: Nine Stories
author: J. D. Salinger
synopsis: J. D. Salinger's only short story collection, gathering nine tales—including "A Perfect Day for Bananafish" and "For Esmé—with Love and Squalor"—that probe innocence, war trauma, and spiritual yearning beneath the polish of postwar American life.

title: Ajax Penumbra 1969
author: Robin Sloan
synopsis: A prequel novella to Mr. Penumbra's 24-Hour Bookstore: a young Ajax Penumbra arrives in 1969 San Francisco and takes a job at a strange, half-empty bookshop, drawn into the secret society of the Unbroken Spine and its search for a cipher devised by the real Renaissance printer Aldus Manutius.

title: Necessity
author: Jo Walton
synopsis: The final book of the Thessaly trilogy: decades after The Just City and The Philosopher Kings, the community has relocated across the galaxy to the planet Plato, where first contact with an alien civilization and the sudden death of the immortal Athene force the philosophers and their children to confront necessity itself.

title: The Maidens
author: Alex Michaelides
synopsis: A grieving group therapist investigates a series of ritualistic murders of students at Cambridge University, drawn into the orbit of a charismatic Classics professor and the secretive undergraduate society, the Maidens, obsessed with Greek tragedy.

title: Mr. President
author: Miguel Ángel Asturias
synopsis: A phantasmagoric portrait of an unnamed Latin American dictatorship, tracing a single week of terror and paranoia through the intertwined fates of a beggar, a general's daughter, and the tyrant's favorite, Angel Face. Written by future Nobel laureate Miguel Ángel Asturias, it is considered a foundational work of the Latin American dictator novel and magical realism.

title: The Library of Babel and Other Stories
author: Jorge Luis Borges
synopsis: A collection of Borges's metaphysical short fiction and essays — including the title story's infinite library of every possible book, an essay on the nature of Hell, and the labyrinthine parables "The Circular Ruins" and "The Babylonian Lottery."

title: Blue Nights
author: Joan Didion
synopsis: A memoir of aging, memory, and parenthood written in the aftermath of the death of Didion's daughter Quintana Roo, moving between Quintana's adoption, childhood, and wedding and Didion's own reckoning with mortality and failure as a mother.

title: Let Me Tell You What I Mean
author: Joan Didion
synopsis: A collection of twelve early Didion essays and pieces of journalism from 1968 to 2000, ranging from literary criticism of Hemingway to reflections on writing, self-doubt, and the craft of nonfiction, with a foreword by Hilton Als.

title: Play It as It Lays
author: Joan Didion
synopsis: A spare, fragmented novel following Maria Wyeth, a failed actress and model adrift in the freeways and vacant lots of 1960s Hollywood, as her marriage, an illegal abortion, and a friend's suicide push her toward emotional collapse.

title: Slouching Towards Bethlehem
author: Joan Didion
synopsis: Didion's first essay collection, anatomizing the countercultural unraveling of 1960s California — from Haight-Ashbury hippies and John Wayne to Joan Baez and a squalid Los Angeles murder — alongside personal essays like 'On Keeping a Notebook' and 'Goodbye to All That.'

title: South and West
author: Joan Didion
synopsis: A posthumously assembled pair of Didion's working notebooks: a 1970 road-trip diary through the Deep South's small towns and heat, and a shorter, unfinished 1976 notebook on California reckoning with the Patty Hearst trial.

title: The White Album
author: Joan Didion
synopsis: An essay collection capturing the fraying of late-1960s and 1970s California — the Manson murders, the Black Panthers, the Doors, shopping malls, and Didion's own migraines and breakdowns — as a portrait of a society coming apart.

title: Babel Tower
author: A. S. Byatt
synopsis: Set in 1960s Britain, the third novel of Byatt's Frederica Potter quartet follows Frederica through a bitter custody battle over her son while an obscenity trial unfolds around 'Babbletower,' a violent underground novel that echoes and comments on her own story.

title: Possession
author: A. S. Byatt
synopsis: Two contemporary literary scholars, Roland Michell and Maud Bailey, uncover a hidden love affair between two invented Victorian poets, Randolph Henry Ash and Christabel LaMotte, in a novel that interweaves modern academic detective work with the poets' own letters and verse.

title: The Djinn in the Nightingale's Eye
author: A. S. Byatt
synopsis: A collection of five fairy stories steeped in the Arabian Nights tradition; in the title novella, a narratology scholar at a conference in Istanbul frees a djinn from a bottle and is granted three wishes.

title: The Matisse Stories
author: A. S. Byatt
synopsis: Three loosely linked novellas — about a hairdresser, an art historian, and a childminder — each orbiting a painting by Henri Matisse and the way art reshapes ordinary lives.

title: Among Others
author: Jo Walton
synopsis: Told as a teenage diary, the novel follows Mori, a Welsh girl who can see fairies and has just used magic to stop her mother, a witch, at a terrible cost — now exiled to an English boarding school, she survives on a voracious diet of science fiction and fantasy novels.

title: Lent
author: Jo Walton
synopsis: A historical fantasy reimagining the life of the real Renaissance friar Girolamo Savonarola, who can see and banish demons in 1490s Florence — until he discovers he is trapped in a time loop, reliving his rise and execution again and again.

title: Franny and Zooey
author: J. D. Salinger
synopsis: Two connected novellas about the youngest members of the Glass family: Franny, having a spiritual crisis over a small book of Russian pilgrim prayers, and her brother Zooey, who tries to talk her back from the edge in a single long afternoon at their parents' apartment.

title: Mr. Penumbra's 24-Hour Bookstore
author: Robin Sloan
synopsis: An unemployed web designer takes a night-shift job at a strange San Francisco bookstore and is drawn into a secret society, the Unbroken Spine, obsessed with a five-hundred-year-old cipher devised by the real Renaissance printer Aldus Manutius.

title: The Sirens of Titan
author: Kurt Vonnegut
synopsis: The richest man in America, Malachi Constant, is swept into a cosmic scheme by the space-and-time-displaced Winston Niles Rumfoord, who reveals that all of human history has been secretly manipulated by an alien robot stranded on Saturn's moon Titan, waiting for a spare part.

title: I Have Some Questions for You
author: Rebecca Makkai
synopsis: A true-crime podcaster returns to teach a course at the elite boarding school she attended, where her roommate was murdered decades earlier, and finds herself reopening the case — and the question of whether the man convicted of the killing was guilty at all.

title: The Borrower
author: Rebecca Makkai
synopsis: A children's librarian discovers her favorite young patron has run away from his parents' anti-gay-conversion efforts and stowed away in her car; the two end up on an improvised, book-fueled road trip across America.

title: The Great Believers
author: Rebecca Makkai
synopsis: A dual-timeline novel moving between Chicago's art world during the devastating first years of the 1980s AIDS crisis and a mother's 2015 search through Paris for her estranged daughter, tracing how loss echoes across a generation.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
synopsis: A psychotherapist becomes obsessed with treating Alicia Berenson, a painter who shot her husband five times and has not spoken a single word since, and sets out to unravel why — and what her cryptic self-portrait titled 'Alcestis' really means.

title: If on a Winter's Night a Traveler
author: Italo Calvino
synopsis: A metafictional novel addressed to 'you, the Reader,' who keeps buying a book called If on a Winter's Night a Traveler only to find it interrupted after its opening chapter — again and again, across ten different invented novels-within-the-novel.

title: Invisible Cities
author: Italo Calvino
synopsis: Marco Polo describes fifty-five fantastical, impossible cities to the aging emperor Kublai Khan in a series of prose poems that are as much a meditation on memory, desire, and language as on any real city.

title: Alexander Hamilton
author: Ron Chernow
synopsis: A sweeping biography of Alexander Hamilton — from his illegitimate birth in the Caribbean through the Revolutionary War, the drafting of the Constitution and The Federalist Papers, his founding of the American financial system as Treasury Secretary, and his fatal duel with Aaron Burr.

title: Grant
author: Ron Chernow
synopsis: A biography of Ulysses S. Grant tracing his rise from failure and alcoholism to Union military genius in the Civil War and a presidency defined by his fierce, embattled defense of Reconstruction and Black civil rights.

title: Washington: A Life
author: Ron Chernow
synopsis: A comprehensive biography of George Washington, following him from surveyor and young officer through the Revolutionary War command and two terms as the first president, portraying the private uncertainties behind the marble-statue myth.

title: Team of Rivals
author: Doris Kearns Goodwin
synopsis: A group biography of Abraham Lincoln and the three rivals he defeated for the 1860 Republican nomination — Seward, Chase, and Bates — whom he then brought into his cabinet, and how that unlikely coalition steered the Union through the Civil War.

title: The Bully Pulpit
author: Doris Kearns Goodwin
synopsis: A joint biography of Theodore Roosevelt and William Howard Taft set against the rise of muckraking journalism at McClure's Magazine, tracing their friendship, political rupture, and the reform-era alliance between the presidency and the press.

title: Soldier of Arete
author: Gene Wolfe
synopsis: The second novel in Gene Wolfe's Latro series: an amnesiac mercenary who forgets everything each day and records his life on a scroll continues his wanderings through ancient Greece in the aftermath of the Persian Wars, guided by gods only he can see.

title: Soldier of the Mist
author: Gene Wolfe
synopsis: A mercenary named Latro, struck on the head at the Battle of Plataea, wakes each day with no memory of the day before and must reconstruct his life from a scroll he keeps — while seeing gods and spirits invisible to everyone else as he wanders through post-war Greece.

title: The Historian
author: Elizabeth Kostova
synopsis: A young woman discovers her father's hidden trove of letters hinting that the historical Dracula, Vlad the Impaler, still exists, and follows a decades-spanning trail of scholars, archives, and vampire lore across Cold War-era Europe to find him.

title: The Thirteenth Tale
author: Diane Setterfield
synopsis: A reclusive, dying novelist famous for a lifetime of invented backstories finally summons a bookseller's daughter to transcribe her true life story — a Gothic tale of twins, a burned house, and a governess that echoes Jane Eyre and Wuthering Heights.

title: The Library at Mount Char
author: Scott Hawkins
synopsis: A group of adopted children, raised by a god-like being called Father to each master a lethal discipline drawn from his cosmic Library, must work together to survive his disappearance and the collapse of the order he imposed on reality.

title: The Sense of an Ending
author: Julian Barnes
synopsis: A retired, comfortably unreflective man receives an unexpected bequest that forces him to reexamine his memory of a brilliant school friend's suicide decades earlier, and discovers how unreliable and self-serving his own account of the past has been.

title: The Storied Life of A. J. Fikry
author: Gabrielle Zevin
synopsis: A widowed, curmudgeonly independent bookseller on a small island finds his life transformed after an abandoned toddler is left in his store, forcing him back into connection with his customers, his community, and eventually love.

title: The Handmaid's Tale
author: Margaret Atwood
synopsis: In the totalitarian theocracy of Gilead, fertile women are stripped of their names and enslaved as 'Handmaids' to bear children for the ruling class; Offred narrates her constrained daily life and the fragments of resistance and memory that survive it.

title: An Unnecessary Woman
author: Rabih Alameddine
synopsis: Aaliya, a reclusive, divorced 72-year-old former bookseller in Beirut, has spent decades secretly translating great works of world literature into Arabic for no one but herself; over one Beirut winter she reflects on her life, literature, and the war-scarred city around her.

title: Hitch-22
author: Christopher Hitchens
synopsis: The memoir of essayist and polemicist Christopher Hitchens, tracing his English boyhood, his years as a Trotskyist journalist, his famous friendships and public feuds, and his ideological journey from the socialist left to a fierce, contrarian internationalism.

title: How to Be a Heroine
author: Samantha Ellis
synopsis: A memoir structured as a chapter-by-chapter rereading of the literary heroines Ellis grew up idolizing — Cathy Earnshaw, Jane Eyre, Scarlett O'Hara, Lizzy Bennet, Franny Glass, and more — and what they reveal about the life she's actually lived.

title: Matilda
author: Roald Dahl
synopsis: A brilliant, telekinetic five-year-old neglected by her crass parents finds an ally in her kind teacher Miss Honey and uses her wits — and eventually her powers — to take down the tyrannical headmistress Miss Trunchbull.

title: My Salinger Year
author: Joanna Rakoff
synopsis: A memoir of the year a young aspiring writer spent working at J. D. Salinger's staid literary agency in the 1990s, typing responses to his fan mail on a Selectric typewriter and slowly discovering both his novels and her own ambitions.

title: Just Kids
author: Patti Smith
synopsis: Patti Smith's memoir of her formative years in late-1960s and 1970s New York and her deep, enduring relationship with photographer Robert Mapplethorpe, from their poverty at the Chelsea Hotel to their emergence as artists.

title: The Anthropocene Reviewed
author: John Green
synopsis: A collection of personal essays reviewing facets of the human-centered planet — from Diet Dr Pepper and sunsets to the QWERTY keyboard and Halley's Comet — each rated on a five-star scale, adapted from Green's podcast of the same name.

title: The House of the Spirits
author: Isabel Allende
synopsis: A multigenerational, magical-realist saga of the Trueba family in an unnamed Latin American country, spanning from the clairvoyant Clara's girlhood through her granddaughter Alba's survival of a military coup and its aftermath.

title: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
author: Stephen Chbosky
synopsis: Told through a series of letters to an anonymous 'friend,' introverted freshman Charlie navigates his first year of high school, new friendships with seniors Sam and Patrick, first love, mental health struggles, and a repressed childhood trauma.

title: Flights
author: Olga Tokarczuk
synopsis: A fragmented novel-essay hybrid weaving together short fictional vignettes and essayistic digressions on travel, anatomy, and the preservation of the body — from a modern flight attendant to the real 17th-century anatomist Filip Verheyen and his amputated leg.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
synopsis: Stephen Hawking surveys the origin and fate of the universe — the Big Bang, black holes, and the nature of time — for readers with no background in physics.

title: Rob Roy
author: Walter Scott
synopsis: Frank Osbaldistone is sent to Scotland on family business and drawn into the Jacobite intrigues of the outlawed Highland clan chief Rob Roy MacGregor.

title: The Extraordinary Adventures of Arsène Lupin
author: Maurice Leblanc
synopsis: The gentleman-thief Arsène Lupin outwits police, rival criminals, and eventually Sherlock Holmes himself across a string of impossible heists and disappearances.

title: Thuvia, Maid of Mars
author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
synopsis: On a Mars scarred by ancient wars, Prince Carthoris of Helium pursues the vanished princess Thuvia, entangled with an army of phantom bowmen and the mysterious hormads of Lothar.

title: My Life
author: Richard Wagner
synopsis: Richard Wagner recounts his childhood, early theatrical failures, and the friendships and intellectual influences that shaped his development as a composer, up through his years in Dresden and exile.

title: The Blue Lagoon
author: H. De Vere Stacpoole
synopsis: Shipwrecked as small children with only an old sailor for a guardian, Dick and Emmeline grow up alone on a Pacific island and slowly discover love with no notion that they're doing anything unusual.

title: Henrietta Temple
author: Benjamin Disraeli
synopsis: The impoverished aristocrat Ferdinand Armine falls instantly and ruinously in love with Henrietta Temple, then must choose between that passion and the wealthy cousin his family depends on him to marry.

title: The Green Mummy
author: Fergus Hume
synopsis: An Egyptologist's murder over a stolen mummy case draws his fiancée's cousin into unraveling a conspiracy involving a cursed emerald and a vengeful priest.

title: The Ramayana
author: Valmiki
synopsis: Prince Rama is exiled to the forest with his wife Sita and brother Lakshmana; when the demon king Ravana abducts Sita, Rama wages war to win her back with the help of the monkey-god Hanuman.

title: Nana
author: Émile Zola
synopsis: Nana rises from the Paris stage to become one of the city's most sought-after courtesans, ruining a succession of lovers and husbands on her way to a horrifying end.

title: Thérèse Raquin
author: Émile Zola
synopsis: Thérèse and her lover Laurent murder her sickly husband to be together, only to find themselves haunted—literally and psychologically—by guilt that destroys them both.

title: Lorna Doone
author: R. D. Blackmore
synopsis: On Exmoor in the 1670s, John Ridd falls in love with Lorna, a young woman raised amid the outlaw Doone clan responsible for his father's murder, and must win her free of them.

title: Second Treatise of Government
author: John Locke
synopsis: John Locke grounds government in the consent of the governed, arguing that legitimate political power exists only to protect life, liberty, and property, and that a government which violates that trust can be justly overthrown.

title: The Interesting Narrative of Olaudah Equiano
author: Olaudah Equiano
synopsis: Kidnapped from West Africa as a child, Olaudah Equiano recounts his enslavement, the horrors of the Middle Passage, and his eventual path to freedom and abolitionist activism.

title: A Woman of No Importance
author: Oscar Wilde
synopsis: At a country house party, the caddish Lord Illingworth's plan to make an American puritan's son his secretary collides with a secret from Mrs. Arbuthnot's past that implicates them both.

title: News from Nowhere
author: William Morris
synopsis: William Guest falls asleep in industrial London and wakes in a socialist, money-free future where craft, beauty, and common ownership have replaced the machinery of capitalism.

title: Demons
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
synopsis: In a provincial Russian town, the nihilist Pyotr Verkhovensky manipulates a cell of radicals toward murder and chaos, while the brooding Nikolai Stavrogin's own moral emptiness draws them all toward catastrophe.

title: Wieland
author: Charles Brockden Brown
synopsis: In rural Pennsylvania, Clara Wieland's brother Theodore descends into fatal religious mania after a mysterious ventriloquist's voice convinces him he has received commands from God.

title: Rappaccini's Daughter
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
synopsis: Giovanni falls in love with Beatrice, the daughter of a scientist whose garden of poisonous plants has left her lethal to the touch of any ordinary being, and must decide whether he can love her without destroying her.

title: Miss Julie
author: August Strindberg
synopsis: On midsummer night, the aristocratic Julie seduces her father's valet Jean in a fevered, class-crossing encounter that ends in her ruin.

title: The Private Memoirs and Confessions of a Justified Sinner
author: James Hogg
synopsis: Robert Wringhim, convinced by a mysterious double named Gil-Martin that his Calvinist election frees him from moral law, is driven to murder his own brother and father in the name of predestined salvation.

title: Self-Reliance
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
synopsis: Ralph Waldo Emerson argues that conformity is the enemy of greatness, urging readers to trust their own instincts over the pressure of society, tradition, and even their own past consistency.

title: The Lair of the White Worm
author: Bram Stoker
synopsis: Adam Salton comes to his ancestral English estate and finds the beautiful Lady Arabella March harbors an ancient, monstrous secret rooted in a primordial worm-lair beneath the countryside.

title: The Canterville Ghost
author: Oscar Wilde
synopsis: When a brash American family moves into Canterville Chase, the resident ghost's centuries-old bag of tricks proves no match for their thoroughly modern skepticism.

title: Eve's Diary
author: Mark Twain
synopsis: Eve narrates her first days in Eden, discovering fire, the moon, and a large slow creature named Adam, in Twain's wry retelling of Genesis from her point of view.

title: The Lady with the Dog
author: Anton Chekhov
synopsis: Gurov, a jaded married man vacationing in Yalta, begins a fleeting affair with the melancholy Anna Sergeyevna that neither of them can walk away from once they return to their separate lives.

title: Ward No. 6
author: Anton Chekhov
synopsis: Dr. Andrei Yefimitch, the apathetic physician of a squalid provincial asylum, strikes up a philosophical friendship with a paranoid patient—until the hospital's petty tyrants decide the doctor himself belongs behind the ward's barred windows.

title: On the Eve
author: Ivan Turgenev
synopsis: In a quiet Russian household, the spirited Elena Stakhova falls in love with Insarov, a Bulgarian revolutionary preparing to fight for his homeland's freedom, and must choose between her family and his cause.

title: Smoke
author: Ivan Turgenev
synopsis: At a German spa town, the disillusioned Russian Litvinov is drawn back into a destructive love affair with the aristocratic Irina, even as he tries to build a stable future with his fiancée.

title: Virgin Soil
author: Ivan Turgenev
synopsis: Nezhdanov and his fellow idealistic revolutionaries attempt to stir peasant unrest in the Russian countryside, discovering how remote their radical convictions are from the people they hope to awaken.

title: The Wild Ass's Skin
author: Honoré de Balzac
synopsis: A ruined young Parisian finds a magic talisman that grants his every wish, but each granted wish shrinks the skin and consumes a portion of his remaining life.

title: La Bête Humaine
author: Émile Zola
synopsis: A hereditary compulsion toward violence stalks the railway engineer Jacques Lantier, whose murderous urges become entangled with a stationmaster's wife covering up her own crime.

title: The Necklace
author: Guy de Maupassant
synopsis: Mathilde Loisel borrows a diamond necklace for a ball, loses it, and spends ten years of poverty and toil to replace it—only to learn it was paste all along.

title: The Cask of Amontillado
author: Edgar Allan Poe
synopsis: Montresor lures his rival Fortunato into the catacombs with the promise of a rare cask of Amontillado sherry, walling him alive behind a fresh brick wall in revenge for an unnamed insult.

title: The Pit and the Pendulum
author: Edgar Allan Poe
synopsis: A prisoner of the Spanish Inquisition, condemned to death, wakes in darkness to find a bottomless pit at his feet and a razor-edged pendulum descending toward his chest.

title: Mrs. Dalloway
author: Virginia Woolf
synopsis: Over a single June day, Clarissa Dalloway prepares for a party in postwar London while shell-shocked veteran Septimus Smith spirals toward suicide, their lives brushing without ever meeting.

title: To the Lighthouse
author: Virginia Woolf
synopsis: The Ramsay family's summers on the Isle of Skye, and a promised trip to the lighthouse deferred by war and death, unfold through shifting streams of consciousness across a single decade.

title: Orlando
author: Virginia Woolf
synopsis: A nobleman who lives for centuries wakes one morning transformed into a woman, and drifts through four hundred years of English literary history. Woolf's genre-bending love letter to Vita Sackville-West.

title: An American Tragedy
author: Theodore Dreiser
synopsis: An ambitious young man's affair with a factory girl becomes an obstacle to the wealthy marriage he covets, and his half-formed plan to be rid of her ends in her drowning and his trial for murder.

title: The Sound and the Fury
author: William Faulkner
synopsis: The decline of the Compson family in Mississippi is told four times over, first through the fractured perceptions of the intellectually disabled Benjy, then through his brothers and a final omniscient turn.

title: As I Lay Dying
author: William Faulkner
synopsis: The Bundren family hauls their mother's coffin across a flooded, fire-threatened Mississippi countryside to bury her as she wished, the journey narrated in turns by fifteen shifting voices.

title: Elmer Gantry
author: Sinclair Lewis
synopsis: A charming, hard-drinking college football star talks his way into the ministry and rises through evangelical showmanship, hypocrisy, and scandal to the top of American religious life.

title: Arrowsmith
author: Sinclair Lewis
synopsis: An idealistic young doctor and researcher is pulled between the corrupting comforts of commercial medicine and the austere demands of real science, culminating in a plague epidemic that tests everything he believes.

title: A Passage to India
author: E. M. Forster
synopsis: A visit to the Marabar Caves ends in a false accusation of assault against an Indian doctor, exposing the racial suspicion and incomprehension underlying British rule.

title: Vile Bodies
author: Evelyn Waugh
synopsis: London's frivolous, party-hopping Bright Young Things chase gossip, money, and each other through a satirized interwar society hurtling toward catastrophe.

title: Point Counter Point
author: Aldous Huxley
synopsis: A large cast of London intellectuals, artists, and cranks pursue affairs, ideas, and betrayals in a novel structured like a fugue, contrapuntally cutting between their intersecting lives.

title: La Reine Margot
author: Alexandre Dumas
synopsis: Amid the massacre of Saint Bartholomew's Day, Queen Margot of Navarre navigates a French court riddled with poison, adultery, and religious slaughter.

title: Camille
author: Alexandre Dumas fils
synopsis: A Parisian courtesan gives up her wealthy lovers and dies of consumption for the sake of a devoted young man's family honor, in the novel that inspired La Traviata.

title: Pot-Bouille
author: Émile Zola
synopsis: Behind the respectable façade of a Paris apartment building, its bourgeois tenants scheme, adulterize, and exploit their servants in Zola's dissection of middle-class hypocrisy.

title: Au Bonheur des Dames
author: Émile Zola
synopsis: A vast Parisian department store swallows the small shopkeepers around it while a poor young shopgirl rises through its ranks and catches the eye of its ruthless owner.

title: The Belly of Paris
author: Émile Zola
synopsis: An escaped political prisoner returns to Paris and takes a job among the market stalls of Les Halles, where gossip and jealousy among the fat and comfortable threaten to betray him.

title: The Debacle
author: Émile Zola
synopsis: Two soldiers endure the catastrophic French defeat at Sedan and the chaos of the Paris Commune, in Zola's unsparing novel of the Franco-Prussian War.

title: Three Tales
author: Gustave Flaubert
synopsis: Three short stories — a servant's devoted, shrinking life, a legend of a bloodstained saint, and the beheading of John the Baptist — showcase Flaubert's precision across wildly different registers.

title: The Overcoat
author: Nikolai Gogol
synopsis: A downtrodden copying clerk scrapes together the money for a new overcoat, only to have it stolen the same night, with ghostly consequences. The story Russian realism is said to have crawled out from under.

title: The Gambler
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
synopsis: A young tutor's obsession with roulette and a capricious woman consumes him at a German spa town, in a novel Dostoevsky dictated at breakneck speed to pay off his own gambling debts.

title: The Cherry Orchard
author: Anton Chekhov
synopsis: An aristocratic family returns to their debt-ridden estate and refuses to face the sale of their beloved cherry orchard, even as the merchant who once served them prepares to buy it.

title: The Queen of Spades
author: Alexander Pushkin
synopsis: An obsessive young officer schemes to learn an old countess's secret formula for winning at cards, with fatal and then haunting consequences.

title: Ann Veronica
author: H. G. Wells
synopsis: A restless young woman defies her controlling father to attend a forbidden dance and pursue scientific study in London, then leaves home outright for an independent life of suffragette activism, romance, and self-invention.

title: The New Machiavelli
author: H. G. Wells
synopsis: A rising British politician's illicit love affair detonates his Parliamentary career, and in exile on the Italian Riviera he writes a bitter memoir of how desire wrecked his ambition to become a modern Machiavelli.

title: Clayhanger
author: Arnold Bennett
synopsis: Edwin Clayhanger leaves school dreading a confrontation with his formidable father Darius, a self-made printer in the industrial Five Towns, and is pressed into the family business just as his own ambitions begin to stir.

title: The Card
author: Arnold Bennett
synopsis: Denry Machin, an audacious young clerk in provincial Bursley, crashes a countess's ball and parlays the resulting fame into rent-collecting schemes, moneylending, and increasingly outrageous acts of generosity that make him the town's beloved rogue.

title: Elizabeth and Her German Garden
author: Elizabeth von Arnim
synopsis: An English wife chronicles a year of transforming a neglected estate in rural Germany into her private paradise, sparring wryly with an exasperated husband, eccentric visitors, and the crushing propriety of provincial society.

title: Right Ho, Jeeves
author: P. G. Wodehouse
synopsis: Bertie Wooster's meddling to pair up his shy friend Gussie Fink-Nottle with a sentimental young woman, and to patch up his cousin's broken engagement, spirals into drunken newt-fancier speeches and general chaos that only Jeeves can untangle.

title: The Inimitable Jeeves
author: P. G. Wodehouse
synopsis: Bertie Wooster's lovelorn friend Bingo Little falls for a fresh woman every few weeks, and Jeeves engineers one improbable rescue after another to keep Bingo's romances and Bertie's own entanglements from ending in disaster.

title: Psmith, Journalist
author: P. G. Wodehouse
synopsis: While an editor is away, the imperturbable Psmith and reporter Billy Windsor turn a genteel New York magazine into a crusading exposé of slum tenements, drawing threats from the gangster landlord profiting off the squalor.

title: Something Fresh
author: P. G. Wodehouse
synopsis: A struggling writer and a spirited young woman get swept into Blandings Castle's chaos when a bumbling young lord's old love letters, a stolen Egyptian scarab, and a houseful of scheming guests collide.

title: The Wrong Box
author: Robert Louis Stevenson and Lloyd Osbourne
synopsis: When his uncle dies in a railway accident, Morris Finsbury buries the body and schemes to hide the death and claim a lucrative tontine, but the wrong corpse ends up shipped to London in a packing case, touching off a farce of mistaken identity.

title: The Waste Land
author: T. S. Eliot
synopsis: A fractured, five-part modernist poem moves through a spiritually barren postwar landscape — tarot readings, a sterile Thames, a drowned sailor — toward a closing invocation of Hindu wisdom and peace.

title: Death Comes for the Archbishop
author: Willa Cather
synopsis: A French priest is appointed the first bishop of the New Mexico territory and spends decades building the church across a vast, unforgiving frontier alongside his devoted friend and fellow missionary.

title: A Lost Lady
author: Willa Cather
synopsis: A young man's idolatry of a charming railroad captain's wife curdles into disillusionment as her husband's fortune collapses and her secret affairs come to light.

title: The Professor's House
author: Willa Cather
synopsis: A historian nearing retirement retreats into his cramped old study, unable to let go of his life's work or the memory of a brilliant former student whose invention has enriched — and unsettled — his family.

title: Discourse on Method
author: René Descartes
synopsis: Descartes recounts abandoning inherited learning for a systematic method of doubt, arriving at his own existence as the one certainty from which reason can rebuild all knowledge.

title: Barrack-Room Ballads
author: Rudyard Kipling
synopsis: Dialect verses give voice to the ordinary British soldier's swagger, homesickness, and fatalism across the far-flung outposts of empire.

title: Stalky & Co.
author: Rudyard Kipling
synopsis: Three cunning English schoolboys scheme, prank, and outmaneuver their masters at a seaside boarding school, turning every punishment into an opportunity for the next plot.

title: The Golden Bowl
author: Henry James
synopsis: An Italian prince's marriage to a wealthy American heiress is complicated by the arrival of her father's new wife, a woman from the prince's own past, in James's intricate late study of marriage and betrayal.

title: The Awkward Age
author: Henry James
synopsis: A young woman's coming-of-age forces her mother's sophisticated London drawing-room circle to confront how much of their frank talk a girl on the edge of adulthood should be allowed to hear.

title: The Sacred Fount
author: Henry James
synopsis: A house-party guest becomes obsessed with a theory that one lover can secretly drain another's youth and wit, and pursues the idea past all evidence and reason.

title: Civil Disobedience
author: Henry David Thoreau
synopsis: Thoreau argues that individual conscience outranks civil law, and defends his refusal to pay taxes to a government that upholds slavery and wages an unjust war.

title: Swann's Way
author: Marcel Proust
synopsis: A sleepless man's memory of a childhood bedtime kiss unfolds into a vast recollection of Combray, and of Swann's own tormented, jealous love for the courtesan Odette. The opening volume of In Search of Lost Time.

title: Within a Budding Grove
author: Marcel Proust
synopsis: The narrator's adolescent infatuations — with the actress Berma on stage, with the diplomat Norpois, and with a band of girls on the beach at Balbec, above all the elusive Albertine — teach him how desire outruns its objects.

title: The Guermantes Way
author: Marcel Proust
synopsis: Fascinated by the aristocratic Guermantes family, the narrator pursues an entrée into their salons even as his grandmother's health fails and his friend Saint-Loup's engagement collapses under the weight of high society's cruelty.

title: The House of the Dead
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
synopsis: A political prisoner recounts four years of Siberian penal servitude — the barracks, the floggings, the strange dignity and cruelty of his fellow convicts — in Dostoevsky's fictionalized account of his own imprisonment.

title: Poor Folk
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
synopsis: An aging copying clerk and a young seamstress, distant relations living across a St. Petersburg courtyard from each other, sustain a tender epistolary friendship that poverty and a wealthy suitor slowly pull apart.

title: The Torrents of Spring
author: Ivan Turgenev
synopsis: A young Russian traveling through Frankfurt falls suddenly for an Italian confectioner's sister and gets engaged, only to be seduced away from her by the magnetic, manipulative wife of an old schoolfriend.

title: The Diary of a Superfluous Man
author: Ivan Turgenev
synopsis: A dying provincial nobleman, looking back over a wasted life, records in his diary the one humiliating unrequited love that defined him as permanently unnecessary to the world.

title: A House of Gentlefolk
author: Ivan Turgenev
synopsis: Believing himself free after his estranged wife's death abroad, Lavretsky falls in love with the devout young Liza, only for his wife to reappear alive, forcing a quiet renunciation on them both.

title: Anna of the Five Towns
author: Arnold Bennett
synopsis: A miserly Staffordshire manufacturer's dutiful daughter comes into an unexpected fortune, but finds herself unable to break free of her father's control or choose between two very different suitors.

title: The Sea Lady
author: H. G. Wells
synopsis: A mermaid comes ashore at an English seaside resort, is passed off as a shipwrecked lady, and quietly seduces an ambitious young politician away from his sensible fiancée and his entire mundane world.

title: In the Days of the Comet
author: H. G. Wells
synopsis: A jealous young man sets out to murder his rival, but a comet's strange green gas transforms the atmosphere overnight, dissolving greed and violence and ushering in a rational socialist utopia.

title: Lyrical Ballads
author: William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor Coleridge
synopsis: The founding volume of English Romanticism, pairing Wordsworth's plain-spoken poems of rustic life with Coleridge's supernatural Rime of the Ancient Mariner.

title: Adonais
author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
synopsis: Shelley's elegy for the young poet John Keats, mourning his early death and consoling itself with the vision of Keats's spirit absorbed back into the eternal beauty of nature.

title: The Hunting of the Snark
author: Lewis Carroll
synopsis: A crew of oddly named adventurers — a Baker, a Butcher, a Banker, a Beaver — sail off to hunt the elusive Snark, in Carroll's nonsense epic that ends on a suddenly dark note.

title: Crito
author: Plato
synopsis: Awaiting execution in his Athens prison cell, Socrates refuses his wealthy friend Crito's offer of an escape, arguing that a citizen who has enjoyed a state's laws his whole life has no right to break them now.

title: Gorgias
author: Plato
synopsis: Socrates corners the celebrated rhetorician Gorgias and his followers into admitting that oratory divorced from justice is mere flattery, and that suffering wrong is better than committing it.

title: In Search of the Castaways
author: Jules Verne
synopsis: A water-damaged message found in a shark leads Lord Glenarvan's expedition around the entire 37th parallel — through the Andes, the Argentine pampas, and the Australian bush — hunting a shipwrecked captain.

title: Bhagavad Gita
author: Anonymous
synopsis: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna's crisis of conscience over killing his own kinsmen prompts the god Krishna to expound duty, the soul's immortality, and paths to liberation.

title: Tao Te Ching
author: Laozi
synopsis: Eighty-one terse verses on the Tao teach effortless action, humility, and rule through non-interference rather than force.

title: Antigone
author: Sophocles
synopsis: Defying King Creon's decree that her rebel brother Polynices lie unburied, Antigone buries him and is sealed alive in a tomb, setting off a chain of suicides that breaks Creon's house.

title: The Persians
author: Aeschylus
synopsis: At the Persian court, news arrives of Xerxes' catastrophic naval defeat at Salamis, and the ghost of the dead king Darius rises to warn against the hubris that caused it.

title: Meno
author: Plato
synopsis: Meno asks Socrates whether virtue can be taught; Socrates instead demonstrates, by walking an untutored slave boy through a geometry problem, that learning is really recollection of truths the soul already holds.

title: The Romance of Tristan and Iseult
author: Joseph Bédier
synopsis: Tristan wins the Irish princess Iseult as a bride for his uncle King Mark, but a love potion drunk by accident binds the two of them instead, dooming them to a secret passion that ends only in death.

title: Dick Sand: A Captain at Fifteen
author: Jules Verne
synopsis: When a whaling ship's officers are lost at sea, its fifteen-year-old apprentice takes command, only for a treacherous cook to secretly steer them off course into captivity in equatorial Africa.

title: The Analects
author: Confucius
synopsis: Fragmentary sayings and dialogues of Confucius and his disciples, compiled after his death, on virtue, ritual propriety, and good government.

title: The Art of War
author: Sun Tzu
synopsis: A terse military treatise on deception, terrain, and calculation, arguing that the greatest general wins the war before it is ever fought.

title: The Dhammapada
author: Anonymous
synopsis: A collection of aphoristic verses attributed to the Buddha's own sayings, on mastering the mind and escaping suffering through right conduct.

title: Uncle Silas
author: Sheridan Le Fanu
synopsis: Orphaned heiress Maud Ruthyn is placed under the guardianship of her charming, sinister uncle Silas, whose remote house hides a decades-old murder and a fresh plot against her life.

title: Wylder's Hand
author: Sheridan Le Fanu
synopsis: A bridegroom vanishes on the eve of his wedding to an heiress, and as his cousin Captain Stanley Lake circles the family fortune, an old house's buried secrets and a hidden corpse surface.

title: The Beetle
author: Richard Marsh
synopsis: A shapeshifting Egyptian cult-priestess stalks a rising London politician to avenge a past outrage, terrorizing a tramp, a scientist, and a young woman engaged to her target in a novel that outsold Dracula on release.

title: The Willows
author: Algernon Blackwood
synopsis: Two canoeists camping on a flooded Danube island sense unseen, ancient presences pressing in from the willow thickets around them, until their camp itself seems to conspire against their escape.

title: The White People
author: Arthur Machen
synopsis: A young girl's secret diary records her initiation by her nurse into a hidden, ancient system of sorcery and forbidden rites in the Welsh hills, framed by a recluse's essay on true evil.

title: The Call of Cthulhu
author: H. P. Lovecraft
synopsis: A scholar assembles his late uncle's notes on a monstrous cult worshipping the sunken god Cthulhu, tracing dreams, a sailor's testimony, and a South Pacific island that should not exist.

title: At the Mountains of Madness
author: H. P. Lovecraft
synopsis: An Antarctic expedition uncovers the frozen ruins of a pre-human civilization beyond impossible peaks, and the survivors' account warns the world never to go back.

title: The Dunwich Horror
author: H. P. Lovecraft
synopsis: A monstrous, half-human child born to a decayed New England family grows into something that outstrips barns and shatters houses, until scholars from Miskatonic University attempt to banish it.

title: The Shadow over Innsmouth
author: H. P. Lovecraft
synopsis: A young traveler's detour through a decaying Massachusetts fishing town reveals its inhabitants' inherited, amphibious secret, and a night of pursuit through its empty streets he barely survives.

title: The Colour Out of Space
author: H. P. Lovecraft
synopsis: A meteorite crashes onto a New England farm and leaches an indescribable color into the soil, water, and family living there, withering them from within before the land is abandoned as a blasted heath.

title: The Pit
author: Frank Norris
synopsis: A Chicago wheat speculator's ruthless corner on the grain market enriches and then consumes him, while his wife Laura drifts toward an artist even as her husband's empire collapses around them.

title: Ramona
author: Helen Hunt Jackson
synopsis: A half-Native orphan raised in a proud Californio family falls for a Luiseño sheep-shearer, and their marriage draws them into the violent dispossession of Native land by incoming American settlers.

title: Pan
author: Knut Hamsun
synopsis: A hunter living alone in a northern Norwegian forest is consumed by a volatile, self-destroying passion for a local merchant's daughter, told in fragments recalled two years after the fact.

title: Buddenbrooks
author: Thomas Mann
synopsis: Four generations of a wealthy Lübeck merchant family decline from civic grandeur into illness, failed marriages, and irrelevance, as commercial ambition gives way to art, illness, and doubt.

title: Steppenwolf
author: Hermann Hesse
synopsis: A solitary, suicidal intellectual who thinks of himself as half man, half wolf is drawn out of his isolation by a dance-hall woman into jazz clubs, drugs, and a hallucinatory Magic Theater confronting his fractured self.

title: Oedipus at Colonus
author: Sophocles
synopsis: The blind, exiled Oedipus reaches a sacred grove near Athens with his daughter Antigone, where Theseus grants him sanctuary as Creon and his own son fight over his prophesied burial place.

title: Human, All Too Human
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
synopsis: Nietzsche breaks from Wagner and Schopenhauer to dissect morality, religion, and art as products of human psychology rather than eternal truths, in aphorisms addressed to 'free spirits.'

title: The Golden Bough
author: James George Frazer
synopsis: Frazer surveys myth, magic, and ritual across cultures and history, tracing the priest-king of Nemi's sacred grove out into a vast comparative theory of how religion evolves from magic toward science.

title: Poetics
author: Aristotle
synopsis: Aristotle dissects tragedy and epic poetry into their working parts — plot, character, and catharsis — grounding his theory in close readings of Homer and Sophocles.

title: In Search of Lost Time
author: Marcel Proust
synopsis: Proust's seven-volume novel follows an unnamed narrator's involuntary memories — most famously a madeleine dipped in tea — through the loves, society, and art of belle-époque and wartime France.

title: Barry Lyndon
author: William Makepeace Thackeray
synopsis: An Irish adventurer schemes, duels, and gambles his way from obscure poverty into the English aristocracy by marrying the widowed Countess of Lyndon, narrating his own rise and ruin without a shred of self-awareness of his villainy.

title: Pendennis
author: William Makepeace Thackeray
synopsis: A vain, impressionable young man drifts from an actress's spell through Oxford disgrace, London literary hackwork, and society courtship, guided and repeatedly rescued by his devoted uncle and the patient Laura.

title: The Newcomes
author: William Makepeace Thackeray
synopsis: Colonel Thomas Newcome, an honest old India veteran, returns to London society and watches his artist son Clive's love for their cousin Ethel founder on family pride and money, as the Colonel's own fortune and health decline.

title: Omoo
author: Herman Melville
synopsis: A sailor and his companion Doctor Long Ghost, cast ashore after a mutiny in the South Seas, drift through Tahiti and its islands as beachcombers, jailed loosely by half-hearted French and native authorities and living by their wits.

title: Mardi
author: Herman Melville
synopsis: A sailor jumps ship with a harpooner companion and, after rescuing an island maiden, drifts into the archipelago-kingdom of Mardi, an allegorical voyage through invented islands each satirizing a nation, philosophy, or folly of the real world.

title: Redburn
author: Herman Melville
synopsis: A naive young gentleman's son signs on as a green hand aboard a merchant ship to Liverpool, enduring the brutal hazing of the forecastle and discovering the squalor of the docks his father once described in genteel guidebook terms.

title: White-Jacket
author: Herman Melville
synopsis: A sailor nicknamed for the makeshift white jacket he sews himself narrates a voyage home aboard a U.S. Navy frigate, cataloguing its floating world of flogging, rank, and shipboard justice.

title: The Confidence-Man
author: Herman Melville
synopsis: Aboard a Mississippi steamboat on April Fool's Day, a shape-shifting swindler works through a series of disguises to test the credulity and charity of his fellow passengers, in Melville's bleak, riddling satire on trust and belief.

title: Fanshawe
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
synopsis: A frail, bookish college student at a small New England school falls for a guardian's ward pursued also by a genial rival and a sinister stranger, and dies quietly after saving her from abduction. Hawthorne's anonymously published, later disowned first novel.

title: St. Ives
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
synopsis: A French prisoner of war escapes an Edinburgh castle during the Napoleonic Wars and flees across Britain in disguise, chasing an inheritance and a sweetheart while a relentless pursuer closes in.

title: The Ebb-Tide
author: Robert Louis Stevenson and Lloyd Osbourne
synopsis: Three destitute beachcombers in Tahiti take charge of a schooner under false pretenses meaning to sell its cargo of champagne, and find the island they're sent to is ruled by a deranged, charismatic trader with his own designs on them.

title: Weir of Hermiston
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
synopsis: A stern Scottish hanging judge's sensitive son, banished to the family estate after a public rebuke, falls for a local girl whose family history entangles him with the very man his father once condemned. Stevenson's unfinished last novel.

title: Twilight Sleep
author: Edith Wharton
synopsis: A wealthy New York matriarch devotes herself to fads, causes, and painless-childbirth science to keep her family numb to any unpleasantness, while her son's marriage and her daughter's unhappiness quietly curdle beneath the anesthetized surface.

title: The Prime Minister
author: Anthony Trollope
synopsis: The scrupulous, thin-skinned Plantagenet Palliser becomes a reluctant coalition Prime Minister while his wife's political ambitions for him collide with his own doubts, entwined with the ruinous marriage of a young woman to a plausible foreign adventurer.

title: He Knew He Was Right
author: Anthony Trollope
synopsis: A young husband's baseless jealousy over his wife's friendship with her godfather curdles into an obsession that destroys his marriage, his reason, and finally himself, in Trollope's dark study of stubborn pride.

title: Ayala's Angel
author: Anthony Trollope
synopsis: Orphaned and shuttled between a rich aunt's household and a poor one, a romantic young woman refuses ordinary suitors while waiting for an imagined ideal 'angel of light,' until a real one finally proves worth having.

title: Three Men on the Bummel
author: Jerome K. Jerome
synopsis: The three friends from Three Men in a Boat, now married and middle-aged, escape their wives for a bicycling tour through the German countryside, bumbling through inns, bureaucracy, and each other's company.

title: The Fortune of the Rougons
author: Émile Zola
synopsis: During the December 1851 coup d'état, republican insurgents march through the Provençal town of Plassans singing the Marseillaise; the laborer Silvère and the young Miette, marked by her father's crime, share a last embrace before she seizes the insurgent banner and marches to her death. The opening volume of Zola's Rougon-Macquart cycle.

title: His Masterpiece
author: Émile Zola
synopsis: A struggling painter in 1860s Paris shelters a stranded young woman during a storm, and their bond deepens even as his fanatical, doomed pursuit of a single perfect canvas consumes his art, his friendships, and eventually his sanity.

title: Abbe Mouret's Transgression
author: Émile Zola
synopsis: A young priest devoted to celibacy loses his memory after an illness and, nursed back to health in a wild, overgrown estate, falls into a passionate love affair with a girl named Albine — until his identity and vows return, and he must choose between her and the Church.

title: A Love Episode
author: Émile Zola
synopsis: A pious young widow in Paris, absorbed in caring for her sickly daughter, is drawn into a consuming affair with the doctor who treats the child, and her awakened passion threatens to unravel the quiet order of her life.

title: Doctor Pascal
author: Émile Zola
synopsis: An aging scientist researching heredity keeps a secret archive documenting his own family's tainted bloodline, until his mother, desperate to destroy the damning records, turns his household against him. The closing volume of the Rougon-Macquart cycle.

title: Peter Ibbetson
author: George du Maurier
synopsis: Orphaned as a boy and exiled from his idyllic French childhood to a joyless life in London, a man discovers decades later that he can meet his first love in shared, lucid dreams that let them relive and even reshape the past together.

title: The Trumpet-Major
author: Thomas Hardy
synopsis: As invasion fever grips the English coast during the Napoleonic Wars, a miller's steady soldier son and his reckless sailor brother both fall for the same neighboring girl, whose choice between them plays out against the threat of Bonaparte's fleet.

title: A Laodicean
author: Thomas Hardy
synopsis: A young architect sketching Gothic ruins is drawn to a wealthy, modern-minded heiress who is restoring her family's ancient castle with telegraphs and industry, and finds himself entangled in her religious doubts, a rival's schemes, and his own ambitions.

title: The Well-Beloved
author: Thomas Hardy
synopsis: A sculptor spends his life chasing an idealized woman he calls his Well-Beloved, who seems to leap from one real woman to another just as he thinks he has finally caught her — across three generations of the same island family.

title: Diana of the Crossways
author: George Meredith
synopsis: A brilliant, independent Irish beauty becomes the target of Victorian society's gossip and persecution after she leaves her husband, and fights to keep her wit, freedom, and reputation intact through a string of suitors and scandals.

title: One of Our Conquerors
author: George Meredith
synopsis: A charming, successful London businessman lives happily with the woman he loves and their daughter under an arrangement society will not sanction, and races to legitimize it with a grand new estate before his vengeful estranged wife can expose them.

title: Imaginary Portraits
author: Walter Pater
synopsis: Four linked portraits of restless, gifted outsiders across history — a melancholy painter who reshapes Parisian taste, a mysterious youth who brings a golden age to a medieval town before it turns on him, and a Dutch philosopher who rejects the comfort and beauty he was born to.

title: Robert Elsmere
author: Humphry Ward
synopsis: A young Oxford-educated clergyman takes up a remote country parish and falls for a devout, austere woman there, even as his growing intellectual doubts about the literal truth of scripture pull him toward a crisis of faith that threatens to end his calling.

title: The Story of a Bad Boy
author: Thomas Bailey Aldrich
synopsis: A spirited boy sent from New Orleans to live with his grandfather in a small New England seaport gets into one scrape after another with his new friends — torching an old stagecoach among them — in a boyhood memoir that helped invent the American "bad boy" genre later perfected by Tom Sawyer.

title: Aurora Floyd
author: Mary Elizabeth Braddon
synopsis: A wealthy banker's beautiful, high-spirited daughter returns from her Paris schooling carrying a dark secret from her past, and a stern naval captain who first scorns her rakish reputation finds himself falling for her anyway — right as that secret threatens to surface.

title: San Kuo; or, Romance of the Three Kingdoms (Volume I)
author: Luo Guanzhong
synopsis: As the Han dynasty collapses into civil war, the sworn brothers Liu Bei, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei rise through battle and betrayal alongside the scheming warlord Cao Cao. This volume covers only the first half of the sprawling saga in C. H. Brewitt-Taylor's English translation, the only English edition on Gutenberg.

title: The Pillow-Book of Sei Shōnagon
author: Sei Shōnagon
synopsis: A Heian-era lady-in-waiting records her sharpest opinions, court gossip, and lists of elegant or irritating things, in one of the earliest and wittiest works of Japanese prose.

title: The History of Mary Prince, a West Indian Slave
author: Mary Prince
synopsis: Prince recounts, in her own words, her sale between owners across Bermuda and Antigua and the routine brutality of enslavement, in the first known narrative of an enslaved woman published in Britain.

title: Iola Leroy; Or, Shadows Uplifted
author: Frances Ellen Watkins Harper
synopsis: A mixed-race woman raised believing herself white is enslaved when her parentage is exposed, and after the Civil War chooses to dedicate her freedom to uplifting the Black community rather than pass into white society.

title: The Marrow of Tradition
author: Charles W. Chesnutt
synopsis: A white supremacist coup and massacre convulse a North Carolina town, entangling a Black doctor and his estranged half-white relations in a novel based on the real 1898 Wilmington massacre.

title: The Conjure Woman
author: Charles W. Chesnutt
synopsis: A formerly enslaved gardener spins seven sly folk tales of conjuring and transformation for his new white employers, each story quietly undercutting the plantation nostalgia it seems to indulge.

title: The Autobiography of an Ex-Colored Man
author: James Weldon Johnson
synopsis: A light-skinned Black man drifts between Black and white worlds in the Jim Crow South, Europe, and New York, and ultimately chooses to pass permanently as white, then wonders if he sold his birthright for a mess of pottage.

title: Black No More
author: George S. Schuyler
synopsis: A scientist invents a machine that turns Black skin white, and the ensuing scramble to buy whiteness upends America's racial order, in a razor-edged satire of race, capitalism, and self-hatred.

title: The Nibelungenlied
author: Anonymous
synopsis: The dragon-slayer Siegfried wins and loses the peerless Kriemhild, and his murder by the Burgundian court ignites her decades-long revenge, ending in the annihilation of an entire people at Attila's court.

title: Every Man in His Humor
author: Ben Jonson
synopsis: A jealous merchant, a would-be poet, a blustering soldier, and a gallery of other obsessives collide across a single London day, in Jonson's city comedy of manias and misunderstandings.

title: Bartholomew Fair
author: Ben Jonson
synopsis: A cross-section of London descends on the riotous Bartholomew Fair — a Puritan zealot, a jealous husband, con men, and a pig-woman — for a day of gluttony, fraud, and public humiliation.

title: The Description of a New World, Called the Blazing-World
author: Margaret Cavendish
synopsis: A woman is swept through the North Pole into a parallel world of talking bear-men and fish-men, becomes its Empress, and commissions philosophers and spirits to explain the nature of the universe to her.

title: Zadig; Or, The Book of Fate
author: Voltaire
synopsis: A wise Babylonian is repeatedly ruined by his own virtue and cleverness — losing wives, eyes, and freedom in turn — until fate reveals its hidden design, in Voltaire's sly philosophical fable.

title: The Chronicles of Clovis
author: Saki
synopsis: The languid schemer Clovis Sangrail talks his way through Edwardian drawing rooms, orchestrating small social catastrophes and absurd revenges with total composure, across this story collection.

title: The Unbearable Bassington
author: Saki
synopsis: A doting mother schemes to marry off her charming, feckless son Comus before his debts and indiscretions catch up with him, in Saki's one true novel, which turns from comedy to real loss.

title: Rosmersholm
author: Henrik Ibsen
synopsis: Back at his family estate, the ex-clergyman John Rosmer has quietly abandoned his old faith and politics under the influence of his late wife's companion Rebecca West, whose real hold on the house is darker than it looks. When his brother-in-law forces a reckoning, Rosmer and Rebecca walk out together to the footbridge over the millrace and do not return.

title: The Master Builder
author: Henrik Ibsen
synopsis: Aging architect Halvard Solness, who has spent his career keeping younger rivals down and is haunted by the fire that built his fortune, is confronted by a strange young woman who demands he make good on a promise from her childhood: to climb as high as he builds. He climbs the tower on his newest house and falls to his death.

title: Opticks
author: Isaac Newton
synopsis: Newton lays out his experiments splitting sunlight through prisms to prove white light is a mixture of distinct colors, then builds a full theory of reflection, refraction, and the colors of thin films and diffraction from those results.

title: The Stranger
author: Albert Camus
synopsis: Meursault, indifferent to his mother's death, kills a man on a sun-blinded beach and is condemned as much for his honesty as his crime.

title: The Lady from the Sea
author: Henrik Ibsen
synopsis: Ellida Wangel, restless and drawn back to the sea, must choose between the mysterious sailor who once claimed her and the husband who finally lets her choose freely. Ibsen's play on marriage as bondage versus chosen commitment.

title: Vera; or, The Nihilists
author: Oscar Wilde
synopsis: A Russian peasant girl turned Nihilist conspirator is chosen to assassinate the new, secretly reformist Tsar, only to discover he is the man she loves. Wilde's first play, a melodrama of revolution and sacrifice.

title: Discourses on the First Decade of Titus Livius
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
synopsis: Machiavelli works through Livy's history of early Rome book by book, drawing out the practical lessons for building and preserving a free republic.

title: History of Florence
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
synopsis: Machiavelli's history of Florence from its Roman origins through the rise of the Medici, tracing the factional struggles that shaped the republic.

title: Past and Present
author: Thomas Carlyle
synopsis: Carlyle sets a 12th-century monastery's ordered, purposeful life under Abbot Samson against the chaos and 'cash nexus' of industrial Victorian England, demanding real leadership over laissez-faire drift.

title: Unto This Last, and Other Essays on Political Economy
author: John Ruskin
synopsis: Ruskin attacks classical political economy's treatment of workers as mere mechanisms, arguing that true wealth is the life and just relations it enables, not accumulation for its own sake.

title: Culture and Anarchy
author: Matthew Arnold
synopsis: Arnold argues for 'culture' — pursuing human perfection through the best that has been thought and said — as the antidote to class self-interest and the modern cult of 'doing as one likes.'

title: A Modern Utopia
author: H. G. Wells
synopsis: A philosopher and his companion, walking in the Alps, step through into a parallel Earth organized as a rationally planned world-state, and debate how such a utopia could actually be governed and kept free.

title: The Watsons
author: Jane Austen
synopsis: Emma Watson, raised in comfort by a wealthy aunt, returns to her poor clergyman father's household and must navigate courtship and family friction with almost no fortune of her own. Austen's unfinished fragment, abandoned after her father's death.

title: A Sicilian Romance
author: Ann Radcliffe
synopsis: Sisters Julia and Emilia Mazzini, raised believing their mother long dead, uncover a hidden wing of their father's castle and the truth of a mother imprisoned rather than buried.

title: Caleb Williams
author: William Godwin
synopsis: A young servant, Caleb Williams, discovers that his admired employer Falkland once committed a murder, and is hunted, framed, and imprisoned across England once Falkland realizes his secret is known.

title: 1Q84
author: Haruki Murakami
synopsis: A woman assassin named Aomame and an aspiring novelist named Tengo find their fates converging after both notice small, unsettling changes to the world — two moons, a shadowy cult called Sakigake, and tiny beings known as the Little People — in a Tokyo that seems to have slipped into a parallel 1984.

title: A Fine Balance
author: Rohinton Mistry
synopsis: During India's State of Emergency, a widowed seamstress, a student boarder, and two tailors fleeing caste violence are thrown together in a cramped Bombay flat, their fragile friendship tested by a country turning against its poorest citizens.

title: Blood Meridian
author: Cormac McCarthy
synopsis: A teenage runaway falls in with a band of scalp-hunters roaming the Texas-Mexico borderlands, dominated by the monstrous, erudite Judge Holden, in a hallucinatory, blood-soaked reckoning with American violence.

title: Educated
author: Tara Westover
synopsis: Raised by survivalist parents in the Idaho mountains with no birth certificate and no schooling, Westover teaches herself enough to escape to college, and finds that education costs her the only family she's ever known.

title: Interpreter of Maladies
author: Jhumpa Lahiri
synopsis: Nine stories trace Indian and Indian-American lives adrift between two cultures — a tour guide who translates a doctor's symptoms and confessions alike, a couple grieving a stillborn child, a babysitter navigating a new country — in Lahiri's Pulitzer-winning debut collection.

title: Lonesome Dove
author: Larry McMurtry
synopsis: Two aging ex-Texas Rangers drive a stolen herd of cattle from the Rio Grande to Montana, the long trail claiming friends, lovers, and outlaws along the way in McMurtry's Pulitzer-winning epic of the fading American frontier.

title: Never Let Me Go
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
synopsis: Kathy, Ruth, and Tommy grow up together at Hailsham, an English boarding school whose true, chilling purpose as a breeding ground for organ donors only gradually reveals itself.

title: No Country for Old Men
author: Cormac McCarthy
synopsis: A Texas welder who stumbles on a drug deal gone wrong and its two million dollars in cash is hunted across the border country by an implacable killer, while an aging sheriff trails behind, increasingly certain the world has outrun him.

title: The Bluest Eye
author: Toni Morrison
synopsis: A poor Black girl in 1940s Ohio longs for blue eyes, believing they would make her beautiful and loved, in Morrison's unsparing debut novel about racism, self-hatred, and a shattered childhood.

title: The Buried Giant
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
synopsis: In a post-Arthurian Britain shrouded in a mist that erases memory, an elderly couple sets out to find the son they can no longer clearly remember, crossing paths with ogres, a dragon, and an aged Sir Gawain.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
author: Stieg Larsson
synopsis: A disgraced financial journalist and a brilliant, damaged hacker investigate a wealthy family's decades-old disappearance, unearthing a trail of serial murder tied to Sweden's darkest secrets.

title: The Glass Castle
author: Jeannette Walls
synopsis: Walls recounts a nomadic childhood of poverty and neglect under her brilliant, alcoholic father and free-spirited mother, and her escape from their chaos to build a stable life in New York.

title: The Help
author: Kathryn Stockett
synopsis: In 1960s Jackson, Mississippi, a young white writer persuades Black maids to share their stories of working for white families, risking all their safety in the segregated South.

title: The Namesake
author: Jhumpa Lahiri
synopsis: Gogol Ganguli, son of Bengali immigrants in America, spends years chafing against the unwanted Russian name his father gave him, before he can understand the private tragedy behind it.

title: The Rebel
author: Albert Camus
synopsis: Camus traces the idea of rebellion from metaphysical revolt against God through revolutionary politics and terror, asking whether rebellion can be lived without collapsing into the very murder and tyranny it rises against.

title: The Remains of the Day
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
synopsis: An aging English butler drives across the countryside to see a former housekeeper he once loved, reflecting on a lifetime of loyal service to a lord whose Nazi sympathies he chose not to see.

title: The Time Traveler's Wife
author: Audrey Niffenegger
synopsis: Henry, a librarian with a genetic disorder that yanks him uncontrollably through time, and Clare, the artist who has loved him since childhood, piece together a marriage lived out of order.

title: The Unconsoled
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
synopsis: A celebrated pianist arrives in an unnamed Central European city for a concert he can't quite remember agreeing to, and finds his schedule, memory, and grip on reality dissolving into dreamlike distortion.

title: The Road
author: Cormac McCarthy
synopsis: A father and his young son push a shopping cart down an ash-covered highway toward the coast, scavenging to survive and hiding from cannibals in an America destroyed by an unnamed apocalypse.

title: When We Were Orphans
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
synopsis: A celebrated English detective returns to 1930s Shanghai to solve the central mystery of his own life: the long-ago disappearance of his parents.

title: A Moveable Feast
author: Ernest Hemingway
synopsis: Hemingway recalls his poor, hungry early years in 1920s Paris — writing in cafés, sparring with Gertrude Stein and Ford Madox Ford, and watching a reckless, talented Fitzgerald begin to unravel — in a posthumously published memoir of the Lost Generation.

title: The Plague
author: Albert Camus
synopsis: A doctor in the Algerian city of Oran leads the fight against a rat-borne epidemic that seals the city's gates, an existentialist parable of absurdity, solidarity, and the will to keep struggling against a fate you cannot beat.

title: A Room of One's Own
author: Virginia Woolf
synopsis: Invited to lecture on women and fiction, Woolf argues that a woman needs money and a room of her own to write at all, tracing the silencing of women's genius from Shakespeare's imagined sister to the present.

author: Stephen King
synopsis: A high school English teacher discovers a portal in the back of a Maine diner that leads to September 1958, and sets off on a mission to stop the assassination of John F. Kennedy. Settling into small-town Texas under a new identity to wait out the years until November 1963, he falls in love and slowly learns that the past is obdurate: it resists being changed, and every attempt to alter it exacts a price. Stephen King blends time-travel suspense with a meditation on fate, memory, and whether a better world is worth what must be sacrificed to build it.

title: A Heartbreaking Work of Staggering Genius
author: Dave Eggers
synopsis: After both of his parents die within five weeks of each other, twenty-something Dave Eggers becomes the guardian of his eight-year-old brother, Toph, and moves with him from Chicago to Berkeley to start over. Blending raw memoir with self-aware, formally inventive digressions, the book follows Eggers's improvised attempts at parenting and grief-stricken reinvention while he co-founds a scrappy San Francisco magazine. It is as much a restless meditation on the vanity and impossibility of memoir-writing itself as it is the story it sets out to tell.

title: A Suitable Boy
author: Vikram Seth
synopsis: Set in the early 1950s, in the first years after Indian independence and partition, the novel follows widowed matriarch Mrs Rupa Mehra as she searches for a suitable husband for her daughter Lata, who is drawn to three very different suitors. Around this central courtship, Vikram Seth weaves the intertwined fortunes of four families across politics, land reform, courtrooms, poetry recitals, and the shoe trade in the fictional city of Brahmpur and beyond. Sprawling in scope, it captures a newly democratic nation finding its footing through the domestic dramas, religious tensions, and everyday compromises of ordinary people.

title: Becoming
author: Michelle Obama
synopsis: Michelle Obama's memoir traces her path from a working-class childhood on Chicago's South Side, through Princeton and Harvard Law School, to a career as a lawyer and hospital executive, and ultimately to the White House. She writes candidly about marriage, motherhood, and the strain of public scrutiny as a Black woman thrust into an institution never built with her in mind, alongside the causes she championed as First Lady. It is both a personal history and a meditation on finding one's own voice inside other people's expectations.

title: Being There
author: Jerzy Kosinski
synopsis: Chance is a middle-aged gardener who has spent his entire sheltered life tending a wealthy man's Washington townhouse garden, his understanding of the world shaped almost entirely by what he watches on television. When his employer dies, Chance is turned out into the street for the first time, and a chance accident delivers him into the orbit of a dying industrialist and his politically connected wife. Mistaken for a man of cultured reticence and profound wisdom, his simple, literal remarks about gardening are read as sage metaphors on economics and politics, and he is swept upward through Washington society and the media toward the highest levels of power. The novel is a spare, deadpan satire of image, television, and the emptiness of public life.

title: Beloved
author: Toni Morrison
synopsis: Set in Ohio in the years after the Civil War, the novel follows Sethe, a formerly enslaved woman haunted by a past she cannot outrun and, eventually, by a mysterious young woman who arrives at her door and seems to embody it. As the true nature of this visitor becomes clear, Sethe, her daughter Denver, and her lover Paul D are forced to confront the unspeakable choice Sethe once made to keep her children out of slavery's reach. Morrison renders memory, motherhood, and trauma with a fractured, incantatory structure that moves between the horrors of Sweet Home plantation and the fragile freedom that follows.

title: Blink
author: Malcolm Gladwell
synopsis: In Blink, journalist Malcolm Gladwell examines the split-second judgments and unconscious pattern-recognition that shape decisions long before conscious reasoning kicks in. Drawing on case studies from art authentication, marriage counseling, military war games, and police shootings, he explores both the uncanny accuracy and the serious perils of instant intuition. The book argues that thin-slicing, rapid judgment from very limited information, can be trained and structured for reliability, but is also vulnerable to bias, overload, and misread signals under pressure.

title: Bring Up the Bodies
author: Hilary Mantel
synopsis: Bring Up the Bodies picks up the story of Thomas Cromwell as Henry VIII's infatuation with Anne Boleyn curdles into a search for grounds to remove her. Over a tense few months in 1535-36, Cromwell maneuvers through the English court, weighing old grudges and new alliances as the king's eye turns toward Jane Seymour. Written in Hilary Mantel's distinctive close third-person present tense, the novel traces how ruthless political calculation and self-preservation converge to bring down a queen.

title: Cloud Atlas
author: David Mitchell
synopsis: Cloud Atlas weaves together six narratives spanning centuries and continents, from a nineteenth-century voyage across the Pacific to a post-apocalyptic future on the Hawaiian islands. Each story is nested inside the next, read or watched or overheard by the protagonist of the one that follows, and the novel breaks off each tale at a cliffhanger before resuming it in reverse order in the second half. Along the way David Mitchell moves fluidly between genres: seafaring journal, epistolary romance, corporate thriller, comic memoir, dystopian interrogation, and oral folktale. Threaded through all six are recurring echoes of exploitation and resistance, suggesting that a single act of courage or cruelty ripples forward through time.

title: David and Goliath
author: Malcolm Gladwell
synopsis: Malcolm Gladwell revisits the biblical story of David and Goliath to argue that apparent disadvantages — dyslexia, small class sizes gone wrong, losing a parent young, being an underdog in an unfair fight — often conceal hidden advantages, while apparent strengths can conceal real weaknesses. Through case studies ranging from a girls' basketball team to civil rights strategists in Birmingham to French villagers hiding Jewish refugees, he examines why the powerful so often misjudge the weak. The book is a sustained argument for rethinking what courage, power, and disadvantage actually mean.

title: Dreams from My Father
author: Barack Obama
synopsis: Barack Obama's memoir traces his search for identity as the son of a Kenyan father he barely knew and a white American mother, moving from a childhood in Hawaii and Indonesia to his early career as a community organizer on Chicago's South Side. Written years before he entered politics, the book grapples with questions of race, absence, and belonging in America. It closes with a journey to Kenya, where Obama meets his father's family and confronts the complicated truth behind the man he had spent a lifetime imagining.

title: Fortunately, the Milk
author: Neil Gaiman
synopsis: A father sent out for milk to go with the kids' breakfast cereal returns much later than expected, and when his skeptical children demand to know why, he launches into an escalating, self-interrupting tall tale. The story spirals through a hot-air balloon, time-traveling stegosaurus professors, alien abductors, pirates, and a volcano, with every wild digression somehow looping back to explain the fate of the milk. It is a fast, silly, illustrated shaggy-dog story about the art of a really good excuse.

title: Freakonomics
author: Steven D. Levitt and Stephen J. Dubner
synopsis: Economist Steven D. Levitt and journalist Stephen J. Dubner apply the tools of economic analysis to a string of unlikely subjects, from cheating sumo wrestlers and schoolteachers to the hidden economics of crack dealing and the surprising link between legalized abortion and falling crime rates. Rather than advancing one grand theory, the book argues that incentives, properly understood through data, explain human behavior far better than conventional wisdom does. Along the way it dismantles assumptions about parenting, real-estate agents, the Ku Klux Klan, and the power of a first name, making the case that curiosity and rigorous number-crunching can expose the hidden side of everyday life.

title: How to Read and Why
author: Harold Bloom
synopsis: In this practical guide to literary appreciation, Harold Bloom moves chapter by chapter through short stories, poems, novels, and plays, showing readers how close, patient rereading rewards attention. He takes up writers from Chekhov, Hemingway, and Flannery O'Connor to Shakespeare, Austen, Whitman, and Dickinson, building a case for particular works as models of what literature can do.
