Equal parts personal canon and instruction manual, the book argues that reading well is a discipline that deepens the self as much as it deepens understanding of the text.

title: Infinite Jest
author: David Foster Wallace
synopsis: In a near-future North America organized around corporate-sponsored calendar years and a hazardous new form of subsidized entertainment, the novel braids together the students of an elite Boston-area junior tennis academy, the recovering addicts and staff of a halfway house down the hill from it, and a cell of wheelchair-bound Quebecois separatists hunting a film cartridge so entertaining that anyone who watches it loses all will to do anything else. Told through a sprawling, digressive structure and hundreds of endnotes, it moves between comedy, addiction and recovery, competitive tennis, family inheritance, and geopolitical farce. At its center is the fractured Incandenza family, whose dead patriarch made the lethal film, and the novel's abiding questions about entertainment, escape, and what makes life worth living.

title: Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell
author: Susanna Clarke
synopsis: In an alternate history England where magic has faded into scholarly memory, the reclusive Mr Norrell reintroduces practical magic to the world and takes on the brilliant, impulsive Jonathan Strange as his pupil. Their rivalry over the proper direction of English magic plays out against the Napoleonic Wars and the fashionable drawing rooms of Regency London, while an ancient, capricious fairy lord works his own designs on the humans around them. Woven throughout with mock-scholarly footnotes cataloguing a fictional history of English magic, the novel builds toward a reckoning with the legendary Raven King, the vanished magician-monarch whose return both men fear and desire.

title: Klara and the Sun
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
synopsis: Klara, a solar-powered Artificial Friend built to keep a lonely child company, watches from a store window and hopes to be chosen. Once purchased for a sickly girl named Josie, she observes the human world with a mixture of naive devotion and startling perceptiveness, coming to believe the Sun itself might be able to save Josie's life. Ishiguro tells the story entirely through Klara's limited, earnest point of view, using her outsider's gaze to probe what love, loyalty, and selfhood really mean.

title: Life of Pi
author: Yann Martel
synopsis: Piscine Molitor Patel, the teenage son of a Pondicherry zookeeper, survives the sinking of the cargo ship carrying his family and their animals to Canada, and finds himself adrift in a lifeboat on the Pacific with a Bengal tiger named Richard Parker. Over 227 days at sea, he must invent the discipline and ingenuity to keep himself alive alongside a predator he cannot escape. Framed as a story told to a novelist years later, the book is as much a meditation on faith, storytelling, and which version of events we choose to believe as it is a survival tale.

title: Love in the Time of Cholera
author: Gabriel García Márquez
synopsis: Love in the Time of Cholera follows Florentino Ariza's decades-long devotion to Fermina Daza, whom he loved as a young telegraph operator before she married the esteemed Dr. Juvenal Urbino instead. Over more than fifty years in an unnamed Caribbean port city, the novel alternates between Florentino's restless pursuit of countless lovers while he waits and the long, ordinary intimacy of the Urbinos' marriage. When Dr. Urbino's death finally frees Fermina, Florentino gets his chance to reclaim a love interrupted half a century before. Gabriel García Márquez treats aging, illness, and desire with the same lush, mythic realism he brought to his earlier work, turning a story of stubborn persistence into a meditation on love as a lifelong condition.

title: Midnight's Children
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: Salman Rushdie's magical-realist epic follows Saleem Sinai, born at the exact moment of India's independence in 1947 and endowed, along with the other 1,000 children born in that first hour, with a strange telepathic gift. Saleem's personal history becomes inseparably tangled with the fate of the newly independent nation as he narrates his family's fortunes across Partition, wars, and political upheaval in India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh. Told in a digressive, self-aware voice to his companion Padma, the novel is at once a coming-of-age story, a family saga, and an allegory of a young nation's turbulent growth.

title: Neverwhere
author: Neil Gaiman
synopsis: When ordinary London businessman Richard Mayhew stops to help an injured young woman named Door, he finds himself erased from the world he knew and pulled down into London Below, a shadow city of forgotten tube stations, sewers, and ancient rituals populated by those who have fallen through the cracks of the world above. Pursued by two unsettling assassins and guided by a duplicitous marquis, Richard and Door search for the reason her family was murdered while Richard tries to find his way back to his old life. Along the way he encounters an earl who holds court in a train carriage, a market that moves nightly, and a beast said to sleep beneath the city, discovering that the London he thought he knew was only ever half the story.

title: Piranesi
author: Susanna Clarke
synopsis: Piranesi lives alone inside an endless House of infinite halls, statues, and tides, meticulously cataloguing its wonders and tending to the bones of the dead he calls his ancestors. His only companion is a visiting scholar he calls the Other, who comes twice a week in search of a mysterious Great and Secret Knowledge. When a new visitor's warnings, and strange gaps in Piranesi's own journals, suggest that the House and his identity within it are not what he has always believed, he is pulled toward a truth that will upend everything he thought he knew about himself and the world.

title: Quichotte
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: Salman Rushdie's Quichotte follows Ismail Smile, an aging pharmaceutical salesman who renames himself Quichotte after a lifetime of watching too much television, and who sets off on a quixotic road trip across America in pursuit of a former talk-show star he is convinced is his destined love. Accompanied by an imaginary son named Sancho who gradually becomes more real, Quichotte's journey is narrated within a novel being written by a struggling spy novelist named Sam DuChamp, whose own life mirrors and refracts his creation's. A dazzling, satirical riff on Cervantes's Don Quixote, the book roams across addiction, racism, celebrity culture, and estrangement between parents and children in an America saturated by screens and conspiracy.

title: Revenge of the Tipping Point
author: Malcolm Gladwell
synopsis: Malcolm Gladwell returns to the ideas of his 2000 bestseller The Tipping Point, this time asking who engineers social epidemics rather than just how they spread. Through stories of a Los Angeles bank-robbery wave, the opioid crisis, Harvard's admissions quotas, and the making of the 1978 television miniseries Holocaust, he examines superspreaders, small-group tipping thresholds like the "magic third," and the moral responsibility of those who set contagions in motion. The book reframes social change as something that can be deliberately manufactured, for better or worse, rather than simply observed after the fact.

title: String Theory
author: David Foster Wallace
synopsis: String Theory collects five of David Foster Wallace's essays on tennis, written between 1990 and 2006, ranging from a wind-swept account of playing junior tennis in the Illinois flatlands to profiles of journeyman pro Michael Joyce, a takedown of a ghostwritten Tracy Austin memoir, and a rhapsodic meditation on Roger Federer. Wallace turns matches, tournaments, and the machinery of professional sport into occasions for thinking about genius, effort, and what a body under extreme pressure can reveal about consciousness itself. Together the pieces argue that tennis, watched and described closely enough, is as demanding an intellectual and aesthetic pursuit as any art form.

title: SuperFreakonomics
author: Steven D. Levitt and Stephen J. Dubner
synopsis: SuperFreakonomics is Steven D. Levitt and Stephen J. Dubner's follow-up to Freakonomics, applying economic reasoning to an eclectic mix of subjects: street prostitution, the hunt for terrorists hidden in banking data, the incentives behind climate change and geoengineering, and the gap between how generous people claim to be and how they actually behave in experiments. Weaving together data, interviews, and counterintuitive case studies, the authors argue that people respond to incentives in ways that often defy conventional wisdom and moral intuition. Along the way they profile inventors, economists, and hustlers whose stories illustrate how looking at a problem sideways can turn up an unexpectedly simple, cheap fix.

title: Talking to Strangers
author: Malcolm Gladwell
synopsis: Malcolm Gladwell examines why encounters with strangers go wrong so often, arguing that people default to trusting what they're told, misread unfamiliar faces and emotions, and assume that behavior in an unfamiliar setting means what it would mean at home. Through cases including the unmasking of Cuban double agents, the wrongful conviction of Amanda Knox, Neville Chamberlain's meetings with Hitler, and the traffic stop that killed Sandra Bland, he traces how these built-in blind spots produce real catastrophes. The book is less about how to spot a liar than about why we should be humble about how little a face-to-face meeting actually tells us.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
synopsis: A young Andalusian shepherd named Santiago sets out from Spain for the Egyptian pyramids after a recurring dream convinces him a treasure awaits him there. Along the way he meets a king, a crystal merchant, an Englishman studying alchemy, and finally an alchemist himself, each of whom teaches him something about listening to his heart and pursuing what Coelho calls his "Personal Legend." Written as a modern fable, the novel follows Santiago's journey through the Tangier marketplace and across the Sahara as he learns to read omens and trust the world's hidden unity. It became one of the best-selling novels in history and established Coelho as an international literary figure.

title: The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay
author: Michael Chabon
synopsis: In 1939, Czech refugee and trained magician Josef Kavalier escapes Nazi-occupied Prague and joins his Brooklyn cousin Sammy Clay to break into the fledgling comic book business. Together they create the Escapist, a costumed hero built from Joe's own longing to free his family from Europe, and ride the industry's boom through fortune, censorship hearings, and war. Spanning two decades of New York's Golden Age of comics, the novel follows the cousins through love, loss, and reinvention as their invented heroics collide with real-world catastrophe.

title: The Art of Racing in the Rain
author: Garth Stein
synopsis: Narrated by Enzo, an aging dog who is convinced that his next life will be a human one, this novel recounts the years he has spent with his owner, Seattle amateur race car driver Denny Swift. As Denny chases a shot at professional racing, marries, and starts a family, Enzo watches from the floor, applying the racing philosophy of his hero Ayrton Senna to the wrecks and comebacks of ordinary life. When tragedy and a bitter custody fight threaten to take Denny's daughter away from him, Enzo becomes the family's silent witness and, in his own way, its protector. The result is a story about loyalty, grief, and the will to keep driving through the rain, told through the eyes of a dog who has been paying closer attention than anyone realized.

title: The Bone Clocks
author: David Mitchell
synopsis: Spanning six decades from 1984 to a climate-ravaged 2043, the novel follows Holly Sykes, an English teenager who runs away from home after a family quarrel and unwittingly becomes entangled in a secret war between two factions of psychically gifted immortals. Told through a shifting cast of narrators, including a caddish novelist, a war reporter, and Holly herself at different ages, it moves from suburban England to Cambridge, Iraq, a literary festival circuit, and beyond. Beneath its globe-trotting realism runs a hidden supernatural plot about soul transmigration that only fully surfaces as the decades, and the world's fortunes, wind down.

title: The Circle
author: Dave Eggers
synopsis: Mae Holland lands a coveted job at the Circle, a Silicon Valley tech company that has absorbed nearly every online service into one all-seeing platform. As she rises through the ranks, she embraces the company's ideology that total transparency and constant connection will perfect society, even as cameras spread everywhere and privacy disappears. The novel follows her transformation from eager new hire to true believer, tracing the human costs of a culture built on the slogans that secrets are lies and sharing is caring.

title: The Color Purple
author: Alice Walker
synopsis: The Color Purple is an epistolary novel told through the letters of Celie, a poor Black woman in the rural American South in the early twentieth century, and later through the letters of her sister Nettie, writing from a missionary posting in West Africa. Across decades, Celie's voice moves from silenced endurance under an abusive father and husband toward self-possession, shaped by her bond with the blues singer Shug Avery and by the women around her. The novel traces how Celie comes to find her own voice, her own understanding of God, and her independence.

title: The Every
author: Dave Eggers
synopsis: In this satirical follow-up to The Circle, a former forest ranger named Delaney Wells goes undercover at the world's dominant tech-and-commerce monopoly, intending to destroy it from within by pitching ever more absurd and invasive products, gambling that the company is too far gone to recognize satire. Instead, each proposal she thinks will horrify the public is embraced and adopted, accelerating the very total-surveillance, algorithmic-consensus culture she set out to expose. The novel follows her uneasy alliances and doubts as the company closes in on total control over knowledge, art, and human behavior.

title: The God of Small Things
author: Arundhati Roy
synopsis: Set in Kerala, India, in the late 1960s and mid-1990s, the novel follows fraternal twins Estha and Rahel as a visit from their glamorous half-English cousin sets in motion a chain of transgressions across lines of caste, class, and family loyalty. Interweaving the twins' childhood with their adult return to the family home, Arundhati Roy traces how one forbidden love and one afternoon's tragedy reshape the destinies of an entire household. Told in lyrical, circling prose that approaches its central wound gradually before finally naming it, the book is as much about the machinery of history and social rule as it is about a single family's private catastrophe.

title: The Graveyard Book
author: Neil Gaiman
synopsis: After his family is murdered, a toddler wanders into a nearby graveyard and is adopted and raised by its ghostly residents, who name him Nobody Owens. Guarded by the mysterious Silas, Bod grows up learning the graveyard's ancient tricks while the man who killed his family still hunts for him beyond the gates. As he edges toward adulthood, Bod must decide how long he can stay safely among the dead before facing the living world, and the man Jack, on his own.

title: The Mirror and the Light
author: Hilary Mantel
synopsis: The concluding novel in Hilary Mantel's Thomas Cromwell trilogy follows the blacksmith's son at the height of his power, in the years after Anne Boleyn's execution, as he serves Henry VIII through a fraught new royal marriage, religious upheaval, and the schemes of rival courtiers. Cromwell reshapes England's church and state while managing the king's volatile moods, the ambitions of old noble families, and his own accumulating enemies. As his influence and wealth grow, so does the danger surrounding him, and the novel traces his final years toward an inevitable reckoning.

title: The Monk of Mokha
author: Dave Eggers
synopsis: The Monk of Mokha is Dave Eggers's narrative nonfiction account of Mokhtar Alkhanshali, a young Yemeni American from San Francisco's Tenderloin who sets out to revive his ancestral homeland's centuries-old coffee trade. Impulsive and self-taught, Mokhtar travels into war-torn Yemen just as a Saudi-led bombing campaign and Houthi advance close in around him, determined to source and export specialty-grade beans from remote highland farms. Eggers braids his harrowing escape from a besieged Sana'a together with the deeper history of coffee's origins in Yemen, producing a story of ambition, heritage, and survival.

title: The Nickel Boys
author: Colson Whitehead
synopsis: In early-1960s Tallahassee, an idealistic Black teenager named Elwood Curtis, inspired by the words of Martin Luther King Jr., is on his way to college when a case of mistaken circumstance gets him sentenced to the Nickel Academy, a brutal reform school. There he befriends the more cynical Turner, and the two boys navigate a system of casual violence, corruption, and racial terror that the school's administrators hide behind a facade of discipline and uplift. Moving between the school and the protagonist's later life, the novel traces how that institution's cruelty reverberates across a lifetime.

title: The Ocean at the End of the Lane
author: Neil Gaiman
synopsis: A middle-aged man returns to his childhood village for a funeral and finds himself drawn back to the farm at the end of the lane, where a strange, ancient family once lived. Sitting by their pond, he recovers buried memories of a fateful summer when he was seven years old: the peculiar Hempstock women who took him in, and a dangerous entity that entered his family through a seemingly ordinary act of kindness gone wrong. Blending horror, myth, and the texture of childhood memory, the novel explores how thin the boundary is between the everyday world adults inhabit and the vast, uncanny truths that children sense but cannot yet name.

title: The Satanic Verses
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: After their hijacked jet explodes over the English Channel, two Indian actors -- Gibreel Farishta, a Bollywood matinee idol, and Saladin Chamcha, an anglicized voice-over artist -- fall to earth transformed, one gaining an angelic glow and the other sprouting horns and hooves. Interwoven with their disorienting new lives in Thatcher-era London are dream-visions of the Prophet Mahound and the founding of a new faith in the desert city of Jahilia, and the story of a village drawn toward the sea by a peasant girl's visions. Salman Rushdie's novel is a sprawling, restless meditation on migration, hybrid identity, and the volatile border between doubt and faith.

title: The Tipping Point
author: Malcolm Gladwell
synopsis: Malcolm Gladwell's first book examines why ideas, products, and behaviors spread through society the way epidemics spread through a population, reaching a single dramatic moment of critical mass. Drawing on case studies ranging from the surprise revival of Hush Puppies to the sudden plunge in New York City's crime rate, he argues that these tipping points are driven by a small set of unusually connected or persuasive people, the inherent "stickiness" of a message, and the power of surrounding context. The result is a work of popular social science that reshaped how readers talk about word of mouth, trends, and sudden social change.

title: The Uncommon Reader
author: Alan Bennett
synopsis: When Queen Elizabeth II stumbles across a mobile library parked outside Buckingham Palace, a polite errand turns into an all-consuming passion for reading. Guided by a young kitchen boy who becomes her literary confidant, she works her way through novels, biographies, and poetry, and her inner life begins to expand in ways the royal household finds increasingly inconvenient. Alan Bennett's slyly funny novella imagines what happens when the most dutiful public figure in Britain discovers the private, subversive pleasure of books.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
synopsis: Nobel laureate psychologist Daniel Kahneman distills a career of research into how the mind reaches judgments and decisions, organized around two systems: fast, intuitive System 1 and slow, deliberate System 2. Drawing on decades of experiments conducted with Amos Tversky, he surveys the biases and mental shortcuts—anchoring, availability, loss aversion, overconfidence—that quietly shape choices about money, risk, and happiness. He also explores the split between the moment-to-moment 'experiencing self' and the retrospective 'remembering self' in judging a life well lived. The book became a landmark popular account of behavioral economics and cognitive psychology.

title: What the Dog Saw
author: Malcolm Gladwell
synopsis: A collection of Malcolm Gladwell's favorite pieces from his years as a New Yorker staff writer, gathered around the question of why some people see things the rest of us miss. The essays range from the invention of the perfect ketchup and a pitchman's rise to the psychology of criminal profilers, the causes of the Enron collapse, and the puzzle of predicting who will succeed. Gladwell weaves interviews, statistics, and case studies together to probe the gap between expertise, intuition, and hindsight.

title: Zeitoun
author: Dave Eggers
synopsis: In August 2005, Abdulrahman Zeitoun, a Syrian-born painting contractor, stays behind in New Orleans as Hurricane Katrina approaches, paddling a secondhand canoe through the flooded city to rescue trapped neighbors and feed abandoned animals. His wife Kathy, evacuated with their children, waits anxiously for news as the city descends into chaos. When Zeitoun is swept up in a post-storm security crackdown and disappears into a makeshift, lawless detention system, the family's ordeal exposes the panic, prejudice, and breakdown of due process that followed the disaster. Dave Eggers reconstructs the true story of one family caught between a natural catastrophe and a man-made one.

title: Wolf Hall
author: Hilary Mantel
synopsis: Wolf Hall reimagines the rise of Thomas Cromwell, a blacksmith's son who claws his way from obscurity to become Henry VIII's indispensable fixer. As Cardinal Wolsey falls and the king's obsession with Anne Boleyn upends the English church and court, Cromwell maneuvers with cool intelligence through a world of shifting allegiances, old grudges, and mortal risk. Written in Mantel's distinctive close third-person present tense, the novel follows Cromwell from Wolsey's disgrace through Anne's coronation, ending as he sets his sights on the Seymour family at Wolf Hall.

title: The Diary of a Madman
author: Nikolai Gogol
synopsis: A lowly St. Petersburg clerk, hopelessly infatuated with his director's daughter, starts eavesdropping on the lapdogs he believes are writing letters to each other, then declares himself the missing King of Spain and marches off to be crowned. His journal entries grow ever more deranged and the dates dissolve into nonsense as the delusion carries him, finally, into an asylum he mistakes for the Spanish royal court.

title: Ethan Brand
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
synopsis: Eighteen years after walking away from his lime-kiln to search the world for the Unpardonable Sin, Ethan Brand returns to find it was in his own heart all along: the cold, remorseless intellect that turned other souls into experiments. He faces down a jeering crowd of drunks, a showman with a diorama, and the father of the girl he ruined, then climbs onto the kiln at dawn and gives himself to the fire, leaving only a skeleton with a heart burned to marble.

title: Pierre et Jean
author: Guy de Maupassant
synopsis: A family friend leaves his entire fortune to the younger of two brothers, Jean, and the news curdles into suspicion in the mind of the elder, Dr. Pierre, who becomes convinced the bequest proves their mother once had an affair and that Jean is not their father's son. Pierre's jealousy and moral disgust wreck his own life as he circles the truth, needling his mother and brother until the family fractures, and he finally exiles himself to sea as a ship's doctor rather than live with what he's uncovered.

title: The Nether World
author: George Gissing
synopsis: In the slums of Clerkenwell, orphaned Jane Snowdon is rescued from her abusive guardians and taken in by her secretly wealthy grandfather Michael Snowdon, who wants her to spend his fortune on the poor. He dies before signing a new will, jeweler Sidney Kirkwood marries the embittered, acid-scarred Clara Hewett instead of Jane, and Clara's brother Bob dies fleeing arrest for coining forged money — leaving Jane to reject inherited money and marriage alike for a life of quiet, grinding toil among the poor she loves.

title: The Odd Women
author: George Gissing
synopsis: In late-Victorian London, sisters Alice and Virginia Madden scrape by as impoverished spinsters while their younger sister Monica marries the dull, jealous Widdowson out of sheer economic desperation. Meanwhile the fiercely independent Rhoda Nunn, who runs a school training women for clerical work, wrestles with her attraction to the charming but unreliable Everard Barfoot, testing whether a modern woman can have both principle and love.

title: Esther Waters
author: George Moore
synopsis: A servant girl seduced and abandoned by a fellow footman fights to keep her illegitimate son alive against workhouse threats, baby farms, and a lifetime of grinding domestic drudgery, while the racing-and-betting world that ruined her keeps dragging her back in.

title: Almayer's Folly
author: Joseph Conrad
synopsis: A failed Dutch trader rots away on the Borneo river of Sambir, chasing a dead man's rumor of gold while his half-Malay daughter Nina falls for the Balinese prince Dain Maroola. When Dutch gunboats close in on Dain and Nina chooses to flee with him, Almayer is left alone in his unfinished house, drowning his ruin in opium and denial.

title: The Beast in the Jungle
author: Henry James
synopsis: John Marcher confides to May Bartram his lifelong conviction that some rare, terrible fate is crouched in wait for him, and she quietly commits herself to watching beside him for it. Years pass in London as the two grow old together on the strength of this shared secret, Marcher too absorbed in his own impending doom to notice what he is actually failing to do. Only after May dies does Marcher grasp, standing at her grave, that the catastrophe he spent his life bracing for was the very love he let pass him by.

title: The Shepherd of the Hills
author: Harold Bell Wright
synopsis: A mysterious stranger calling himself Daniel Howitt settles among the Ozark backwoods folk, tutoring the wild, spirited Sammy Lane and befriending the giant-strong Young Matt while nursing a private grief that ties him to the mountain's darkest legend. As Sammy is torn between Matt's rough devotion and a smooth-talking suitor from the city, old secrets about a dead outlaw and a broken family surface, forcing the shepherd to confront the very tragedy that drove him into hiding.

title: Under Western Eyes
author: Joseph Conrad
synopsis: A St. Petersburg student, Razumov, betrays a fellow student who has just assassinated a government minister, then finds himself recruited as a spy among Genevan revolutionary exiles — including the dead man's sister, who has no idea who really doomed her brother.

title: Beau Geste
author: P.C. Wren
synopsis: When their aunt's priceless sapphire, the 'Blue Water,' vanishes, three brothers each vanish in turn to shield the others from suspicion, enlisting under false names in the French Foreign Legion. Years later a fellow officer arrives at a desert garrison to find every man of its besieged fort dead at his post and the fort's commander stabbed with no killer in sight, and pulls at the thread that unravels the brothers' sacrifice.

title: The Pathfinder
author: James Fenimore Cooper
synopsis: On the shores of Lake Ontario during the French and Indian War, frontier scout Natty Bumppo escorts Sergeant Dunham's daughter Mabel through hostile wilderness to her father's remote fort, and finds himself falling for her even as a scheming quartermaster and a young ship's master vie for her hand. When treachery among the garrison exposes a spy in their midst, Pathfinder must choose between the woman he loves and the solitary life of the forest he can never leave.

title: Phineas Redux
author: Anthony Trollope
synopsis: Phineas Finn returns to Parliament only to be framed for the murder of his rival Mr. Bonteen, and Trollope turns the back half of his Palliser series into a courtroom drama, with Madame Max Goesler racing to dig up the evidence that saves Phineas from the gallows.

title: The Duke's Children
author: Anthony Trollope
synopsis: Widowed Duke of Omnium Plantagenet Palliser tries to steer his three grown children away from marriages and habits he can't control: son Silverbridge switches political parties, wrecks money on a crooked racehorse partnership, and falls for an American commoner, Isabel Boncassen; daughter Mary refuses every suitor but the penniless Frank Tregear; and Gerald gambles his way out of Cambridge. The Duke's resistance crumbles chapter by chapter until he gives his blessing to the matches he once forbade.

title: Demos
author: George Gissing
synopsis: A working-class London radical unexpectedly inherits a Midlands ironmaster's fortune and land, and tries to build a socialist industrial community on it while his own vanity, an unhappy marriage of convenience, and old class loyalties corrode the project from within; his sudden violent death hands the estate back to the dispossessed gentry heir, who quietly undoes the socialist scheme and wins the woman his rival had married for status.

title: Born in Exile
author: George Gissing
synopsis: A brilliant, poor young scientist fakes a religious conversion to court a clergyman's daughter and buy his way into respectable society, but his hidden contempt for the faith he's performing eats at him until the deception collapses and strips him of the life he engineered. He drifts abroad in disgrace and dies alone, far from home.

title: The Black Robe
author: Wilkie Collins
synopsis: Wealthy, guilt-haunted Lewis Romayne kills a man in a duel and becomes the target of Father Benwell, a Jesuit who schemes to steer Romayne's fortune and his troubled marriage to Stella Eyrecourt toward the Church. Benwell's manipulations, built on a hidden connection between Stella and the dead man's widow, drive Romayne from his wife and child into the priesthood, wrecking the marriage he swore to protect.

title: Hereward the Wake
author: Charles Kingsley
synopsis: Hereward, exiled for his wild youth, fights as a mercenary across Flanders and Ireland before storming home when the Normans conquer England. He rallies Saxon outlaws in the Fens around Ely for a doomed guerrilla war against William the Conqueror, and ends his life broken and half-forgotten, a last relic of the England that vanished with Harold at Hastings.

title: Atlas Shrugged
author: Ayn Rand
synopsis: As American industry collapses under mounting collectivist regulation, railroad executive Dagny Taggart and steel magnate Hank Rearden fight to keep their businesses alive while the country's most capable minds mysteriously vanish one by one.

title: We the Living
author: Ayn Rand
synopsis: In Soviet Russia after the revolution, Kira Argounova fights to survive and stay true to herself while caught between a doomed aristocrat lover and the idealistic Communist officer who loves her.

title: East of Eden
author: John Steinbeck
synopsis: Two families, the Trasks and the Hamiltons, replay the Cain-and-Abel story across generations in California's Salinas Valley, as brothers compete for a father's love and a monstrous mother haunts the next generation.

title: Of Mice and Men
author: John Steinbeck
synopsis: Migrant ranch hands George Milton and the gentle, immensely strong Lennie Small dream of one day owning a small farm of their own, but Lennie's inability to control his strength brings their fragile hope to a tragic end during a season of work on a California ranch.

title: It
author: Stephen King
synopsis: Seven childhood friends in Derry, Maine face an ancient shape-shifting evil that preys on children, then reunite as adults thirty years later to finish what they started.

title: The Shining
author: Stephen King
synopsis: Aspiring writer Jack Torrance takes a winter caretaker job at the isolated, haunted Overlook Hotel with his wife and psychic young son, and the hotel's malevolent influence slowly consumes him.

title: The Quiet American
author: Graham Greene
synopsis: In 1950s Saigon, cynical British journalist Thomas Fowler watches an idealistic young American aid worker's theory-driven meddling in Vietnam's war curdle into disaster, entangled with both of them loving the same Vietnamese woman.

title: My Brilliant Friend
author: Elena Ferrante
synopsis: In 1950s Naples, Elena narrates her lifelong friendship and rivalry with the brilliant, volatile Lila, as the two girls claw their way toward an education and a way out of their impoverished, violent neighborhood.

title: The Godfather
author: Mario Puzo
synopsis: Vito Corleone rules one of New York's five Mafia families with quiet, ruthless authority, until an assassination attempt pulls his reluctant war-hero son Michael into the family business — and toward becoming the very thing he swore he'd never be.

title: Lord of the Flies
author: William Golding
synopsis: Stranded on a deserted island after a plane crash, a group of British schoolboys try to govern themselves — and descend into savagery as fear of a mythical "beast" takes hold.

title: The Fountainhead
author: Ayn Rand
synopsis: Uncompromising architect Howard Roark refuses to bend his individualist vision to please clients, critics, or the conformist tastes of the establishment, colliding with a rival architect, a newspaper tycoon, and a critic determined to destroy him.

title: Interview with the Vampire
author: Anne Rice
synopsis: A vampire named Louis recounts his two-century existence to a young reporter — his transformation by the charismatic and cruel Lestat, his doomed love for the child-vampire Claudia, and his search across Europe for others of his kind and some meaning in his damnation.

title: Night
author: Elie Wiesel
synopsis: Elie Wiesel's spare memoir of his teenage years in the Auschwitz and Buchenwald concentration camps, where he watched his family and his faith be destroyed.

title: Stoner
author: John Williams
synopsis: William Stoner, a Missouri farm boy who discovers literature almost by accident, spends a quiet, largely unnoticed life teaching English at the University of Missouri, sustained through a loveless marriage and departmental cruelty by his devotion to scholarship.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
synopsis: In Depression-era Alabama, young Scout Finch watches her father Atticus defend a Black man falsely accused of rape, while she and her brother Jem untangle their own fears about the reclusive neighbor Boo Radley.

title: Our Man in Havana
author: Graham Greene
synopsis: A hapless vacuum-cleaner salesman in pre-revolutionary Havana is recruited by British intelligence and, to keep the checks coming, invents an entire network of fictitious agents and diagrams of secret weapons out of vacuum-cleaner parts — until his fabrications start coming true.

title: The Man in the High Castle
author: Philip K. Dick
synopsis: In an alternate 1962 where the Axis powers won World War II, a divided America under Japanese and Nazi occupation is unsettled by a banned novel imagining a world where the Allies won instead.

title: A Separate Peace
author: John Knowles
synopsis: At a New England boarding school during the early years of World War II, the quiet, competitive Gene Forrester and his magnetic, athletic best friend Phineas share an idyllic summer that ends the moment Gene's jealousy leads to a single, irreversible act.

title: Doctor Sleep
author: Stephen King
synopsis: Decades after surviving the Overlook Hotel as a boy, Dan Torrance is a recovering alcoholic working hospice care when he telepathically befriends Abra Stone, a girl with psychic gifts far stronger than his own — and draws the attention of a cult of quasi-immortals who feed on children like her.

title: Shogun
author: James Clavell
synopsis: Shipwrecked English pilot John Blackthorne is stranded in feudal Japan in 1600, where he becomes entangled in the political maneuvering of the warlord Toranaga as the country lurches toward civil war, learning its language, customs, and the price of loyalty along the way.

title: The Pillars of the Earth
author: Ken Follett
synopsis: Across decades of civil war in twelfth-century England, a master builder, a disgraced monk-turned-prior, and a headstrong noblewoman fight to raise a great Gothic cathedral in the fictional town of Kingsbridge, against a scheming bishop and a family bent on ruin.

title: The Princess Bride
author: William Goldman
synopsis: Framed as an abridgment of a beloved old adventure novel, Goldman's tale follows farm girl Buttercup and her true love Westley through pirates, giants, swordsmen, and a scheming prince, narrated with constant winking commentary from the "abridger" himself.

title: The Thorn Birds
author: Colleen McCullough
synopsis: Across three generations on a vast Australian sheep station, Meggie Cleary's lifelong, forbidden love for the ambitious priest Ralph de Bricassart shapes and scars the Cleary family from the outback to Rome.

title: The Unbearable Lightness of Being
author: Milan Kundera
synopsis: Against the backdrop of the Prague Spring and its crushing, a womanizing surgeon, his wife, his mistress, and her lover pursue love, betrayal, and the meaning of a life that happens only once — narrated by an author who keeps interrupting to test his characters against Nietzsche's eternal return.

title: We Have Always Lived in the Castle
author: Shirley Jackson
synopsis: Eighteen-year-old Merricat Blackwood lives in isolation with her sister Constance and ailing Uncle Julian, the only survivors of a family poisoning years before — until a money-hungry cousin arrives and the villagers' hostility boils over.

title: Perfume: The Story of a Murderer
author: Patrick Süskind
synopsis: Born with a superhuman sense of smell but no scent of his own, Jean-Baptiste Grenouille rises from the stench of 18th-century Paris to become a perfumer obsessed with capturing the ultimate scent — the smell of a beautiful young woman — whatever the cost.

title: Butcher's Crossing
author: John Williams
synopsis: A Harvard dropout heads west to join a buffalo-hunting expedition into the Colorado Territory, seeking some idea of unspoiled nature that the brutal, wasteful slaughter and a killing winter methodically strip away.

title: Augustus
author: John Williams
synopsis: Told through invented letters, journals, and memoranda, this novel traces the life of Octavius Caesar from the murder of his great-uncle Julius Caesar through decades of war and rule as Rome's first emperor, ending in the private grief and isolation behind his public triumph.

title: Demon Copperhead
author: Barbara Kingsolver
synopsis: Born to a teenage single mother in a trailer in the Appalachian mountains of Virginia, red-haired Damon "Demon" Copperhead survives foster care, child labor, addiction, and the collapse of everyone he loves — narrating his own hard-luck rise with grim wit and stubborn hope. A modern retelling of David Copperfield transplanted to the opioid-crisis-era rural South.

title: The Pearl
author: John Steinbeck
synopsis: A poor pearl diver named Kino finds an extraordinary pearl that promises to lift his family out of poverty, but its discovery brings only greed, violence, and ruin down on him, his wife Juana, and their infant son.

title: Tortilla Flat
author: John Steinbeck
synopsis: In the hills above Monterey, the amiable paisano Danny inherits two small houses and gathers a band of loyal, wine-loving friends around him, whose loose, Round-Table-like fellowship comes undone once ease and property enter their lives.

title: The Third Man
author: Graham Greene
synopsis: Pulp novelist Rollo Martins arrives in postwar, occupied Vienna to find his old friend Harry Lime freshly dead — and the circumstances of the death, and of Harry himself, far murkier than they first appear.

title: The Comedians
author: Graham Greene
synopsis: Returning to Papa Doc Duvalier's Haiti to sell his empty hotel, the cynical Brown finds himself entangled with a British couple posing as a presidential candidate and his wife, an idealistic American vegetarian activist, and the doomed resistance to a regime built on terror.

title: King Rat
author: James Clavell
synopsis: In a Japanese POW camp in Singapore during WWII, an enterprising American corporal known as the King runs a black-market empire that keeps him better fed and housed than any officer, while a British flight lieutenant, Peter Marlowe, is drawn into an uneasy friendship and partnership with him.

title: The Family
author: Mario Puzo
synopsis: Mario Puzo's final novel, completed by Carol Gino after his death, follows Pope Alexander VI (Rodrigo Borgia) and his children Cesare and Lucrezia as they scheme, seduce, and murder their way to dominance over Renaissance Italy.

title: The Days of Abandonment
author: Elena Ferrante
synopsis: When her husband abandons her and their two children for a younger woman, Olga's carefully composed life in Turin unravels over one suffocating August, as grief and rage curdle into something closer to derangement.

title: Sweet Thursday
author: John Steinbeck
synopsis: Back from the war, Doc finds Cannery Row changed and himself lonely, until Fauna, the new madam of the Bear Flag, decides to matchmake him with an ex-prostitute named Suzy — with Mack and the boys throwing a chaotic costume party to help things along.

title: The Red Pony
author: John Steinbeck
synopsis: In four linked stories set on a California ranch, young Jody Tiflin learns about life, death, and the limits of his parents' love through a series of animals — a red pony, an old paint horse, and the promise of a new colt.

title: The Wayward Bus
author: John Steinbeck
synopsis: A busload of mismatched passengers is stranded together after a flash flood traps their driver's makeshift detour off the highway, and the forced intimacy of the night strips away each one's polite self-deception about who they really are.

title: The Sicilian
author: Mario Puzo
synopsis: In the years after WWII, Michael Corleone is sent back to Sicily to bring home the legendary bandit Salvatore Giuliano — a Robin Hood figure to the peasantry, hunted by the state and used as a pawn by the Mafia's Don Croce, whose fate turns out to be already sealed before Michael arrives.

title: A Gun for Sale
author: Graham Greene
synopsis: A hired killer named Raven tracks the man who paid him in stolen, marked banknotes across a blacked-out English city, dragging a chorus girl witness into a plot that reaches all the way to a European war being engineered for profit.

title: Monsignor Quixote
author: Graham Greene
synopsis: A humble Spanish parish priest, unexpectedly elevated to monsignor and convinced he is descended from Cervantes' Don Quixote, sets off on a rambling road trip across Spain in a battered old car with his Communist ex-mayor friend, debating faith and politics along the way.

title: The Honorary Consul
author: Graham Greene
synopsis: In a provincial Argentine river town, a kidnapping meant for the American ambassador snags the wrong man — a boozy, aging honorary consul — and drags a local doctor into a doomed hostage standoff run by his own boyhood friend, now a defrocked priest turned guerrilla.

title: The Man Within
author: Graham Greene
synopsis: Andrews, a young smuggler who has betrayed his own gang out of self-loathing, flees across the Sussex Downs and takes refuge with a solitary woman, Elizabeth, as his former friends close in and his trial for the betrayal approaches.

title: The Outsider
author: Stephen King
synopsis: A beloved Little League coach is arrested for the brutal murder of a boy, with overwhelming forensic evidence and dozens of witnesses placing him at the scene — except he was also, provably, one hundred miles away at the time, forcing detective Ralph Anderson and investigator Holly Gibney to consider an explanation beyond reason.

title: The Haunting of Hill House
author: Shirley Jackson
synopsis: Four strangers gather at the notoriously haunted Hill House for a summer of paranormal investigation, and the fragile, lonely Eleanor Vance finds the house's attentions turning on her alone.

title: The Lottery and Other Stories
author: Shirley Jackson
synopsis: Twenty-five stories, from the quietly sinister to the openly strange, collected around the title story's small-town ritual of annual, communal violence.

title: Dark Tales
author: Shirley Jackson
synopsis: A posthumous collection of Shirley Jackson's uncanny short fiction, gathering seventeen stories of quiet dread, domestic menace, and small-town cruelty — including 'The Possibility of Evil' and 'Louisa, Please Come Home.'

title: The Institute
author: Stephen King
synopsis: Twelve-year-old genius Luke Ellis is kidnapped in the night and wakes up in a facility that looks like his old bedroom but isn't — a covert institute that harvests psychic children for a purpose none of them fully understand, until a former cop stumbles onto the truth from the outside.

title: The Claiming of Sleeping Beauty
author: Anne Rice
synopsis: In this erotic retelling written under the pen name A. N. Roquelaure, a prince conquers the sleeping kingdom by waking Beauty with a kiss, then carries her off to his own realm to be trained in obedience and desire alongside a court of other captive princes and princesses.

title: Heart of a Dog
author: Mikhail Bulgakov
synopsis: A brilliant Moscow surgeon transplants human glands into a stray dog, transforming it into a foul-mouthed, Soviet-minded man named Sharikov — a creation that quickly outgrows its creator's control and threatens to take over his apartment and his life.

title: The White Guard
author: Mikhail Bulgakov
synopsis: As Kyiv changes hands amid the chaos of the Russian Civil War, the Turbin siblings and their circle of friends try to hold onto loyalty, love, and a sense of home while armies, ideologies, and the city itself collapse around them.

title: Black Snow
author: Mikhail Bulgakov
synopsis: A struggling Moscow writer, Maksudov, turns his unpublishable novel into a play and is drawn into the vain, backbiting, superstition-ridden world of the Independent Theatre, whose legendary director stages everything except the play as written.

title: It's a Battlefield
author: Graham Greene
synopsis: After a Communist bus driver named Drover is condemned to death for killing a policeman during a riot, an Assistant Commissioner of Police, a Communist Party official, a young idealist, and Drover's own wife each circle the case in London, revealing how little any of them can actually change its outcome.

title: Burning Bright
author: John Steinbeck
synopsis: In this experimental "play-novelette," the aging circus performer Joe Saul, desperate for a child of his own, is unknowingly given one when his wife Mordeen conceives with another man to spare him the grief of his sterility — and the same three archetypal characters recur across a circus, a farm, and a ship to play out the same moral dilemma.

title: Morphine
author: Mikhail Bulgakov
synopsis: Told through a dead colleague's diary, a young country doctor recounts his own rapid descent into morphine addiction after first using the drug to relieve a nervous pain.

title: Gai-Jin
author: James Clavell
synopsis: In 1862 Japan, foreign traders and diplomats in the port of Yokohama scramble for advantage amid samurai plots, assassination, and a xenophobic shogunate on the edge of civil war, while young heir Malcolm Struan and French orphan Angelique Richaud fall into a doomed romance at the center of it all.

title: Noble House
author: James Clavell
synopsis: Over one turbulent week in 1963 Hong Kong, tai-pan Ian Dunross fights to save the storied trading house Struan's from a hostile raid by his rival Quillan Gornt, while American financiers, Soviet spies, and old feuds between founding families all converge on the colony at once.

title: Tai-Pan
author: James Clavell
synopsis: In 1841, Dirk Struan, the ruthless "tai-pan" of the trading house Noble House, fights to found the new colony of Hong Kong and secure his family's fortune against pirates, rival traders, plague, and the vengeful Brock family.

title: Whirlwind
author: James Clavell
synopsis: As the Iranian Revolution erupts around them, the Scottish helicopter pilots of S-G Helicopters race to fly their fleet and crews out of the country before the fanatics, the KGB, and the collapsing old regime catch up with them.

title: The Lying Life of Adults
author: Elena Ferrante
synopsis: After overhearing her father compare her to a hated, disfigured aunt, twelve-year-old Giovanna seeks out that aunt in Naples's rougher outskirts and discovers a version of her family's history, and of herself, that unravels everything she thought she knew about her parents' marriage.

title: The Story of a New Name
author: Elena Ferrante
synopsis: Lila's disastrous marriage to Stefano collapses under an affair with Nino, the boy both women have loved since childhood, while Elena buries herself in her studies and a engagement of her own, each woman's escape from the neighborhood costing her something the other envies.

title: Those Who Leave and Those Who Stay
author: Elena Ferrante
synopsis: As Elena publishes her first novel and marries into a prestigious Milanese family, Lila works brutal factory hours in Naples and is drawn into the city's labor unrest — their friendship stretching across widening distances of class, ambition, and the turbulent politics of 1970s Italy.

title: The Story of the Lost Child
author: Elena Ferrante
synopsis: In the fourth and final Neapolitan novel, Elena returns to Naples with her daughters as her decades-long entanglement with Lila comes full circle, culminating in the disappearance of Lila's young daughter Tina — a loss that reshapes both women's lives and the meaning of their friendship.

title: Against Interpretation and Other Essays
author: Susan Sontag
synopsis: Sontag's landmark essay collection, spanning film, theater, and literature criticism written in the early-to-mid 1960s, that argues against reductive interpretation in favor of attending to art's form and sensuous surface — and introduces her concept of "Camp" to American criticism.

title: Notes on Camp
author: Susan Sontag
synopsis: In fifty-eight numbered notes, Sontag defines and defends Camp as a sensibility — a taste for the exaggerated, the artificial, and the failed-seriousness of things — tracing it through opera, film, furniture, and literature.

title: On Women
author: Susan Sontag
synopsis: A posthumous collection of Susan Sontag's essays, interviews, and letters on beauty, aging, fascism, and feminism, spanning from the 1970s through the end of her career.

title: The Art of Nonfiction
author: Ayn Rand
synopsis: A posthumously edited transcript of Ayn Rand's 1969 course on nonfiction writing, walking through subject selection, outlining, drafting, and style with examples drawn from her own published essays and articles.

title: The Art of Fiction
author: Ayn Rand
synopsis: Assembled from Ayn Rand's own 1958 lecture notes on the craft of fiction writing, this posthumously published guide walks through theme, plot, characterization, and style, dissecting real novels line by line — including her own — to show what separates the Romantic from the Naturalistic writer.

title: Journey Without Maps
author: Graham Greene
synopsis: Greene's account of an arduous, half-mapped trek through Sierra Leone and Liberia in 1935, walking for weeks through remote bush villages with his cousin Barbara and a train of native carriers, in search of something he can never quite name.

title: In Search of a Character
author: Graham Greene
synopsis: Two journals from Graham Greene's travels in West and Central Africa — a wartime Atlantic convoy and, more centrally, a 1959 trip to a Belgian Congo leper colony — kept while he was forming the novel that became A Burnt-Out Case.

title: Diaboliad
author: Mikhail Bulgakov
synopsis: A mild-mannered Moscow clerk named Korotkov is fired over a bureaucratic mix-up with his own name, then chased through an ever-multiplying, nightmarishly reduplicating Soviet office hierarchy in a futile attempt to get his job back.

author: David McCullough
synopsis: Narrative history of the year 1776, following George Washington and the Continental Army from the siege of Boston through the disastrous defense of New York, the retreat across New Jersey, and the crossing of the Delaware to the counterstrokes at Trenton and Princeton.

title: 21 Lessons for the 21st Century
author: Yuval Noah Harari
synopsis: A collection of essays on how technological disruption, biotechnology, and artificial intelligence are undermining the political and religious stories that structured twentieth-century life, covering topics from work and data to nationalism, immigration, terrorism, and post-truth politics.

title: A Little Life
author: Hanya Yanagihara
synopsis: Four college friends—Willem, JB, Malcolm, and Jude—build careers and share an apartment in New York, and the novel widens over decades into the backstory of Jude St. Francis, a lawyer whose ruined legs, scarred body, and secret cutting trace back to abuse by Brother Luke at a monastery and years of exploitation before he was taken in by his law professor Harold.

title: A Mercy
author: Toni Morrison
synopsis: In 1680s colonial Virginia, the trader Jacob Vaark takes in Florens, an enslaved girl offered to him by her mother in payment of a debt, to join the household of women bound to his remote farm. Told in shifting first-person voices, the novel traces how Jacob's death from smallpox and the fragile bonds among these women unravel the household, while Florens searches for the free black blacksmith she loves.

title: A People's History of the United States
author: Howard Zinn
synopsis: A narrative history of the United States running from Columbus's 1492 landing through the 2000 election, told deliberately from the standpoint of Arawaks, indentured servants and slaves, industrial workers, immigrants, women, and dissenters rather than the 'Founding Fathers,' generals, and presidents who usually anchor textbook accounts.

title: A Raisin in the Sun
author: Lorraine Hansberry
synopsis: The Younger family in 1950s Chicago clashes over what to do with a $10,000 life-insurance check, as son Walter's dream of a liquor-store investment collides with his mother's plan to buy a house in the white neighborhood of Clybourne Park.

title: A Short History of Nearly Everything
author: Bill Bryson
synopsis: Bryson traces how scientists pieced together the history of the universe, the Earth, and life itself, from Darwin's On the Origin of Species through geology, chemistry, and paleontology, dwelling on the eccentric, often overlooked people who made the discoveries.

title: A Thousand Splendid Suns
author: Khaled Hosseini
synopsis: Mariam, an illegitimate girl married off to the abusive shoemaker Rasheed, and Laila, a younger neighbor forced into the same marriage after losing her family and her love Tariq to war, forge a fierce bond as they endure decades of violence and upheaval in Kabul.

title: A Walk to Remember
author: Nicholas Sparks
synopsis: In 1958 Beaufort, North Carolina, minister's daughter Jamie Sullivan draws reluctant high school senior Landon Carter into her Christmas play and her Bible readings, and he falls for her as she conceals that she is dying of leukemia.

title: A Man Called Ove
author: Fredrik Backman
synopsis: Ove, a rigid fifty-nine-year-old widower obsessed with rules and his Saab, keeps having his repeated suicide attempts interrupted by a pregnant new neighbor, her family, and a stray cat that gradually pull him back into life.

title: A Walk in the Woods: Rediscovering America on the Appalachian Trail
author: Bill Bryson
synopsis: A middle-aged travel writer resolves to hike all 2,100-plus miles of the Appalachian Trail from Georgia to Maine with his out-of-shape, recovering-alcoholic old friend Katz, and the two stumble through blizzards, bears, exhaustion, and the trail's oddball hikers and towns while never quite making it the whole way.

title: Alias Grace
author: Margaret Atwood
synopsis: A convicted servant-girl in 1850s Canada, imprisoned since sixteen for the axe-murder of her employer and his housekeeper-mistress, is interviewed by a young doctor probing her patchy, contradictory memories of the killings while she recalls her immigrant childhood and the fatal household she worked in before the crime.

title: All the Light We Cannot See
author: Anthony Doerr
synopsis: A blind French girl hides in her great-uncle's house in besieged Saint-Malo with a legendary cursed diamond, while a German orphan boy conscripted into the Wehrmacht for his gift with radios is sent to hunt the Resistance transmission she depends on, their paths converging as Allied bombs fall on the walled city in August 1944.

title: All the Pretty Horses
author: Cormac McCarthy
synopsis: After his grandfather's death and the loss of the family ranch, teenage John Grady Cole leaves West Texas on horseback with his friend Rawlins, crossing into Mexico where a runaway boy named Blevins draws them into trouble with the rurales and John Grady falls for the daughter of a wealthy hacienda owner.

title: American Pastoral
author: Philip Roth
synopsis: Narrator Nathan Zuckerman reconstructs the life of Seymour 'Swede' Levov, the golden athlete of Weequahic's Jewish community who inherits his father's Newark glove factory and builds a seemingly ideal life, only to have it shattered when his stuttering teenage daughter Merry bombs the local general store and post office in protest of the Vietnam War, killing a man and vanishing underground.

title: Anathem
author: Neal Stephenson
synopsis: On the planet Arbre, a young monk-like scholar cloistered in a walled mathematical community is drawn out into the wider world when an alien starship enters orbit, forcing the secular authorities and the sequestered orders of philosophers to confront a threat neither can handle alone.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
synopsis: Ten strangers, each secretly guilty of a death they've escaped punishment for, are lured to an isolated island off the Devon coast, where an unseen accuser broadcasts their crimes and murders them one by one in the pattern of an old nursery rhyme.

title: Angela's Ashes
author: Frank McCourt
synopsis: A memoir of a childhood spent in Depression-era Brooklyn and then Limerick, Ireland, where poverty, a drunken father, dead infant siblings, and a devoutly Catholic upbringing shape a boy's slow, resourceful climb toward escaping back to America.

title: Angels & Demons
author: Dan Brown
synopsis: After a CERN physicist is branded with an ambigram and murdered, Harvard symbologist Robert Langdon and physicist Vittoria Vetra race across Rome to stop the resurrected Illuminati from detonating stolen antimatter beneath the Vatican during a papal conclave.

title: Another Country
author: James Baldwin
synopsis: A Black jazz musician in New York self-destructs through an abusive affair with a white woman and jumps off the George Washington Bridge, and his death exposes the tangled, interracial, and bisexual relationships among the friends and sister he leaves behind in Greenwich Village and beyond.

title: Astrophysics for People in a Hurry
author: Neil deGrasse Tyson
synopsis: A concise tour through modern astrophysics, from the Big Bang and the formation of matter through dark matter, dark energy, the electromagnetic spectrum, and the planets of the solar system, closing with reflections on humanity's cosmic perspective.

title: Atonement
author: Ian McEwan
synopsis: In the summer of 1935, thirteen-year-old Briony Tallis misinterprets an encounter between her sister Cecilia and the housekeeper's son Robbie Turner, then falsely accuses Robbie of a crime, sending him to prison and later to war, a lie whose consequences Briony spends the rest of her life trying to atone for as a novelist rewriting the truth.

title: Books: A Memoir
author: Larry McMurtry
synopsis: The novelist-turned-antiquarian-bookseller traces his life from a bookless Texas ranch childhood through decades of scouting, buying, and dealing rare books at his Georgetown and Archer City shops, Booked Up.

title: The Baron in the Trees
author: Italo Calvino
synopsis: After a childhood quarrel with his father, young Cosimo Piovasco di Rondò climbs into the trees of his family's Ligurian estate and vows never to set foot on the ground again, living out the rest of his life aloft while hunting, reading Enlightenment texts, corresponding with Diderot, falling for a girl named Viola, and getting drawn into the political upheavals of his era from among the branches.

title: Carrie
author: Stephen King
synopsis: Carrie White, a bullied high-school outcast raised by a fanatically religious mother, discovers she has telekinetic powers after her first period triggers a humiliating locker-room hazing; when a prom-night prank goes wrong she turns her power on the town of Chamberlain, Maine. The novel is assembled from Carrie's own narrative interwoven with fictional news clippings, letters, and excerpts from a post-disaster commission report and memoirs by survivors like Susan Snell.

title: Caste: The Origins of Our Discontents
author: Isabel Wilkerson
synopsis: Wilkerson argues that a rigid, largely unspoken caste system, not simply racism, structures American life, and traces its architecture through eight shared pillars found also in the Indian caste system and Nazi Germany's race laws. The book moves between historical case studies (Nazi officials studying American segregation statutes, a schoolteacher's blue-eyed/brown-eyed classroom experiment) and analysis of contemporary events like the police killing of Freddie Gray.

title: Child of God
author: Cormac McCarthy
synopsis: Lester Ballard, dispossessed of his family's Tennessee farm and increasingly shunned by his community, descends into squatting in caves, scavenging, and eventually necrophilia and murder, narrated in spare prose interspersed with the recollections of local townspeople.

title: China Rich Girlfriend
author: Kevin Kwan
synopsis: As Rachel Chu prepares to marry Nick Young, she learns the identity of her long-lost biological father, a mainland Chinese billionaire, and is pulled into the rivalries, scandals, and extravagant spending of Shanghai and Hong Kong's ultra-wealthy alongside Nick's cousin Astrid and the social-climbing Kitty Pong. A running thread involves Kitty's new sister-in-law Colette assigning her a strict etiquette and literary reading curriculum to remake her into old-money society.

title: Cities of the Plain
author: Cormac McCarthy
synopsis: Cowboys John Grady Cole and Billy Parham, now working a New Mexico ranch near the Texas border in the early 1950s, cross into Juárez where John Grady falls for a young epileptic prostitute named Magdalena, setting the pair against a violent pimp. The novel closes the Border Trilogy begun in All the Pretty Horses and The Crossing.

title: The Common Reader: Second Series
author: Virginia Woolf
synopsis: A collection of essays, most first published in periodicals like the Times Literary Supplement and The Nation, in which Woolf writes about English writers and books from the Elizabethans through her own contemporaries, discussing figures such as Sidney, Donne, Defoe, Sterne, Swift, Chesterfield, De Quincey, Cowper, Hazlitt, the Brontes' circle, Elizabeth Barrett Browning, George Gissing, George Meredith, Christina Rossetti, and Thomas Hardy, and closing with an essay on how one should read a book.

title: Congo
author: Michael Crichton
synopsis: In 1979 a corporate-funded expedition led by geologist Karen Ross, primatologist Peter Elliot, his sign-language-trained gorilla Amy, and mercenary guide Charles Munro races into the Zairean rain forest to find a lost city called Zinj and its fabled diamond deposits, following the trail of a previous expedition wiped out by a mysterious force.

title: Contact
author: Carl Sagan
synopsis: Radio astronomer Ellie Arroway leads the SETI-derived Project Argus team that detects and decodes an extraterrestrial signal from Vega, a discovery that leads to construction of an enigmatic interstellar Machine and to Ellie's own journey through it, forcing her and the world to reckon with the boundaries between science, faith, and the numinous.

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
synopsis: A sweeping popular-science tour of the universe and the history of science, tracing astronomy and cosmology from ancient Ionia and the Library of Alexandria through Kepler, Newton, and Einstein to modern space exploration, while weaving in reflections on the scientific method, the search for extraterrestrial life, and the dangers of nuclear war.

title: Crazy Rich Asians
author: Kevin Kwan
synopsis: When American-born Chinese economics professor Rachel Chu travels to Singapore with her boyfriend Nick Young to attend his best friend's wedding, she discovers he belongs to one of Asia's wealthiest, most status-obsessed families, and must navigate the opulence, gossip, and disapproval of his mother Eleanor and the extended Young-Shang-T'sien clan.

title: Daisy Jones & The Six
author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
synopsis: An oral-history-style novel that reconstructs, through interwoven first-person interview testimony from band members, family, and industry figures, the rise of 1970s rock band Daisy Jones & The Six and the affair, addiction, and creative tensions between singer Daisy Jones and bandleader Billy Dunne that led to the group's abrupt on-stage breakup in Chicago in 1979.

title: Death on the Nile
author: Agatha Christie
synopsis: Heiress Linnet Ridgeway marries Simon Doyle, the former fiancé of her friend Jacqueline de Bellefort, and the newlyweds find Jacqueline pursuing them on their Egyptian honeymoon aboard a Nile steamer; when Linnet is shot dead in her cabin, Hercule Poirot investigates the passengers to find the killer.

title: Death's End
author: Cixin Liu
synopsis: Half a century after the Doomsday Battle, aerospace engineer Cheng Xin wakes from hibernation into the Deterrence Era, in which the threat of mutually-assured destruction between Earth and the Trisolaran invaders has kept an uneasy peace; she inherits the "Swordholder" role controlling humanity's broadcast deterrent, and the narrative follows her choices (and the coded fairy tales sent by Yun Tianming) across the fall of deterrence, humanity's exile to Australia and later the Bunker and Broadcast Eras, and on toward the fate of the solar system.

title: Deception
author: Philip Roth
synopsis: A novel told almost entirely in overheard dialogue between a writer named Philip and his English mistress in London, moving between their pillow talk, arguments about jealousy and fidelity, and his account of researching a biography of the reclusive writer Lonoff whose widow blocked him at every turn; the book ends with the lover confronting him after reading his manuscript about their affair.

title: Difficult Loves
author: Italo Calvino
synopsis: A collection of short stories grouped by period (Riviera Stories, Wartime Stories, Postwar Stories, and Stories of Love and Loneliness), moving between prewar Ligurian coastal boyhood scenes, wartime partisan skirmishes and Allied-occupation port life, and later solitary character studies — a soldier, a bather, a clerk, a reader, a poet — each caught in a single charged encounter or moment of near-connection, rendered through closely observed physical and sensory detail.

title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
author: Philip K. Dick
synopsis: Bounty hunter Rick Deckard, whose wife Iran dials her moods on a Penfield mood organ and who keeps a fake electric sheep because a real animal is beyond his means, is assigned to retire a group of escaped Nexus-6 androids, including Rachael Rosen, Roy and Irmgard Baty, and opera singer Luba Luft, whose deaths leave him shaken and questioning what separates him from them.

title: East, West
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: A three-part story collection moving between the subcontinent and the West, retelling Hamlet's gravedigger Yorick as a jester in old Denmark, following Christopher Columbus's years of courting Queen Isabella for patronage, and tracing immigrant friendships and marriages such as those of Chekov and Zulu and the porter Mecir.

title: Ender's Game
author: Orson Scott Card
synopsis: Child prodigy Ender Wiggin is pushed through Battle School's zero-gravity war games, eventually commanding the newly formed Dragon Army of green recruits, before being maneuvered into commanding the fleet that destroys the alien buggers, after which he travels the stars with his sister Valentine as a Speaker for the Dead.

title: Exit Ghost
author: Philip Roth
synopsis: After eleven years of rural seclusion, the aging, incontinent, impotent writer Nathan Zuckerman travels to Manhattan for a medical procedure, gets drawn into young biographer Richard Kliman's effort to expose a scandal about Zuckerman's late mentor E.I. Lonoff, and is overtaken by a futile infatuation with a much younger writer, Jamie Logan.

title: Exit West
author: Mohsin Hamid
synopsis: In an unnamed city sliding into civil war, Saeed and Nadia fall into a relationship and eventually pass through one of the mysterious doors that have begun appearing worldwide, doors that deposit refugees instantly in Mykonos, London, and finally San Francisco, while their bond slowly erodes as they remake themselves in each new place.

title: Fire from Heaven
author: Mary Renault
synopsis: A childhood-to-adolescence portrait of Alexander the Great growing up in the Macedonian court of his father Philip and his volatile mother Olympias, tutored by Aristotle at Mieza and bound to his lifelong companion Hephaistion, ending as Philip is assassinated and the young Alexander claims the throne.

title: Funeral Games
author: Mary Renault
synopsis: After Alexander the Great's death in Babylon, his generals Perdikkas, Ptolemy, Eumenes, Antigonos, and the rest tear his empire apart in years of shifting alliances, murders, and civil war, while his mother Olympias, his widow Roxane, and his half-witted half-brother Philip Arridaios become pawns and casualties of the succession struggle.

title: Fury
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: Malik Solanka, a retired Cambridge historian of ideas and dollmaker who has fled London for New York, tries to escape a rage he cannot explain while his creation Little Brain becomes a global media phenomenon and he is drawn into the affairs of Neela Mahendra and a revolution brewing on the fictional islands of Lilliput-Blefuscu.

title: God Help the Child
author: Toni Morrison
synopsis: Bride, a dark-skinned woman rejected in childhood by her light-skinned mother Sweetness for the color of her own skin, builds a glamorous cosmetics-executive life for herself in adulthood, but it begins to unravel after her lover Booker leaves her and she sets out to find him, uncovering both his and her own buried childhood wounds along the way.

title: Good Night, Mr. Wodehouse
author: Faith Sullivan
synopsis: Set in the small Minnesota town of Harvester from the early 1900s through the 1940s, the novel follows Nell Stillman through marriage, widowhood, and raising her son Hilly, with the comic novels of P. G. Wodehouse serving as a recurring source of comfort and escape through her hardships.

title: Grimus
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: Flapping Eagle, a Native American man granted immortality by a mysterious elixir, wanders the earth for centuries before following his equally immortal sister's trail to Calf Island, a fantastical, dimension-bending land ruled by the reclusive, godlike Grimus, whose power over reality and the island's inhabitants Flapping Eagle must ultimately confront.

title: Guns, Germs, and Steel: The Fates of Human Societies
author: Jared Diamond
synopsis: Diamond argues that the divergent historical trajectories of societies on different continents stem from geographic and environmental factors: the availability of domesticable plants and animals and continental axis orientation, which gave some regions a head start in food production leading to denser populations, epidemic diseases, writing, technology, and centralized political organization. The book traces this argument from the Cajamarca encounter between Pizarro and Atahuallpa through the origins of farming, livestock-borne germs, writing, and technology, then applies the framework to Polynesia, China, Eurasia, and Africa.

title: Homo Deus: A Brief History of Tomorrow
author: Yuval Noah Harari
synopsis: Harari argues that having largely tamed famine, plague, and war, humankind's next projects will be pursuing immortality, bliss, and divine-like power, tracing how the humanist belief in individual free will and inner experience may be superseded by dataism, biotechnology, and artificial intelligence.

title: How to Get Filthy Rich in Rising Asia
author: Mohsin Hamid
synopsis: A satirical self-help book narrated in second person that tracks an unnamed protagonist's rise from rural poverty in an unnamed South Asian country to wealth through bottled water and real-estate ventures, tracing his moves to the city, his education, work, romance with 'the pretty girl,' entanglements with violence and bureaucracy, and eventual old age and death.

title: If Beale Street Could Talk
author: James Baldwin
synopsis: Nineteen-year-old Tish Rivers narrates her efforts, alongside her family, to prove the innocence of her fiance Fonny Hunt, jailed in New York on a rape charge he did not commit, while she carries their child.

title: In Cold Blood
author: Truman Capote
synopsis: A nonfiction account of the November 1959 murder of the Clutter family in Holcomb, Kansas, reconstructing the crime, the investigation, and the capture, trial, and execution of killers Perry Smith and Dick Hickock through interviews with townspeople, investigators, and the killers themselves.

title: Interface
author: Stephen Bury
synopsis: After a stroke, Illinois governor William Cozzano is secretly fitted with a brain implant that lets political operatives feed him poll-tested responses in real time as he runs a manipulated presidential campaign.

title: Into the War
author: Italo Calvino
synopsis: Three autobiographical narratives set in San Remo in 1940, following the teenage narrator and his fellow Avanguardisti through Italy's entry into the Second World War, a stint helping evacuees in occupied Menton, and nights spent on anti-aircraft duty.

title: Italo Calvino
author: Martin McLaughlin
synopsis: A critical study tracing Calvino's career book by book, from the early short stories and The Path to the Spiders' Nests through the Our Ancestors trilogy, the Cosmicomic stories, Invisible Cities, and If on a Winter's Night a Traveller, situating each work within its literary influences and intertexts.

title: Jazz
author: Toni Morrison
synopsis: In 1926 Harlem, cosmetics salesman Joe Trace shoots his young lover Dorcas after she leaves him for someone else, and at the girl's funeral his wife Violet slashes the corpse's face with a knife.

title: Jurassic Park
author: Michael Crichton
synopsis: Paleontologist Alan Grant and a small group of scientists are invited to inspect billionaire John Hammond's island resort, where dinosaurs have been cloned from ancient DNA, just before the park's security systems fail and the animals get loose.

title: Letting Go
author: Philip Roth
synopsis: Gabe Wallach, a young academic in 1950s Chicago and New York, becomes entangled in the troubled marriage of his friends Paul and Libby Herz while avoiding commitments of his own.

title: Literary Life: A Second Memoir
author: Larry McMurtry
synopsis: McMurtry recounts his development as a novelist and man of letters, from his early influences and the writing of his first books through decades of reading, teaching, and the movie adaptations of his fiction.

title: Moth Smoke
author: Mohsin Hamid
synopsis: After losing his bank job in Lahore, Daru Shezad slides into drug use, petty crime, and an affair with Mumtaz, the wife of his wealthy best friend Ozi.

title: Mother Mary Comes to Me
author: Arundhati Roy
synopsis: Arundhati Roy's memoir traces her fraught, intense bond with her mother Mary Roy, a strong-willed school founder in Kerala, from a chaotic childhood in Ayemenem and Kottayam through Roy's own path into architecture, screenwriting, activism, and the writing of The God of Small Things and The Ministry of Utmost Happiness. The book closes with Roy reflecting on her mother's death and imagining her still walking the shoreline of memory.

title: Murder on the Orient Express
author: Agatha Christie
synopsis: When the Orient Express is stalled by snow in the Balkans, wealthy American passenger Ratchett is found stabbed to death in his locked compartment, and detective Hercule Poirot, who is aboard the same train, questions the twelve other passengers in the coach to determine who among them killed him.

title: My Name Is Red
author: Orhan Pamuk
synopsis: In 16th-century Istanbul, miniaturist and illuminator Enishte Effendi is commissioned to secretly illustrate a book for the Sultan in the Frankish style, and when one of the workshop's master miniaturists is found murdered, the narration passes between multiple voices — including the corpse, the murderer, Enishte's daughter Shekure, her suitor Black, and the miniaturists Master Osman, Butterfly, Stork, and Olive — as they piece together who among the illustrators is the killer.

title: Nemesis
author: Philip Roth
synopsis: Set in Newark in the summer of 1944, the novel follows playground director Bucky Cantor as a polio epidemic spreads through his Jewish neighborhood, forcing him to weigh his duty to the children under his care against an offer to join his fiancée Marcia at a Pocono Mountains summer camp, Indian Hill. The narrative moves between the fear and death on the Chancellor Avenue playground and camp life at Indian Hill, including Indian Night ceremonies and a climactic javelin-throwing scene.

title: Nights of Plague
author: Orhan Pamuk
synopsis: Presented as a historian's edition of Princess Pakize's letters, the novel follows the Ottoman-era plague outbreak of 1901 on the fictional Mediterranean island of Mingheria, where Doctor Nuri and Princess Pakize navigate quarantine measures, the murder of the Sultan's Royal Chemist Bonkowski Pasha, and the political unraveling that leads to Mingheria's revolution and declared independence under Commander Kâmil.

title: On James Baldwin
author: Colm Tóibín
