synopsis: Colm Tóibín weaves his own history of reading James Baldwin, beginning with Go Tell It on the Mountain at eighteen, into a critical and biographical account of Baldwin's fiction, essays, and public life — his novels, his years in Paris and Harlem, his friendships and rivalries with writers like Richard Wright and Norman Mailer, and his civil-rights-era encounters with figures such as Robert Kennedy and Malcolm X.

title: On Literature
author: Umberto Eco
synopsis: A collection of Eco's occasional essays and lectures on literature, ranging from Dante's Paradiso and Aristotle's Poetics to his own novels, tracing the social functions of literature, the practice of intertextual irony, and his personal debts to writers like Borges.

title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
author: Ken Kesey
synopsis: Narrated by Chief Bromden, a large half-Indian patient who feigns deafness and muteness on a psychiatric ward run by the controlling Big Nurse (Ratched), the novel follows Randle McMurphy, a brash new patient who challenges her authority through card games, a deep-sea fishing trip, and a late-night party, provoking escalating retaliation including electroshock and lobotomy.

title: Our Gang
author: Philip Roth
synopsis: A satirical send-up of a Nixon-like president called Tricky Dixon, told through interviews, press conferences, and dialogue: he defends his stance on 'sanctity of human life' while dodging on Vietnam and Cambodia, gets ambushed by advisers deciding whom to blame for domestic unrest, is implicated in the disappearance of baseball player Curt Flood, and is eventually assassinated and sent to Hell, where he runs for office against Satan.

title: Outer Dark
author: Cormac McCarthy
synopsis: In backwoods Appalachia, Culla Holme fathers a child with his sister Rinthy and abandons it in the woods, telling her it died; when she discovers the truth and sets off searching for the baby and the tinker who took it, Culla wanders separately through a landscape of hangings, a turpentine camp, and a marauding trio of drifters who eventually murder the child before Culla's eyes.

title: Pachinko
author: Min Jin Lee
synopsis: A multigenerational saga following a Korean family, beginning with Sunja, a fisherman's daughter in Japanese-occupied Korea who bears a child out of wedlock, as they emigrate to Osaka and struggle across decades as ethnic Korean outsiders in Japan, with sons Noa and Mozasu taking divergent paths through education and the pachinko business.

title: Paradise
author: Toni Morrison
synopsis: A group of armed men from the all-Black town of Ruby, Oklahoma raid a nearby former convent to kill or drive out the women sheltering there, and the novel moves between the men's rationalizations, voiced partly through Reverend Richard Misner's doubts about the town's hardening insularity, and the convent women's interwoven backstories, closing on an ocean vision of a woman named Piedade singing to a rescued companion.

title: Patrimony: A True Story
author: Philip Roth
synopsis: Philip Roth recounts the final two years of his elderly father Herman Roth's life in Elizabeth, New Jersey, from the 1989 diagnosis of a brain tumor through a decision against surgery, a swallowing crisis, and his death, interwoven with Newark childhood stories, the family shaving mug, and Roth's own emergency heart bypass during the same period.

title: People of the Book
author: Geraldine Brooks
synopsis: Book conservator Hanna Heath is brought to Sarajevo to examine and stabilize the illuminated Sarajevo Haggadah after it is rescued from the museum, and the physical clues she finds in its binding and stains, an insect wing, wine stains, salt, a white hair, trigger interleaved historical narratives tracing the manuscript's path back through Vienna, Venice, Tarragona, and fifteenth-century Seville.

title: A Promised Land
author: Barack Obama
synopsis: Obama's memoir of his early political rise and first term as president, covering the 2008 campaign, the financial crisis, the fight for healthcare reform, and decisions like the raid on bin Laden, told through detailed behind-the-scenes accounts of White House deliberations.

title: Reading Like a Writer
author: Francine Prose
synopsis: A close-reading guide for writers and readers that works word by word, sentence by sentence, and paragraph by paragraph through passages from classic and contemporary fiction to show how great prose actually functions, drawing constantly on named authors from Chekhov to Nabokov.

title: Reamde
author: Neal Stephenson
synopsis: A sprawling techno-thriller that follows a MMORPG-spawned ransomware virus called REAMDE as it drags a games executive, his niece, Russian mobsters, and Islamist militants into a globe-spanning chase across British Columbia, China, and the Philippines.

title: Rich Dad Poor Dad for Teens: The Secrets About Money
author: Robert T. Kiyosaki
synopsis: An adaptation of Kiyosaki's financial-education framework for a teen audience, using the contrasting lessons of his own 'rich dad' and 'poor dad' to argue for financial literacy, asset ownership, and entrepreneurship over conventional schooling and salaried work.

title: Rich People Problems
author: Kevin Kwan
synopsis: The final novel of the Crazy Rich Asians trilogy, centered on the Singaporean Young/Shang family's scramble over the deathbed and inheritance of matriarch Su Yi, mixing satire of ultra-wealthy excess with Nick and Rachel's efforts to reconcile with his estranged family.

title: SPQR: A History of Ancient Rome
author: Mary Beard
synopsis: Mary Beard traces Roman history from the legendary founding by Romulus and the semi-mythical kings through the political crises of the Republic, opening with Cicero's suppression of the Catiline conspiracy, and on through the rise of the emperors and the Roman world beyond the city, ending around 212 CE.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
synopsis: Harari surveys the history of Homo sapiens from the Cognitive Revolution through the Agricultural Revolution, the unification of humankind under empires, money, and religion, and the Scientific Revolution, closing with speculation about the species' technological future.

title: Secret Son
author: Laila Lalami
synopsis: Raised by his mother in a one-room house in the slums of Casablanca, Youssef El Mekki discovers that the father he believed dead is alive and wealthy, moves into his new family's world of privilege, and then, after a reversal of fortune sends him back to the streets, is drawn into a fringe Islamist organization known as the Party.

title: Seveneves
author: Neal Stephenson
synopsis: When the moon inexplicably blows apart, humanity has roughly two years before the fragments will bombard Earth and scour it lifeless, forcing a scramble to build a Cloud Ark of orbiting habitats around the space station Izzy; the story later jumps five thousand years to the descendants of seven survivors who have rebuilt a society in a habitat ring.

title: Shalimar the Clown
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: In the Kashmiri village of Pachigam, the clown and tightrope walker Shalimar marries the dancer Boonyi, whose affair with the American ambassador Max Ophuls sets off a chain of betrayal and revenge that turns Shalimar into an assassin and eventually entangles Max's daughter Kashmira in Los Angeles.

title: Shame
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: In the border town of Q. and later in the corridors of power of a thinly veiled Pakistan, the fates of General Raza Hyder, the Prime Minister Iskander Harappa, and Hyder's shame-driven daughter Sufiya Zinobia entangle with Omar Khayyam Shakil, a man born to three mother-sisters and raised without shame himself.

title: Shoe Dog: A Memoir by the Creator of Nike
author: Phil Knight
synopsis: Phil Knight recounts building Blue Ribbon into Nike, from an early-morning run through Oregon that opens the book, through importing Onitsuka running shoes from Japan, scouting factories, and fighting through cash crises, lawsuits, and boardroom betrayals to grow the company.

title: Snow
author: Orhan Pamuk
synopsis: The poet Ka travels to the snowbound Turkish city of Kars to investigate a wave of suicides among religious girls forbidden to wear headscarves, and gets swept into local political intrigue, a theatrical coup staged by the actor Sunay Zaim, and his own tangled love for Ipek and reunion with the revolutionary Fazil.

title: Snow Crash
author: Neal Stephenson
synopsis: In a balkanized near-future America run by corporate Burbclaves, pizza-delivery driver and part-time hacker the Deliverator and skateboard courier Y.T. get drawn into the spread of a mind-altering drug/virus called Snow Crash that threatens users in both the real world and the virtual Metaverse.

title: Stardust
author: Neil Gaiman
synopsis: Tristran Thorn, a young man from the village of Wall bordering the magical land of Faerie, crosses the wall to retrieve a fallen star to win his heart's desire, only to find the star is a living, injured young woman with her own dangers to escape.

title: Stella Maris
author: Cormac McCarthy
synopsis: A twenty-year-old doctoral candidate in mathematics checks herself into a psychiatric hospice in Black River Falls, Wisconsin, in 1972 carrying forty thousand dollars in cash, and her recorded sessions with a psychiatrist range across grief for her dead father and brother, her plans to disappear into the Romanian mountains, and long dialogues on Gödel, Spengler, and the foundations of mathematics.

title: Sula
author: Toni Morrison
synopsis: In the Bottom, a Black hill community above Medallion, Ohio, two girls, Nel and Sula, grow up inseparable before Sula leaves town for a decade of college and drifting; when she returns, her defiance of the community's moral codes, including sleeping with Nel's husband, turns her into the town's living embodiment of evil even as the novel traces the Peace and Wright family households across the decades.

title: Suttree
author: Cormac McCarthy
synopsis: Cornelius Suttree, who has abandoned a life of privilege, lives alone on a houseboat on the Tennessee River in Knoxville around 1950, fishing for a living and moving through a demimonde of prostitutes, junkmen, drunks, and petty criminals like Gene Harrogate, in a sequence of episodes marked by arrests, illness, and sudden violent death.

title: Terminal Man
author: Michael Crichton
synopsis: Harry Benson, a computer scientist who suffers blackout seizures and violent rages after a car accident left him with psychomotor epilepsy, undergoes an experimental operation at a Los Angeles hospital to implant a computer that delivers electrical stimulation to his brain to suppress his attacks; when the implant instead teaches him to trigger his own pleasurable seizures, he escapes the hospital and goes on a killing spree while doctors and police try to track him down.

title: The Anatomy Lesson
author: Philip Roth
synopsis: Novelist Nathan Zuckerman, crippled by unexplained chronic neck and shoulder pain and unable to write since publishing his notorious novel Carnovsky, is cared for by four women while feuding bitterly with his brother Henry and obsessing over a scathing critical essay by Milton Appel. Unable to work and convinced he wants a different life, he flies to Chicago posing as a pornography publisher to enroll in medical school, gets into a drunken graveside brawl that shatters his jaw, and ends up hospitalized, trailing interns on their rounds as a patient fascinated by real physical suffering.

title: The Breast
author: Philip Roth
synopsis: David Kepesh, a 38-year-old literature professor, narrates from a hospital bed after his body has transformed into a giant female breast; he recounts the onset of the transformation, sessions with his psychiatrist Dr. Klinger and nurse Miss Clark, and visits from his father, girlfriend Claire, and colleague Arthur Schonbrunn, while wrestling with whether his fate is a hallucination and whether it was inspired by the Kafka and Gogol stories he taught.

title: The Bull from the Sea
author: Mary Renault
synopsis: Narrated by Theseus in first person, the novel opens with his return to Athens after killing the Minotaur in Crete, and follows his kingship, his bond with Pirithoos, his abduction of the Amazon Hippolyta and her death defending Athens at his side, and his marriage to Phaedra whose passion for his son Hippolytos leads to the young man's death and Theseus's own ruin.

title: The Castle of Crossed Destinies
author: Italo Calvino
synopsis: A traveler takes shelter in a castle where an enchanted forest has struck all the guests mute, so they can only tell their life stories by laying out and pointing to tarot cards from a shared deck, producing tangled, overlapping tales—an ingrate's punishment, an alchemist's bargain, a doomed bride, a grave-robber, Roland driven mad with love, Astolpho's flight to the moon—that the narrator and others must piece together from the spread; a second part, 'The Tavern of Crossed Destinies,' repeats the device with a different deck, and a closing note describes Calvino's own struggle to construct both sections as a 'machine for constructing stories' out of the tarot images.

title: The Charioteer
author: Mary Renault
synopsis: Laurie Odell, wounded and evacuated from Dunkirk, recovers in a wartime English hospital while reconnecting with Ralph Lanyon, the older schoolmate who once gave him a copy of Plato's Phaedrus, and falling for Andrew, a conscientious-objector orderly; the novel traces Laurie's divided loyalties and his effort to reconcile the Phaedrus's ideal of love with the messy realities of his own life.

title: The Crossing
author: Cormac McCarthy
synopsis: Teenage brothers Billy and Boyd Parham cross from their New Mexico ranch into Mexico, first to return a trapped she-wolf to the mountains and later after their parents are killed, encountering a devastated hacienda, an itinerant opera troupe, and the loss of Boyd along the way before Billy makes a final solitary crossing.

title: The Dark Forest
author: Cixin Liu
synopsis: Facing an incoming Trisolaran invasion fleet, the UN's Planetary Defense Council names four Wallfacers—including sociologist Luo Ji—to devise secret defense strategies hidden even from their own species, since Trisolaris's sophons can monitor all human communication but not thought; Luo Ji eventually formulates the "dark forest" theory of cosmic civilizations as a deterrent, while political commissar Zhang Beihai maneuvers within the emerging Space Force and Earth's three star fleets are wiped out when they encounter a single Trisolaran probe.

title: The Death of Ivan Ilyich
author: Leo Tolstoy
synopsis: After the sudden death of Ivan Ilych Golovin, a Court of Justice official, his colleagues react with thoughts of promotions rather than grief, and the story traces back through Ivan Ilych's conventional rise through the legal bureaucracy to the mysterious illness that slowly kills him, isolating him in physical agony and existential dread until, in his final hours, he finds a strange peace.

title: The Diamond Age
author: Neal Stephenson
synopsis: In a nanotech-saturated future of tribal enclaves and floating city-states, a stolen interactive book called the Young Lady's Illustrated Primer raises a poor Shanghai girl named Nell while its engineer, its ruthless commissioner, and a Confucian judge in the Leased Territories are drawn into the fallout of its theft.

title: The Duniazat
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: In 1195 Cordoba, the exiled philosopher Ibn Rushd (Averroes) takes in an orphaned girl named Dunia who is secretly a jinn princess, fathers a multitude of earlobe-less children with her during his internal exile, and abandons her and the children (nicknamed the Duniazat) when he is recalled to court after the Almohad victory at Alarcos; the story then traces how her descendants, ignorant of their supernatural origin, spread across the world over the following centuries.

title: The Facts: A Novelist's Autobiography
author: Philip Roth
synopsis: Philip Roth frames his own memoir as a letter to his fictional alter ego Nathan Zuckerman, tracing his Newark boyhood, his father's near-fatal 1944 surgery, his years at Bucknell and Chicago, his troubled first marriage to Josie, and the furor over his early Jewish-themed stories, then closes with a fictional Zuckerman letter that skeptically dissects the manuscript and urges Roth not to publish it.

title: The Fall
author: Albert Camus
synopsis: In an Amsterdam sailors' bar, the self-declared "judge-penitent" Jean-Baptiste Clamence delivers a rambling confession to a stranger, recounting his fall from a celebrated, self-satisfied Parisian lawyer into guilt after he failed to help a young woman who jumped into the Seine, and the corrosive philosophy of universal judgment he built from that failure.

title: The Ghost Writer
author: Philip Roth
synopsis: In 1956, young writer Nathan Zuckerman spends an evening at the Berkshires farmhouse of his literary idol E. I. Lonoff, where he becomes fixated on Amy Bellette, a mysterious young woman in the Lonoff household, and privately imagines she may secretly be Anne Frank, while witnessing Lonoff's wife Hope unravel and finally leave.

title: The Golden House
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: Narrated by a young filmmaker neighbor, René, the novel follows Nero Golden and his three sons as they arrive in a Greenwich Village enclave on the day of a new president's inauguration to escape a hidden past in Bombay, and traces the family's unraveling over the following years of secrets, madness, and betrayal, ending in a fire that consumes the Golden house.

title: The Humbling
author: Philip Roth
synopsis: Aging stage actor Simon Axler loses his ability to act after a string of onstage failures, including a disastrous Macbeth, and suffers a breakdown; after a subsequent affair with a much younger woman, Pegeen, collapses, he stages his own suicide as a reenactment of the final line of Chekhov's The Seagull.

title: The Innocence of Objects
author: Orhan Pamuk
synopsis: Pamuk's nonfiction catalogue of his Museum of Innocence in Istanbul, walking through the museum's vitrines box by box while recounting how he collected everyday objects (Hilton Hotel postcards, matchbooks, photographs) to build the museum alongside his novel, and reflecting on the psychology of collecting, waiting, and time.

title: The King Must Die
author: Mary Renault
synopsis: Narrated in first person by Theseus, the novel follows him from his boyhood in Troizen, where he is raised believing himself fathered by a god, through his journey to Athens and his selection as one of the youths sent as tribute to Crete, where he trains as a bull-dancer in the Bull Court of Knossos Palace under the rule of the Cretan priest-queens.

title: The Last White Man
author: Mohsin Hamid
synopsis: In an unnamed town, a white man named Anders wakes to find his skin has turned dark brown, and as the same transformation spreads to others, the community descends into fear and militant violence before gradually, over years, accepting a world where everyone has changed color. The novel follows Anders and his partner Oona, and later their daughter, through this upheaval and its long aftermath.

title: The Last of the Wine
author: Mary Renault
synopsis: Narrated by Alexias, an Athenian youth who comes of age during the final years of the Peloponnesian War, the novel follows his education under Sokrates, his love for the older Lysis, and their shared endurance of famine, siege, and the terror of the Thirty Tyrants as Athens collapses toward defeat.

title: The Magic Mountain
author: Thomas Mann
synopsis: Young engineer Hans Castorp arrives at a Swiss Alpine sanatorium to visit his tubercular cousin Joachim, is himself diagnosed with a touch of the disease, and stays for seven years, drawn into a timeless world of illness, desire for the enigmatic Clavdia Chauchat, and prolonged ideological combat between the humanist Settembrini and the totalitarian ex-Jesuit Naphta, ending with Naphta's suicide and Castorp's departure into the First World War.

title: The Mask of Apollo
author: Mary Renault
synopsis: An Athenian tragic actor named Nikeratos narrates his career on the fourth-century BC theater circuit, from playing extras in his father's troupe to touring Sicily, where he becomes entangled with Dion of Syracuse and the philosopher Plato in their attempt to reform the tyranny of Dionysios II.

title: The Ministry of Utmost Happiness
author: Arundhati Roy
synopsis: The novel follows Anjum, a hijra who makes a home in a Delhi graveyard, and Tilo, a woman entangled with men on opposing sides of the Kashmir conflict, weaving together their stories with those of the Kashmiri insurgency, Gujarat's riots, and Delhi's protest movements.

title: The Moor's Account
author: Laila Lalami
synopsis: Mustafa ibn Muhammad, a Moroccan slave known to history only as Estevanico, narrates his own account of the disastrous 1527 Narvaez expedition to Florida, correcting the official Spanish record as he and a handful of survivors are shipwrecked, enslaved by various tribes, and wander for years across North America seeking a way back to freedom.

title: The Moor's Last Sigh
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: Moraes 'Moor' Zogoiby, born with a withered hand and aging at twice the normal rate, tells the saga of his Cochin spice-trading family, dominated by his painter mother Aurora, tracing four generations of Indian history from colonial Malabar through Bombay's criminal underworld.

title: The Museum of Innocence
author: Orhan Pamuk
synopsis: Kemal, a wealthy Istanbul businessman engaged to marry a woman of his own class, falls obsessively in love with his poor distant cousin Fusun, and after losing her spends years amassing objects connected to her that he eventually assembles into the museum of the title.

title: The Naive and the Sentimental Novelist
author: Orhan Pamuk
synopsis: Pamuk's Charles Eliot Norton Lectures at Harvard on what happens in the minds of writers and readers of novels, examining the visual imagination, character, plot, and the elusive 'center' of a novel through his own fiction and classics from Tolstoy to Proust.

title: The Nature of Alexander
author: Mary Renault
synopsis: Mary Renault's account of Alexander the Great's life and campaigns, opening with his funeral cortege in Babylon and tracing his conquests through Macedon, Persia, and India using ancient sources such as Arrian, Plutarch, and Diodorus.

title: The Orchard Keeper
author: Cormac McCarthy
synopsis: Set in a remote Tennessee community between the two world wars, the novel follows the boy John Wesley Rattner, the bootlegger Marion Sylder who unknowingly killed the boy's father, and old Uncle Ather, whose lives converge around an abandoned orchard.

title: The Other Americans
author: Laila Lalami
synopsis: After her father is fatally struck by a hit-and-run driver outside the family's Mojave Desert diner, Nora Guerraoui returns home and, alongside Detective Coleman and her old classmate Jeremy, works through the investigation while confronting her Moroccan immigrant family's history.

title: The Pachinko Parlour
author: Elisa Shua Dusapin
synopsis: A young Franco-Korean woman spends a summer in Tokyo tutoring a Japanese girl named Mieko in French while staying with her aging Korean grandparents, who fled to Japan during the Korean War and never returned, and repeatedly puts off a planned visit to the pachinko parlour they run.

title: The Passenger
author: Cormac McCarthy
synopsis: A salvage diver in 1980s New Orleans investigates a sunken jet with a passenger missing from the wreckage while his memory of his dead sister, a mathematician who took her own life, keeps intruding as long dialogues with a flippered hallucination called the Thalidomide Kid.

title: The Persian Boy
author: Mary Renault
synopsis: A Persian boy named Bagoas, castrated and sold as a slave after his family's ruin, becomes a favorite in King Darius's court and then Alexander the Great's companion, narrating Alexander's conquests and death from inside the royal tent.

title: The Praise Singer
author: Mary Renault
synopsis: The poet Simonides, in old age at the Sicilian court, looks back over his life as a singer trained under the bard Kleobis, his years in tyrant Athens under Pisistratos and his sons, and the murder of Hipparchos by Harmodios and Aristogeiton.

title: The Prophet's Hair
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: A relic believed to be a hair from the Prophet Muhammad's beard is stolen in Srinagar and passes through the hands of a moneylender who is transformed into a tyrant, then a professional burglar hired to steal it back, with maiming and ruin following everyone it touches.

title: The Red-Haired Woman
author: Orhan Pamuk
synopsis: A teenage apprentice well-digger named Cem, working outside Istanbul under master well-digger Mahmut, falls for an older woman known as the Red-Haired Woman, and a violent accident at the well entangles his life for decades with the myths of Oedipus and of Rostam and Sohrab.

title: The Road to San Giovanni
author: Italo Calvino
synopsis: Five autobiographical essays in which Calvino reconstructs his father's conviction that their farmland above San Remo was the true world and the town below a mere appendix, revisits his obsessive youth as a moviegoer absorbing 1930s Hollywood stars scene by scene, and recalls his time as a partisan fighter and the mechanics of memory itself.

title: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
synopsis: Magazine writer Monique Grant is summoned by reclusive Hollywood legend Evelyn Hugo to ghostwrite her life story, which Hugo recounts husband by husband, from her escape out of Hell's Kitchen to her decades-long hidden relationship with producer Harry Cameron.

title: The Strange Library
author: Haruki Murakami
synopsis: A boy who visits the library to look up how the Ottoman Empire collected taxes is led down into a basement labyrinth where an old man imprisons him to memorize books before eating his brain, and he plots escape with the help of a sheep man and a voiceless girl.

title: The Testaments
author: Margaret Atwood
synopsis: Fifteen years after the events of The Handmaid's Tale, the regime of Gilead is narrated through the interwoven testimonies of Aunt Lydia, who keeps a secret manuscript hidden inside a hollowed-out copy of Cardinal Newman's Apologia Pro Vita Sua in the Ardua Hall archive, and two younger women, Agnes and Daisy, whose paths converge toward the regime's downfall.

title: The Three-Body Problem
author: Cixin Liu
synopsis: Beginning when astrophysicist Ye Wenjie, working at a secret Cultural Revolution-era radio base, makes contact with an alien civilization, the novel follows nanomaterials researcher Wang Miao as he investigates a wave of scientist suicides and the virtual-reality game Three Body, which encodes the plight of the Trisolaran civilization.

title: The Uses of Literature
author: Italo Calvino
synopsis: A collection of Calvino's essays and lectures, spanning theoretical pieces on cybernetics, structuralism, and "levels of reality" in fiction alongside close readings of specific classics — the Odyssey, Ovid's Metamorphoses, Ariosto's Orlando Furioso, Stendhal's Charterhouse of Parma, Manzoni's The Betrothed, Balzac's city fiction, Voltaire's Candide, and Cyrano de Bergerac's lunar fantasy — plus shorter pieces on Fourier, Marianne Moore, Pliny, and Roland Barthes.

title: The White Castle
author: Orhan Pamuk
synopsis: A frame narrative presents a manuscript found by a modern editor: the first-person account of a young Italian scholar captured by pirates and enslaved in seventeenth-century Istanbul, given as a gift to "Hoja," an Ottoman scholar who so physically resembles him that the two become entangled in an obsessive intellectual and psychological rivalry. Together they serve the sultan as astrologers/scientists and design a giant siege weapon used in a military campaign against a fortress, while their identities increasingly blur and swap.

title: The Dream Hotel
author: Laila Lalami
synopsis: In a near-future America, Sara Hussein is held at "Madison," a retention center (a converted elementary school run by private contractor Safe-X) after being flagged by a predictive-policing "risk score" system tied to a neural implant called the Dreamsaver that monitors her dreams; the book follows her daily life among fellow retainees and her strained correspondence with her husband and children, as she and others push back against the facility's surveillance and precrime detention regime.

title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
author: Gabrielle Zevin
synopsis: In late-1990s/2000s Cambridge and Los Angeles, childhood acquaintances Sam Masur and Sadie Green reunite as young adults and, together with Sam's roommate Marx, found a video game studio, building acclaimed titles while navigating Sam's chronic pain from a foot injury/amputation, professional rivalry, and a decades-long entangled friendship.

title: Truman
author: David McCullough
synopsis: This biography of Harry S. Truman covers his boyhood and youth in Independence, Missouri, his World War I artillery service in France, his rise through Kansas City's Pendergast political machine, his vice presidency and accession to the presidency on Roosevelt's death, and his presidency through the atomic bomb decision, the Marshall Plan, the 1948 campaign, the Korean War and firing of MacArthur, into his retirement in Independence and death, drawing on his diaries, letters, and interviews with associates.

title: Under the Jaguar Sun
author: Italo Calvino
synopsis: Three linked stories, left unfinished at Calvino's death, meant to explore the five senses: a couple touring Oaxaca's convents and ruins whose relationship becomes entangled with the region's cuisine and colonial history; a deposed king reduced to paranoid listening from his throne room; and a man obsessed with tracking a lost lover through scent alone.

title: Victory City
author: Salman Rushdie
synopsis: A blind poet-prophetess, Pampa Kampana, lives two hundred and forty-seven years and narrates the rise and fall of the empire of Bisnaga, which she conjures from a handful of magic seeds and populates by whispering invented life stories into her subjects' ears, spanning generations of kings, wars, and dynastic betrayal.

title: Walking with the Comrades
author: Arundhati Roy
synopsis: Reportage essays from Roy's weeks traveling with Maoist guerrillas in the forests of central India, describing the Janatana Sarkar's armed cadres, women commanders like Comrade Niti who carries an AK on her shoulder, and the war between the Indian state and adivasi insurgents in Chhattisgarh's Dandakaranya region.

title: Water for Elephants
author: Sara Gruen
synopsis: An elderly Jacob Jankowski recalls his youth as a veterinary student who joins the Benzini Brothers traveling circus during the Great Depression, working the menagerie under the volatile boss August, falling for August's wife Marlena, and caring for the elephant Rosie amid the show's harsh, itinerant world.

title: When She Was Good
author: Philip Roth
synopsis: In the small Midwestern town of Liberty Center, Lucy Nelson grows up hardened by her father's alcoholism and her family's failures, setting her will against them and later against her husband Roy Bassart, whom she marries despite secretly despising him.

title: White Fragility: Why It's So Hard for White People to Talk About Racism
author: Robin DiAngelo
synopsis: DiAngelo argues that most white Americans are so racially insulated from discomfort about race that even mild challenges to that comfort—like being called out for a racist remark—trigger a defensive reaction she calls white fragility, and she traces how this dynamic protects the racial status quo. Drawing on decades of running diversity trainings, she dissects moves like color-blindness and color-celebration claims that let white people position themselves as exempt from racism.

title: Words Are My Matter
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
synopsis: A collection of talks, essays, introductions, and book reviews (mostly from 2000-2016) in which Le Guin discusses genre, fantasy, science fiction, gender, aging, and the craft of writing, and reviews and introduces the work of writers including H. G. Wells, José Saramago, Italo Calvino, and Margaret Atwood.

title: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance
author: Robert M. Pirsig
synopsis: A narrator and his son Chris ride a motorcycle from Minnesota toward the West Coast with friends, alternating road observations and practical talk about motorcycle repair with the narrator's recovered memories of his former self, Phaedrus, a philosophy teacher whose obsessive pursuit of a definition of Quality led him through Kant, Aristotle, and Poincare toward a breakdown and electroshock treatment.

title: Zodiac: An Eco-Thriller
author: Neal Stephenson
synopsis: Boston-based rogue environmental activist and industrial chemist Sangamon Taylor tracks toxic dumping by corporations like Basco, using sewer outfalls, illegal sampling, and stunts staged from a Zodiac inflatable boat, before uncovering a genetically engineered organism plot tied to Basco executive Alvin Pleshy. The story climaxes in a violent confrontation on Boston Harbor with Pleshy and Biotronics president Laughlin, leaving Sangamon's friend Boone badly wounded.

title: Atmosphere: A Love Story
author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
synopsis: Joan Goodwin, a physics teacher turned NASA astronaut candidate in the early 1980s, trains alongside fellow astronauts Vanessa Ford, Griff, Lydia Danes, and Hank Redmond in Houston while raising her young niece Frances, and falls in love with Vanessa; a present-day frame set on December 29, 1984 follows a shuttle mission in crisis after Griff and others are endangered during a spacewalk and reentry.

title: t zero
author: Italo Calvino
synopsis: A collection of speculative first-person monologues narrated largely by the cosmic being Qfwfq, ranging from the Moon's origin and the first birds to cellular mitosis and reproduction, and culminating in a story where the narrator becomes a character trapped in the Chateau d'If alongside Abbe Faria, watching Alexandre Dumas assemble the branching draft possibilities of the novel The Count of Monte Cristo.

author: Ben Lerner
synopsis: A young Brooklyn poet and novelist, newly signed to a lucrative book deal and diagnosed with a dilated aorta, drifts through a New York bracing for a hurricane while he agrees to father a child for his best friend. A meditative, autofictional novel about time, art, mortality and literary fraud.

title: A Brief History of Seven Killings
author: Marlon James
synopsis: A polyphonic, multi-decade novel built around the 1976 attempted assassination of a reggae superstar known as the Singer in Kingston, Jamaica. Gang leaders, CIA operatives, a Rolling Stone journalist, and ordinary Jamaicans narrate the events and their fallout through the 1991 crack-era New York.

title: A Life's Work
author: Rachel Cusk
synopsis: Novelist Rachel Cusk gives a frank, unsentimental account of pregnancy, birth and the first year of her daughter's life, from colic and sleepless nights to the loss of her former self. Interweaving readings of novels and childcare manuals, it is a landmark of the modern motherhood memoir.

title: Aftermath
author: Rachel Cusk
synopsis: Rachel Cusk's memoir of her marriage breaking down and the disorienting life that follows for her and her two young daughters. She reads her own separation through Greek tragedy, writing about family, authority and the self in the wreckage of a household.

title: Agrippa
author: Robert Harris
synopsis: Told as the secret memoir of Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa, born feet-first and nicknamed the mother-killer, who becomes the commoner general and right-hand man of Octavius, the future Augustus. It follows the two friends from Caesar's assassination through the civil wars and the fall of the Republic.

title: Angle of Yaw
author: Ben Lerner
synopsis: Ben Lerner's second poetry collection, in five sections, mixing prose-poem and fragmentary lyric to interrogate sports, war, politics, the novel and the page itself. It closes with a Twenty-One Gun Salute for Ronald Reagan.

title: Another America
author: Barbara Kingsolver
synopsis: Barbara Kingsolver's poetry collection, in five sections, about injustice, exile, violence and endurance in the United States and the Americas. This bilingual edition pairs each poem with a Spanish translation by Rebeca Cartes.

title: Artful
author: Ali Smith
synopsis: Four Oxford lectures on time, form, edge, and offer and reflection, reworked by Ali Smith into a hybrid of essay and fiction. A grieving narrator reads her late partner's unfinished lectures on books, poems, and art, and the two voices slowly merge into one conversation about how stories work.

title: Babel
author: R. F. Kuang
synopsis: In an alternate 1830s Britain powered by silver-working, a Cantonese orphan is brought to Oxford to train at the Royal Institute of Translation, known as Babel, where magic is made from the gaps between languages. As he learns that the empire's wealth rests on colonial exploitation, he must choose between the institution that raised him and a secret society resisting it.

title: The Lacuna
author: Barbara Kingsolver
synopsis: Born to an American father and Mexican mother, Harrison Shepherd grows up between Mexico and the United States, and finds work as a plaster-mixer and cook in the household of Diego Rivera and Frida Kahlo, where he also becomes secretary to the exiled Leon Trotsky. Told through his notebooks and the papers of his archivist, the novel follows his later life as a reclusive novelist in North Carolina, caught up in the anti-Communist hysteria of the postwar years.

title: Black Leopard, Red Wolf
author: Marlon James
synopsis: In a mythic, pre-colonial Africa, a mercenary known as Tracker, who can smell anyone's trail, is hired to find a missing boy and joins a band of misfits that includes a shape-shifting Leopard. Narrated to an inquisitor from a prison cell, the first book of the Dark Star trilogy turns the hunt into a tangled and violent account of kingdoms, witches and monsters.

title: Companion Piece
author: Ali Smith
synopsis: During the pandemic lockdown, a lockdown-era academic who layer-paints the words of poems looks after her ailing father while a phone call from a near-stranger and two young girls, one obsessed with the Cottingley Fairies, upend her isolation. Folk tales of a smith, a curfew and a curlew cross with her own story as Smith explores real versus fake and the stories we inherit.

title: Coventry
author: Rachel Cusk
synopsis: A collection of essays by the novelist Rachel Cusk, gathering personal pieces on driving, rudeness, motherhood, family and home alongside criticism of art and literature. The final section turns to classics and bestsellers, with essays on Edith Wharton, D. H. Lawrence, Olivia Manning, Natalia Ginzburg, Kazuo Ishiguro and others.

title: Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea
author: Emily Wilson
synopsis: A collection of essays by the classicist and translator of the Odyssey and the Iliad on Greek and Roman literature and the art of translating it. Topics include Sappho, Aristophanes, Roman comedy, Helen of Troy, the Stoics, Christopher Logue's War Music, Edith Hamilton, and the problems of rendering Homer into English.

title: Small Wonder
author: Barbara Kingsolver
synopsis: A collection of twenty-three essays written in the wake of September 11, ranging from a Grand Canyon meditation and a defense of forests and seeds to letters to a daughter and a mother. Kingsolver weighs wonder, family, food, storytelling and what it means to love a country while grieving and questioning it.

title: Flight Behavior
author: Barbara Kingsolver
synopsis: Dellarobia Turnbow, a restless young farm wife in rural Tennessee, climbs a mountain intending to throw her life away and instead finds the forest ablaze with millions of monarch butterflies that have wintered in the wrong place. As scientists, reporters and a skeptical congregation descend on her family's land, her marriage, faith and sense of the future are all put to the test.

title: Girl Meets Boy
author: Ali Smith
synopsis: A retelling of Ovid's myth of Iphis set in contemporary Inverness, narrated alternately by two sisters, Midge and Imogen. While Imogen works at a corporation that bottles and sells Scottish water, a charismatic graffiti artist turns both sisters' lives upside down.

title: Glorious Exploits
author: Ferdia Lennon
synopsis: In Syracuse in 412 BC, two unemployed potters, Lampo and Gelon, decide to stage Euripides with the starving Athenian prisoners left to die in the city's quarries, trading scraps of food for recited lines. What starts as an eccentric scheme grows into an ambitious production that draws in the prisoners, the guards, and the whole divided city.

title: Glyph
author: Ali Smith
synopsis: A family story about a young man and a gassed, blinded horse in the First World War is passed down through generations and resurfaces in the present, when a sibling's bedroom is visited by what seems to be a ghost horse. The narrators search the internet, history and their own memories to work out what, if anything, the inherited story is really about.

title: How to be both
author: Ali Smith
synopsis: A two-part novel that can be read in either order: in one half, the spirit of a fifteenth-century Ferrarese painter, Francesco del Cossa, looks back on a life spent disguised as a boy to paint; in the other, a modern teenager, George, grieves her mother and becomes fascinated by a fresco in Italy. The halves echo and refract each other on art, gender, time and loss.

title: In the Fold
author: Rachel Cusk
synopsis: A young man from a modest background becomes entranced by the wealthy, chaotic Hanbury family of a country house called Egypt, and years later, married with a son, he finds the old pull of their world reasserting itself. A comedy of class, envy and domestic disillusionment.

title: Kudos
author: Rachel Cusk
synopsis: The writer Faye travels to a literary festival in Europe and passes through a series of encounters with publishers, interviewers and fellow passengers who talk at length about their lives. The final novel of the Outline trilogy, told almost entirely through what others confide to her.

title: Like
author: Ali Smith
synopsis: Two timelines intertwine: a mother and her young daughter Kate living in a seaside caravan, and Amy and Ash, two girls whose intense friendship begins in a small Scottish town. Ali Smith's debut novel circles loss, desire and the missing person at the heart of both stories.

title: Mean Free Path
author: Ben Lerner
synopsis: A book of poems in two linked sequences, 'Mean Free Path' and 'Doppler Elegies', that fold elegy, ambient media and political dread into fragmented, self-interrupting lines. Dedicated to Ari, it plays with reference, grief and the distance between speaker and subject.

title: Moon Witch, Spider King
author: Marlon James
synopsis: Second book of the Dark Star trilogy, told by the witch Sogolon, who recounts her own version of the events in Black Leopard, Red Wolf. From a childhood of abuse to a career as a spy and assassin at the court of the Kwash kings, she exposes what the Tracker's account left out.

title: Outline
author: Rachel Cusk
synopsis: A writer flies to Athens to teach a short creative-writing course and, over the following days, listens as seatmates, students, friends and fellow writers recount their marriages, regrets and self-deceptions. The narrator stays largely in outline while the stories of others fill the book.

title: Parade
author: Rachel Cusk
synopsis: Four linked stories (The Stuntman, The Midwife, The Diver, The Spy) circle artists and the marriages, families and reputations around them, beginning with a painter known only as G who starts painting upside down. The book is told in Cusk's detached, fable-like register.

title: Partita
author: Barbara Kingsolver
synopsis: Livia, a gifted young pianist from a Southern dairy-farm community, is haunted by her brother's death on the railroad tracks and by the question of how he could do it. Structured like a Bach partita, the novel follows her through conservatory ambition, a doomed love affair, injury, and a return to the farm and the neighbors she left.

title: Saving Agnes
author: Rachel Cusk
synopsis: Agnes Day, a recent English graduate, drifts through a shabby London of flatshares, dead-end temp jobs and unreliable love, trying to work out who she is supposed to be. Her housemates and a succession of lovers keep pulling her in different directions as she searches for a stable sense of self. Cusk's first novel is a comic portrait of early adulthood in the early 1990s.

title: The Accidental
author: Ali Smith
synopsis: The Smart family, on holiday in a rented house in Norfolk, is thrown into disarray when a stranger named Amber walks in and is taken for a colleague by each of them. The novel moves between the voices of the mother, stepfather, teenage son and young daughter, and of Amber herself.

title: The Country Life
author: Rachel Cusk
synopsis: Stella Benson, a lonely young woman escaping a failed London life, takes a job caring for a disabled teenage boy on a Sussex farm owned by the overbearing Maddens. Her letters, observations and awkward encounters with the household and village slowly unsettle the pastoral promise of country life. The novel is a comic, darkening riff on Jane Eyre and the English rural idyll.

title: The Devotion of Suspect X
author: Keigo Higashino
synopsis: In Tokyo, a brilliant but reclusive high-school math teacher, Ishigami, moves to shield his neighbor Yasuko Hanaoka after her abusive ex-husband turns up dead. Detective Kusanagi investigates and turns for help to his friend, the physicist Manabu Yukawa, who was Ishigami's university rival.

title: The Disappearers
author: Marlon James
synopsis: In 1988 Kingston, a group of men mount a staging of John Herbert's prison play Fortune and Men's Eyes, and the production ends in violence and a series of disappearances. The novel follows the survivors through journals, interview transcripts and letters across 1988, 1994, 1999 and 2005, from Jamaica to Miami and back.

title: The Last Supper
author: Rachel Cusk
synopsis: Rachel Cusk's account of a summer spent in Italy with her husband and two small children, travelling through Tuscany, Umbria, Rome and the south in search of art, food and a sense of home. Structured around the paintings of Piero della Francesca, Giotto and Raphael, it mixes travel writing with reflections on family life, motherhood and the writer's own restlessness.

title: The Lichtenberg Figures
author: Ben Lerner
synopsis: Ben Lerner's debut collection, a sequence of unrhymed fourteen-line sonnets that fracture and recombine speech, cliche, political and domestic scenes. Winner of the Hayden Carruth Award, it takes its title from the branching patterns left by electrical discharge.

title: The Lights
author: Ben Lerner
synopsis: A collection of poems and prose poems by Ben Lerner, organized around light, night, grief, fatherhood and the ordinary and civic life of the present. Moving between lyric, essay and anecdote, it takes in museums, paintings, a residency and the speaker's daughters.

title: The Poisonwood Bible
author: Barbara Kingsolver
synopsis: In 1959 the Baptist missionary Nathan Price takes his wife and four daughters to the Belgian Congo, where his zeal collides with the culture around him and with the country's slide toward independence and upheaval. The story is told in the alternating voices of Orleanna Price and her daughters over the following three decades.

title: The Temporary
author: Rachel Cusk
synopsis: Francine Snaith, a young woman who believes herself marked out by destiny, takes temp work in London and meets Ralph, a man weighed down by his past and his unreliable father. Their relationship becomes a study of hope, self-deception and the gap between how people see themselves and how they are seen. Cusk's second novel.

title: The Topeka School
author: Ben Lerner
synopsis: Adam Gordon, a high-school debate champion in 1990s Topeka, Kansas, grows up among his parents' psychiatric community at the Foundation while navigating masculinity, speech and the threat of violence. The novel shifts among the perspectives of Adam, his psychologist mother Jane and his father Jonathan, and later returns to Adam as an adult and father.

title: There but for the
author: Ali Smith
synopsis: At a dinner party in Greenwich, a guest named Miles Garth goes upstairs, locks himself in the spare room and refuses to come out. Four linked sections follow different people drawn into his orbit, among them a ten-year-old girl with a gift for wordplay, as the novel plays on language, history and the idea of belonging.

title: Transcription
author: Ben Lerner
synopsis: A writer on his way to interview Thomas, his ninety-year-old former teacher and a towering translator and thinker, drifts between recorded talks, memory, family life and the fragile business of turning speech into text. The narrator's pandemic-era care for his young daughter and his time in Providence, Madrid and a hotel on the French-Swiss border shape a meditation on mentorship, listening and mediation.

title: Transit
author: Rachel Cusk
synopsis: In the wake of her marriage's collapse, a writer moves with her two young sons to London and begins renovating a flat. Through a series of conversations with builders, hairdressers, fellow writers, old friends and a former lover, the story builds a quiet portrait of change, vulnerability and fate. It is the second novel in Cusk's Outline trilogy.

title: Unsheltered
author: Barbara Kingsolver
synopsis: Willa Knox inherits a crumbling house in Vineland, New Jersey, and tries to hold together her family amid a collapsing economy and a fraught new baby. A century and a half earlier, in the same town, the science teacher Thatcher Greenwood defends Darwin's ideas against a hostile community, with help from the naturalist Mary Treat. The two timelines echo each other across eras of upheaval.

title: Whistler
author: Ann Patchett
synopsis: Daphne, a high-school English teacher in New York, is shadowed through the Metropolitan Museum by an old man named Eddie, whom she first met as a nine-year-old trapped with him in a snowbound crashed car. Moving between that childhood night and the present, the novel follows her complicated family, her mother and stepfather, her sister Leda, and the long bond with the man who once edited novels.

title: Winter
author: Ali Smith
synopsis: On Christmas Eve, the semi-retired Sophia Cleves sees a disembodied child's head floating in her large, cold house in Cornwall. Her son Art, a nature blogger, hires a stranger named Lux to pose as his girlfriend for the holiday, and the group is joined by Sophia's estranged sister Iris, a veteran of the Greenham Common protests. The second of Smith's Seasonal quartet, it plays with ghosts, politics and the legacy of art.

title: Yellowface
author: Rebecca F. Kuang
synopsis: June Hayward, a struggling white novelist, watches her more successful Chinese American rival Athena Liu die in an accident and walks away with Athena's unpublished manuscript about Chinese laborers in World War I. She submits it as her own under an ambiguous pen name, and a satire of the publishing industry unfolds as her bestselling success becomes threatened by accusations of plagiarism and cultural appropriation.

title: Spring
author: Ali Smith
synopsis: Third of the Seasonal quartet, set in a Brexit-era Britain of detention centres and shrinking hope. A grieving screenwriter, a worn-down detention-centre guard and a mysterious girl on a train are drawn together, with Katherine Mansfield and Rainer Maria Rilke threaded through the story. (Source PDF is the Dutch translation, Lente.)

title: Beautiful World, Where Are You
author: Sally Rooney
synopsis: Two old friends, novelist Alice and literary editor Eileen, trade long emails about desire, faith, art and a world in crisis while their own love lives with Felix and Simon stumble toward uncertain footing.

title: Conversations with Friends
author: Sally Rooney
synopsis: Frances, a young Dublin poet and student, and her ex-girlfriend Bobbi perform spoken word together and become entangled with an older writer, Melissa, and her actor husband Nick. Frances begins an affair with Nick while examining her own detachment and the limits of intimacy.

title: Flesh
author: David Szalay
synopsis: Following István from a Hungarian housing estate through army service, prison-adjacent drift and private security work, the novel traces his life through sparse, affectless scenes of sex, grief and money as he rises into London's wealthy circles.

title: Free Food for Millionaires
author: Min Jin Lee
synopsis: Casey Han, a Korean American Princeton graduate raised in Queens, struggles to find her footing in 1990s Manhattan among wealthy friends, Wall Street ambition, immigrant family duty, and a fraught love life. The novel follows her and the people around her across New York's Korean church and finance worlds.

title: Intermezzo
author: Sally Rooney
synopsis: Two brothers in Dublin, Peter, a successful barrister, and Ivan, a young chess prodigy, are left reeling after their father's death, each entangled in a complicated relationship with an older or younger woman while their own bond frays and slowly reforms.

title: Mr Salary
author: Sally Rooney
synopsis: Home in Dublin for Christmas while her estranged father is dying of leukaemia, a young Boston graduate student stays with Nathan, the older relative who once housed and financed her, and presses him to turn their unspoken intimacy into something real.

title: Normal People
author: Sally Rooney
synopsis: Connell and Marianne grow up in the same small Irish town, he a popular schoolboy and she an isolated outsider, and begin a secret relationship. Over the following years at Trinity College Dublin they drift together and apart as class, confidence and misunderstanding shape their lives.

title: Botchan
author: Natsume Sōseki
synopsis: A hot-headed Tokyo math teacher is shipped off to a provincial school, where he nicknames his scheming colleagues Red Shirt and Porcupine and wages a one-man war on small-town hypocrisy.

title: In Praise of Shadows
author: Jun'ichirō Tanizaki
synopsis: A novelist wanders from toilets to lacquerware to Nō costumes to make the case that Japanese beauty lives in shadow, and that electric light and Western gadgetry are quietly erasing it.

title: Aino Folk-Tales
author: Basil Hall Chamberlain
synopsis: Chamberlain writes down the oral tales of the Ainu of Yezo as told by chiefs and villagers, from how the owl got his feather cap to why dogs cannot speak. Fox-gods, the civilizer Okikurumi, the Panaumbe and Penaumbe cycle, a man who weds the Bear-Goddess and a hunter in Hades fill its moral tales and scraps of folklore.

title: Glimpses of Unfamiliar Japan: First Series
author: Lafcadio Hearn
synopsis: Hearn lands in Yokohama, rides by jinricksha to Kamakura and Enoshima, then settles in Matsue to explore Izumo's shrines, festivals and village superstitions. He visits the Great Shrine of Kitzuki, the cave of the children's ghosts, and the temple at Hinomisaki, finding the living Shinto in the national heart rather than in books.

title: Glimpses of Unfamiliar Japan: Second Series
author: Lafcadio Hearn
synopsis: Hearn continues his Matsue years with the household shrine, women's hair, a garden of frogs and lotus, ancestor worship and the Japanese smile, then sails to the remote Oki islands and the farewell of Kumamoto. Ghost-lore, Buddhist funerals, student essays and the Shinto roots of the family religion fill out a portrait of old Izumo giving way to the new Japan.

title: In Ghostly Japan
author: Lafcadio Hearn
synopsis: Opening with a Bodhisattva's vision of a mountain made of skulls, Hearn gathers tales of the Long-sleeved Robe and the Peony-Lantern ghosts, and a fortune-teller who saves a man haunted by his dead lover. Essays follow on incense games, the footprints of the Buddha, Japanese verse and Buddhist proverbs, with a priest who meets a Tengu among the closing stories.

title: Japanese Fairy Tales
author: Yei Theodora Ozaki
synopsis: Twenty-two tales retold for Western children: Urashima Taro rides a tortoise to the Sea King's palace, Momotaro sets out from a peach to fight ogres, and a sparrow loses her tongue to a wicked old woman. Along the way come goblins, talking badgers and monkeys, the Bamboo-cutter's moon-child and the Empress who mends the sky with stones of five colors.

title: Kokoro: Hints and Echoes of Japanese Inner Life
author: Lafcadio Hearn
synopsis: Hearn turns from outward Japan to its heart, from a murderer's confrontation with his victim's child at a Kumamoto railway station to a bugler who dies sounding the charge and a cholera-time village. Long essays on karma, pre-existence and ancestor-worship set Buddhist doctrine beside Herbert Spencer and Huxley, and an appendix gives three popular ballads sung by Matsue's outcast yama-no-mono.

title: Kwaidan: Stories and Studies of Strange Things
author: Lafcadio Hearn
synopsis: A blind biwa-player named Hoichi is summoned each night to recite the fall of the Heike to a court of ghosts, until a priest paints the Heart Sutra over his body and forgets his ears. Snow-women, headless Rokuro-Kubi, a man-eating jikininki and a dream of a kingdom inside an ant-hill give way to Hearn's closing essays on butterflies, mosquitoes and ants.

title: Shadowings
author: Lafcadio Hearn
synopsis: Hearn retells strange Japanese tales of reunited ghosts, a dreamer's vision of Fugen-Bosatsu and a painted girl who steps from her picture, then turns to essays on the shrilling of cicadas, girls' names and old street ballads. The book closes with reveries on nightmares and a mysterious dream-book that rewrites itself.

title: The American Diary of a Japanese Girl
author: Yoné Noguchi
synopsis: Morning Glory, a young Japanese woman, lands in San Francisco and records her wide-eyed, wisecracking adventures with her uncle, from Longfellow-loving society ladies to a cottage next door to a poet named Heine. Her broken-English diary lampoons American manners while she dreams of becoming a novelist.

title: The Book of Tea
author: Kakuzo Okakura
synopsis: Okakura turns the humble cup of tea into an Eastern philosophy of life, tracing Teaism from Chinese medicine to Zen-flavoured Japanese ceremony. He moves from the bare tea-room and its Taoist love of the imperfect to flower-arranging, art appreciation and the tea-master Rikiu's final tea before his suicide.

title: The Japanese Spirit
author: Yoshisaburo Okakura
synopsis: Okakura traces how Shinto, Confucianism, Taoism and Zen Buddhism fused into the Japanese national character, from the Samurai code and hara-kiri to the tea ceremony and the seventeen-syllable hokku. A Japanese professor explains his country to a Western audience.

title: The No Plays of Japan
author: Arthur Waley
synopsis: Waley's translation of twenty-odd No plays, where ghosts of Heike warriors, a jealous Rokujo and a fisherman-turned-angel return to chant their sorrows to wandering priests. Framed by a long introduction on the masks, music and Buddhist outlook of the stage.

title: The Spirit of Japanese Art
author: Yoné Noguchi
synopsis: Noguchi profiles Japanese artists from Koyetsu and Utamaro to the madcap Kyosai and the Turner-loving Hara, arguing that kokoromochi, the spirit behind the brush, matters more than technique. He mixes anecdotes, tea-room visits and comparisons with Whistler and Western painters.

title: Japan: An Attempt at Interpretation
author: Lafcadio Hearn
synopsis: Hearn traces Japanese civilization to its roots in ancestor-worship, arguing that the household shrine, the Shinto communal cult and the tradition of loyalty explain a nation the West misreads. He moves from the family altar through Buddhism, feudal military rule and the Jesuit peril to the Shinto revival, with Herbert Spencer as his guide.

title: Kimiko, and Other Japanese Sketches
author: Lafcadio Hearn
synopsis: Hearn tells of Kimiko, a geisha from the Street of the Geisha who knows the power of beauty and the weakness of passion, and of Ai, the samurai's daughter who sells herself to Kimika to keep her mother alive. Companion sketches follow a tiny nun in her miniature temple of Amida and a mother's grief for her dead child.

title: Gleanings in Buddha-Fields: Studies of Hand and Soul in the Far East
author: Lafcadio Hearn
synopsis: Hearn opens with a village that deifies the man who burned his rice-fields to save it from a tidal wave, then wanders Kyoto and Osaka among toy-shops, newspaper offices and faces in Japanese art. Later chapters collect Buddhist allusions in folk-song, set Nirvana beside Herbert Spencer's evolution, and translate the case of the boy Katsugoro who remembers a past life.

title: The Religion of the Samurai: A Study of Zen Philosophy and Discipline in China and Japan
author: Kaiten Nukariya
synopsis: A Soto Zen scholar traces Zen from Bodhidharma and the Sixth Patriarch through Ei-sai and Do-gen to the Japanese warrior class. He explains the sitting meditation, the awakening of the innermost wisdom and why Zen discipline gave the samurai calm in the face of death.

title: Shinto: The Ancient Religion of Japan
author: W. G. Aston
synopsis: Aston sketches the nature-gods (kami), the myths of Izanagi and Izanami, the doubled spirit (mitama), the norito prayers and the shrine festivals of Japan's native religion. He argues that Shinto is not ancestor-worship, has little moral code, and is doomed beside its foreign rivals.

title: Old-World Japan: Legends of the Land of the Gods
author: Frank Rinder
synopsis: Rinder retells Japanese myths and folk tales, from the birth of the gods and Izanagi's descent to Hades to the Star Lovers, the Moon-Maiden and the golden boy Kintaro. Illustrated by T. H. Robinson, the stories favour colour and charm over scholarship.

title: Warriors of Old Japan, and Other Stories
author: Yei Theodora Ozaki
synopsis: Ten retold Japanese legends of archers, knights and goblins: Tametomo bends his mighty bow, Yorimasa dies after the battle of the bridge, and the giant priest Benkei is bested by young Yoshitsune. The tales end with the Bowl-Wearing Princess and Lazy Taro, the idler who wins a lord's daughter.

title: Kibun Daizin; Or, From Shark-Boy to Merchant Prince
author: Gensai Murai
synopsis: Bunkichi, a poor boy in a Wakayama fishing town, wins the name Shark-Boy by poisoning the man-eating shark that terrorizes the bay. He rides a doomed ship through a storm to Yedo with a cargo of oranges and rises to become the wealthy merchant Kibun Daizin.

title: Home Life in Tokyo
author: Jukichi Inouye
synopsis: A Japanese insider walks English readers through the Tokyo household: food and sake, kimono and hair-styling, the house and its servants, marriage, childbirth, funerals, and festivals. Chapters on music, theatre, flower-arranging and parlour games like sugoroku and ode-cards round out a year of ordinary life.

title: Japanese Fairy Tales
author: Grace James
synopsis: Thirty-eight Japanese tales and legends, from the bamboo cutter's Moon Maiden and Urashima beneath the sea to the Tongue-Cut Sparrow and the Bell of Dojoji. Ghosts, fox maidens, thunder gods and doomed lovers drift through Warwick Goble's illustrated pages.

title: I Am a Cat
author: Natsume Sōseki
synopsis: A nameless stray cat adopted by the dyspeptic schoolteacher Kushami watches his household and its string of cranky, pedantic visitors, mocking human vanity from under the veranda. The prankster Meitei's tall tales, the businessman Kaneda's famous nose and Kangetsu's violin misadventures pile up into a sprawling satire of Meiji Japan.

title: Kusamakura
author: Natsume Sōseki
synopsis: A painter climbs a spring mountain path hoping to live in a detached, 'non-human' aesthetic state and takes lodgings at a remote hot-spring inn. There the enigmatic, half-mad Onami drifts through his days, he reads her an English novel at random, and he cannot paint her until he sees her face at a train station seeing off her cousin to war.

title: And Then
author: Natsume Sōseki
synopsis: Daisuke, a thirty-year-old gentleman of leisure, lives off his father's money and scorns the idea of working or marrying on command. When his old friend Hiraoka returns to Tokyo broke and unhappy, Daisuke is forced to face his long-buried love for Hiraoka's wife Michiyo, and to choose between family wealth and the one woman he wants.

title: The Gate
author: Natsume Sōseki
synopsis: Sōsuke and his wife Oyone live a hushed, borrowed life in a rented house under a cliff in Tokyo, bound by a betrayal in their past that cost them family, friends and children. When his younger brother moves in and a landlord's chatter points back to the friend they wronged, Sōsuke retreats to a Zen temple to find a way through the gate and finds only a locked door.

title: Ten Nights of Dreams
author: Natsume Sōseki
synopsis: Ten short dreams, each opening with 'I had this dream.' A dying woman promises to return after a hundred years, a crowd watches the sculptor Unkei carve a Nio guardian out of wood, and a blind child on the narrator's back knows exactly where the murder happened.

title: Light and Darkness
author: Natsume Sōseki
synopsis: Tsuda, a salaried Tokyo clerk, is hospitalised for surgery while his wife Onobu, his sister Ohide and his mother-figure patrons circle around money, vanity and an old lover he has never told his wife about. Every conversation is a duel of appearances, and the novel stops unfinished mid-confrontation.

title: Rashomon
author: Ryūnosuke Akutagawa
synopsis: A dismissed servant sheltering from the rain under Kyoto's ruined Rashomon gate debates starving versus turning thief. Climbing to the loft, he finds an old woman plucking hair from corpses to make wigs, and her blunt self-justification tips him into robbing her.

title: Hell Screen
author: Ryūnosuke Akutagawa
synopsis: The great painter Yoshihide, who can only paint what he has seen, is ordered by his lord to depict hell on a screen. He demands to watch a carriage with a woman inside burn, and the lord obliges with a horrifying twist: the victim is Yoshihide's own beloved daughter.

title: Kappa
author: Ryūnosuke Akutagawa
synopsis: A mental patient recounts falling into the land of the kappa, a satirical underground society of water imps with poets, capitalists, and strange birth and death customs. His friendship with the poet Tok and the suicide that follows expose the despair beneath the absurdity.

title: In a Grove
author: Ryūnosuke Akutagawa
synopsis: A samurai is found dead in a bamboo grove, and each witness and participant tells a different story before a police magistrate. The bandit Tajomaru, the samurai's wife, and the dead man's spirit through a medium each claim the killing, leaving the truth unresolvable.

title: The Spider's Thread
author: Ryūnosuke Akutagawa
synopsis: Buddha, strolling beside the lotus pond of Paradise, spots the thief Kandata suffering in the Blood Pond of Hell and lowers a single silver spider thread to him for the one kindness of his life. Kandata climbs, but when he kicks away the other sinners following him, the thread snaps.

title: Cogwheels
author: Ryūnosuke Akutagawa
synopsis: A haunted writer travelling to Tokyo for a wedding is dogged by omens: a ghost-raincoat story, a brother-in-law's death on the rails, and translucent spinning cogwheels in his vision heralding migraines. Drifting between hotels, bookshops, and a priest's loft, he sinks toward madness and suicidal dread.

title: No Longer Human
author: Osamu Dazai
synopsis: Oba Yozo confesses, in three notebooks, a life spent hiding terror of other people behind a clown's grin. From school-boy comic to drinking, doomed love affairs, morphine and an asylum, he slides toward the verdict that he is no longer human. A frame narrator finds the notebooks in a Kyobashi bar.

title: Run, Melos!
author: Osamu Dazai
synopsis: Melos, a simple shepherd, storms the palace of the tyrant king of Syracuse and is sentenced to death, but begs three days to attend his sister's wedding, leaving his friend Selinuntius as hostage. He sprints back through flood, bandits and exhaustion to keep his word before sunset.

title: The Setting Sun
author: Osamu Dazai
synopsis: After defeat in 1945, the aristocratic Kazuko and her ailing mother retreat to a mountain villa in Izu, where snakes and bad omens gather. Her opium-addicted brother Naoji returns from the front, and Kazuko pursues a married novelist in a desperate bid for love as her class dies out.

title: Night on the Galactic Railroad
author: Kenji Miyazawa
synopsis: Giovanni, a poor boy who works in a print shop to support his sick mother, falls asleep on a hill during the star festival and wakes on a train running along the Milky Way. His friend Campanella rides beside him, and together they meet bird-catchers, drowned passengers and a singing cross of light.

title: The Dancing Girl
author: Mori Ōgai
synopsis: Aboard a steamer in Saigon harbor, Ōta Toyotarō recalls his years as a young state official in Berlin, where he fell for Elis, a sixteen-year-old dancer weeping outside a church. Dismissed from his post and living in a garret with her, he is pulled back toward career and homeland by his friend Aizawa, and betrays her.

title: The Wild Geese
author: Mori Ōgai
synopsis: A medical student recalls his lodging house near Tokyo's Mujinzaka slope, where Otama, the kept mistress of a smug moneylender, watches the student Okada pass her window each day. When she finally resolves to speak to him, a stone thrown at a flight of wild geese changes everything.

title: Takekurabe
author: Higuchi Ichiyō
synopsis: In the lanes beside the Yoshiwara pleasure quarter, children of rival gangs squabble through festival season while Midori, a courtesan's younger sister, and Shinnyo, a priest's son destined for the temple, grow shy and awkward with each other. Childhood ends as Midori is readied for her own life in the quarter.

title: Ukigumo
author: Futabatei Shimei
synopsis: Bunzō, an honest clerk fired from his government post, lives with his aunt and her Westernized daughter Osei in Tokyo. His rival Noboru Honda, a glib careerist, wins Osei's attention while Bunzō dithers, in a pioneering psychological novel written in colloquial Japanese.

title: Lemon
author: Motojirō Kajii
synopsis: A depressed, penniless young man wanders Kyoto, oppressed by an unnamed dark weight, until he buys a single lemon whose cool scent and color lift his spirits. In the Maruzen bookshop he stacks heavy art books into a tower, sets the lemon on top like a bomb, and walks out.

title: The Moon Over the Mountain
author: Atsushi Nakajima
synopsis: Li Zheng, a proud Tang official who quit his post to become a poet, vanishes and turns into a tiger. His old friend Yuan Can, passing through on an official journey, hears his voice from the grass as he recites his poems and confesses that pride and cowardice made him a beast.

title: The Holy Man of Mount Koya
author: Izumi Kyōka
synopsis: A traveling Buddhist priest tells of crossing the Hida mountains, where a forest path swarms with snakes and leeches. He is sheltered by a bewitching woman in a lonely cottage with a simple-minded husband, and discovers that the animals around her are men she has transformed.

title: The Two-Sen Copper Coin
author: Edogawa Rampo
synopsis: A gentleman thief hides a stolen 50,000 yen, and two poor roommates fall to decoding a cryptic note of dots and dashes made from a copper coin's secret message. When one of them thinks he has cracked it and fetches the loot, the other reveals the whole thing was his elaborate prank.

title: The Human Chair
author: Edogawa Rampo
synopsis: A famous woman novelist opens a bundle of manuscript pages from a stranger and reads a chilling confession: a homeless furniture maker once hid inside a leather armchair and lived in it, feeling the bodies of those who sat on it. A second letter arrives to say that he wrote the story for her.

title: The Stalker in the Attic
author: Edogawa Rampo
synopsis: Bored and fascinated only by crime, lodger Saburo discovers he can crawl through the ceiling space above his boarding house and spy on his neighbors through the boards. His game turns deadly when he drips morphine through a knot-hole onto a hated fellow lodger, and the detective Akechi Kogoro sees through him.

title: Beast in the Shadows
author: Edogawa Rampo
synopsis: A detective novelist meets the beautiful wife of a businessman, who is being blackmailed by the reclusive horror writer Oe Shundei, her former lover. When the husband is found drowned and the letters keep coming, the narrator is drawn into a hunt where every clue seems lifted from Shundei's own stories.

title: The Strange Tale of Panorama Island
author: Edogawa Rampo
synopsis: Hitomi Hirosuke, a penniless writer who dreams of building his own utopia, discovers he is the double of a dead millionaire and takes his place after digging up the grave. With the fortune he builds a vast artificial island of panoramas, fireworks and underwater wonders, until a former colleague sees through him.

title: The Black Lizard
author: Edogawa Rampo
synopsis: The female master thief Black Lizard announces she will steal the Star of Egypt, a priceless diamond owned by the jeweler Iwase, and kidnaps his daughter Sanae to get it. Only the great detective Akechi Kogoro can match her in a duel of disguises, traps and nerve.

title: The Tattoo
author: Jun'ichirō Tanizaki
synopsis: In old Edo, the tattooist Seikichi has spent years searching for a woman whose skin is worthy of his soul's masterpiece. When a teenage geisha apprentice arrives, he drugs her and inks a giant black widow spider across her back, and she wakes transformed, making him her first victim.

title: Naomi
author: Jun'ichirō Tanizaki
synopsis: Jōji, a sober Tokyo engineer, takes a fifteen-year-old café waitress named Naomi into his home to mould her into the perfect Westernized wife. She grows into a capricious, scornful beauty with a string of dancing-hall lovers, and he ends up her willing slave, grovelling on all fours for her favours.

title: A Portrait of Shunkin
author: Jun'ichirō Tanizaki
synopsis: A narrator pieces together the story of Shunkin, a blind, imperious Osaka shamisen master, from a slim memorial biography and local memory. Her devoted servant Sasuke becomes her pupil and lover, and after a night attacker scars her face he pierces his own eyes with a needle so he will never see her ruined.

title: Some Prefer Nettles
author: Jun'ichirō Tanizaki
synopsis: Kaname and his wife Misako drift toward a divorce neither can bring herself to name, while his old father-in-law indulges in a Kyoto mistress and the puppet theatre of Osaka. Torn between modern Tokyo tastes and the old Kansai ways, Kaname finds himself drawn to the doll-like Ohisa and the slow, graceful traditions she embodies.

title: Diary of a Mad Old Man
author: Jun'ichirō Tanizaki
synopsis: Seventy-seven-year-old Utsugi, ailing and half-paralysed, records in his diary his obsessive lust for his son's glamorous wife Satsuko, who toys with him and extracts silk scarves and jewels in return for small intimacies. He plans to have her sole carved on his gravestone like a Buddha's footprint stone, so that he can feel her tread on him after death.

title: Dogra Magra
author: Yumeno Kyūsaku
synopsis: A man wakes in a cell of a Kyushu university asylum with no memory of who he is, while two rival professors feed him a cursed manuscript, a ghastly murder case and a theory of ancestral dreams. Each document overturns the last in a looping, maddening labyrinth of mind and heredity.

title: The Crab Cannery Ship
author: Kobayashi Takiji
synopsis: Fishermen and boys hired in Hakodate are shipped to the Okhotsk Sea aboard the rotting factory ship Hakkō Maru, where the overseer Asakawa drives them to sickness and death for the company's profit. Beaten down and finally pushed to strike, the men learn what organization means.

title: The Wind Has Risen
author: Hori Tatsuo
synopsis: A writer follows his fiancée Setsuko, who is dying of tuberculosis, to a mountain sanatorium, where they spend a hushed last season together watching her paintings and the seasons fade. After her death he spends a snowbound winter alone in a mountain cabin, reading and writing to come to terms with the loss.

title: The Book of the Dead
author: Orikuchi Shinobu
synopsis: In eighth-century Nara, a noble's daughter copying the Pure Land sutra a thousand times is drawn to a mountain temple at Taima by the vision of a figure in the sunset. Meanwhile a long-entombed prince, a royal ghost, wakes in his dark tomb, calling for the woman he loved.

title: On Decadence
author: Sakaguchi Ango
synopsis: Writing in the ruins of defeated Japan, Ango argues that the kamikaze pilots turning into black marketeers and the war widows taking new lovers are simply humans returning to themselves. Bushido and the emperor system were devices against human weakness, and people must fall all the way down to find their own salvation.

title: The Golden Demon
author: Ozaki Kōyō
synopsis: Hazama Kan'ichi, a poor student raised in the Shigisawa household, is betrothed to their daughter Miya until the wealthy Tomiyama dazzles her with diamonds and a rich marriage. Crushed and furious, Kan'ichi throws away his studies and becomes a ruthless moneylender, while Miya's regret pours out in long, unanswered letters.

title: The Broken Commandment
author: Shimazaki Tōson
synopsis: Segawa Ushimatsu, a respected schoolteacher in Nagano, hides that he was born into the outcast burakumin class, bound by his father's one commandment: never reveal it. Drawn to the writings and courage of the openly outcast thinker Inoko Rentarō, he moves into a temple lodging and wrestles with the confession that will cost him everything.

title: Musashino
author: Kunikida Doppo
synopsis: A narrator living in a thatched hut near Shibuya walks the oak woods and fields of the Musashino plain through autumn and winter, quoting his diary for the sound of wind in the leaves, the low sun and the quiet. He finds the poetry of a place in its crossroads, village edges and small streams, and in a Russian birch wood he first learned to hear.

title: The Quilt
author: Tayama Katai
synopsis: Takenaka Tokio, a thirty-something writer weary of his marriage, takes in the bright young Yoshiko as his literary disciple and falls painfully in love with her. When her sweetheart Tanaka follows her to Tokyo, Tokio's jealousy, drinking and hypocrisy spiral until he sends her home.

title: A Country Teacher
author: Tayama Katai
synopsis: Seizō, a middle-school graduate from Gyōda who dreams of poetry and a literary career, takes a post at a village school in Saitama and lodges at a temple in Hanyū. Over the years friendships fade, love goes nowhere, debts and illness close in, and the Russo-Japanese War rumbles on while he wastes away teaching in the country.

title: Nogiku no Haka
author: Itō Sachio
