synopsis: Looking back more than ten years, Masao recalls growing up in a farmhouse at Yagiri with his cousin Tamiko, two years his elder, whose easy closeness is spoiled when the household gossips. Sent away to school, he learns too late that Tamiko was married against her will and died holding his photograph and letter, and he lays wild chrysanthemums on her grave.

title: Vita Sexualis
author: Mori Ōgai
synopsis: Professor Kanai, a philosophy lecturer who has never written a book, decides to set down the history of his own sexual life, so that he might one day show it to his grown-up son. He recalls his boyhood from the age of six, from lending-library romances and a stolen peek at a bawdy picture book to dormitory crushes and a half-awakened feeling for the maid Ochō, down to his first visit to a teahouse as a young doctor.

title: Sanshō the Bailiff
author: Mori Ōgai
synopsis: A mother and her two children, fourteen-year-old Anju and twelve-year-old Zushiō, trudge toward their father in the far west, but boatmen lure them aboard and sell them apart: the mother to Sado, the children to the rich bailiff Sanshō at Yura. Worked hard in his household, the siblings plot an escape, and in the end Zushiō's cry restores sight to his blind mother on Sado.

title: The Boat on the Takase River
author: Mori Ōgai
synopsis: On the Takase boat that carries convicts down the river from Kyoto toward exile, the constable Shōbei escorts Kisuke, a condemned man who seems oddly cheerful about leaving. Kisuke tells his story of killing his brother, and Shōbei is left doubting whether it was murder at all as the boat slips on through the dark.

title: The Abe Family
author: Mori Ōgai
synopsis: When Lord Hosokawa Tadatoshi of Kumamoto dies in 1641, his retainers seek permission to follow him in death, a custom with its own unwritten rules. Abe Yaichiemon is refused leave to die, then mocked as a man who clings to life, and he kills himself anyway; his family barricades itself in their house and is attacked by the clan's troops.

title: Li Ling
author: Atsushi Nakajima
synopsis: After his small army is crushed by the Xiongnu, the Han general Li Ling is taken alive, and the furious Emperor Wu massacres his family. Cut off in the steppe, Li Ling weighs exile against his old comrade Su Wu's loyalty, while the court historian Sima Qian, castrated for defending him, pours himself into his great history.

title: Meijinden
author: Atsushi Nakajima
synopsis: Kichang of Handan sets out to become the greatest archer under heaven, training first to never blink and to see a louse as large as a horse under the master Fei Wei. Sent on to the ancient hermit Ganying, who shoots a kite from the sky with an unstrung bow, he returns an expressionless old man who forgets what a bow even is.

title: Under the Cherry Trees
author: Motojirō Kajii
synopsis: A narrator tells a silent companion that corpses must be buried under every cherry tree in full bloom, since beauty so perfect is unbearable otherwise. Roots, he imagines, drink up the crystalline fluid of the decay, and the grisly vision finally frees him to enjoy the blossoms.

title: The Nose
author: Ryūnosuke Akutagawa
synopsis: The priest Zenchi Naigu has a nose five or six inches long that dangles below his chin, and he has fretted over it all his life. A disciple's method of boiling and treading it shortens it at last, but the people around him laugh more than ever, and he longs for his old nose back.

title: Yam Gruel
author: Ryūnosuke Akutagawa
synopsis: A mocked, red-nosed low official in the household of the Regent Mototsune dreams only of eating his fill of yam gruel. The warrior Toshihito carries him off to Tsuruga, sends a fox ahead with a message, and sets a feast before him, but the poor man's appetite fails once the dream comes true.

title: Matasaburo the Wind Imp
author: Kenji Miyazawa
synopsis: A red-haired boy named Saburo appears one stormy September morning at a one-room mountain schoolhouse, and the village children come to suspect he is the wind spirit Matasaburo. When the gales return, he vanishes as suddenly as he came, leaving only his teacher's word that his father's molybdenum mine is closing.

title: The Restaurant of Many Orders
author: Kenji Miyazawa
synopsis: Two pompous city hunters in British uniforms, lost in the mountains after their dogs drop dead, stumble upon the Wildcat House restaurant. Each door bears a more peculiar request, until they realize that they are the meal.

title: Gauche the Cellist
author: Kenji Miyazawa
synopsis: Gauche, the worst player in a cinema orchestra, is bullied by his conductor and practises all night in his ruined watermill. A cat, a cuckoo, a baby raccoon and a mother mouse visit in turn, and by serving them he finds his playing transformed before the big concert.

title: Villon's Wife
author: Osamu Dazai
synopsis: The wife of Otani, a drunken, dissolute poet, goes to work at a small Nakano restaurant after her husband steals money from its owners. Told in her own voice, she finds a lightness in the squalor and tells him it doesn't matter if they are monsters, so long as they stay alive.

title: Schoolgirl
author: Osamu Dazai
synopsis: A teenage girl's single day, from waking up to going to bed, is told in a restless stream of moods: the commuter train, school, housework, and a quiet evening reading to her mother. She is sharp, self-mocking and unsure which of her selves is real.

title: Tsugaru
author: Osamu Dazai
synopsis: Commissioned to write a regional guide, Dazai spends three weeks in spring circling the Tsugaru peninsula at the northern tip of Honshu. He drinks crab and apple wine with old friends in Kanita, trudges to windswept Tappi, and finally seeks out Take, the nursemaid who raised him.

title: An Encouragement of Learning
author: Fukuzawa Yukichi
synopsis: Opening with 'Heaven did not create one man above another,' Fukuzawa argues in a series of plain-spoken essays that only practical learning separates the wise from the foolish. He urges commoners and samurai alike to seek independence of body and mind, since a nation's independence rests on its people's.

title: The Autobiography of Fukuzawa Yukichi
author: Fukuzawa Yukichi
synopsis: Fukuzawa dictates the story of his life, from a poor samurai childhood in Nakatsu through Dutch studies in Osaka, voyages to America and Europe, and the founding of Keio. He tells it with a blunt, funny disregard for old-fashioned manners as he helps drag Japan into the modern world.

title: An Inquiry into the Good
author: Nishida Kitarō
synopsis: Nishida, teaching at a Kanazawa high school, builds a philosophy on 'pure experience,' the unbroken moment before subject and object divide. From that base he works through the nature of reality, the good as the unity of the self, and religion as the deepest union with God.

title: The Silver Spoon
author: Naka Kansuke
synopsis: A grown man opens a small box and finds the little silver spoon he pried from his mother's cabinet as a sickly child, and the memories pour out. Raised by a doting aunt who tells him tales and has him recite poems at bedtime, he drifts through shrines, festivals, schoolyard bullying and first friendships.

title: The Sumida River
author: Nagai Kafū
synopsis: Rogetsu, a failed haikai master, watches his nephew Chokichi pine for Oito, a childhood sweetheart now training as a geisha, while the boy's mother pushes him toward a respectable business life. Chokichi drifts through the back streets of Asakusa and the Sumida riverside until a flood and a fever bring the story to a hospital door.

title: The Doctrine of the Mean
author: Zisi
synopsis: A Confucian classic on cultivating equilibrium and sincerity as the constant, unswerving path to moral harmony.
